5.s: preti pañcārbhavaṃ trīṇi dādhikrāṇi parāṇyataḥ | ṛgdyāvāpṛthivyau stauti dādhikrāṇāṃ mukhe tu yā ||
5.d: प्रेति पञ्चार्भवं त्रीणि दाधिक्राणि पराण्यतः | ऋग्द्यावापृथिव्यौ स्तौति दाधिक्राणां मुखे तु या ||
5.e: (With) Forth' (pra: iv. 33. 1) begins a group of five hymns addressed to the Rbhus (iv. 33-37). Following that are three (hymns) addressed to Dadhikra (iv. 38-40); but the stanza which is at the head of the hymns addressed to Dadhikra (iv. 38. 1) praises Heaven and Earth.

5.s: parokṣairamuto vāgbhira nāmabhiśca stutāstrayaḥ | agnirvāyuśca sūryaśca haṃsaḥ śuciṣadityṛci ||
5.d: परोक्षैरमुतो वाग्भिर नामभिश्च स्तुतास्त्रयः | अग्निर्वायुश्च सूर्यश्च हंसः शुचिषदित्यृचि ||
5.e: Then with indirect (paroksa) expressions (vac) and names the three, Agni, Vayu, Surya, are praised in the stanza, 'The Swan dwelling in light' (hamsah sucisat: iv. 50. 5).

5.s: niyuktā sūryadevatyā haṃsa ityaitareyake | dvai tvaindrāvaruṇe sūkte tatastrīṇyāśvināni kaḥ ||
5.d: नियुक्ता सूर्यदेवत्या हंस इत्यैतरेयके | द्वै त्वैन्द्रावरुणे सूक्ते ततस्त्रीण्याश्विनानि कः ||
5.e: In the Aitareya (Brahmana) 'The Swan' (hamsah: iv. 40. 5) is prescribed as having Surya for its deity. Now (there follow) two hymns addressed to Indra -Varuna (iv. 41, 42), then three (iv. 43-45) addressed to the Asvins (beginning) 'Who?' (kah: iv. 43. 1).

5.s: agraṃ vāyo vihītyeṣu vāyavyāḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ | nava caivendravāyavyā indrastisraḥ śatena ṣaṭ ||
5.d: अग्रं वायो विहीत्येषु वायव्याः सप्त कीर्तिताः | नव चैवेन्द्रवायव्या इन्द्रस्तिस्रः शतेन षट् ||
5.e: In the (hymns) 'The best' (agram: iv. 46. 1), 'O Vayu' (vayo: iv. 47. 1), 'Enjoy' (vihi: iv. 48. 1-5) seven stanzas are declared to be addressed to Vayu; and nine are addressed to Indra - Vayu, (viz.) 'Indra' (indrah: iv. 47. 2-4) being three, (and) 'With a hundred' (satena: iv. 46. 2-7) being six. iv.

5.s: idaṃ kathitadevatyaṃ yastastambhottamo dvṛcaḥ | stutirindrābṛhaspatyor aṣṭāvetā ṛcaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
5.d: इदं कथितदेवत्यं यस्तस्तम्भोत्तमो द्वृचः | स्तुतिरिन्द्राबृहस्पत्योर् अष्टावेता ऋचः स्मृताः ||
5.e: 'This' (idam: iv. 49), addressed to the deities mentioned in it, (and) the last couplet (10, 11) of 'He who has propped (yas tastambha: iv. 50)-these eight stanzas b are traditionally held to be (in) praise of Indra-Brhaspati.

5.s: sūktaṃ tu tadbārhaspatyam idamityauṣase pare | purodhātuḥ karmaśaṃsā sa indrājocyate tṛce ||
5.d: सूक्तं तु तद्बार्हस्पत्यम् इदमित्यौषसे परे | पुरोधातुः कर्मशंसा स इन्द्राजोच्यते तृचे ||
5.e: That a hymn, however, is addressed to Brhaspati ; the two next (beginning) 'That' (idam: iv. 51, 52) are addressed to Usas. In the triplet 'Surely that king' (sa id raja: iv. 50. 7-9) laudation of the function of the appointer of priests (purodhatuh) is expressed.

5.s: tatsāvitre dve tu ko vaiśvadevaṃ mahī dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ paraṃ tu yat | kṣetrasyeti tisrastu kṣaitrapatyāḥ śunaṃ vāhāḥ śunadevī tvṛguttarā ||
5.d: तत्सावित्रे द्वे तु को वैश्वदेवं मही द्यावापृथिवीयं परं तु यत् | क्षेत्रस्येति तिस्रस्तु क्षैत्रपत्याः शुनं वाहाः शुनदेवी त्वृगुत्तरा ||
5.e: There are two hymns addressed to Savitr (beginning) 'That' (tat: iv. 53, 54); 'Who?' (kah: iv. 55) is addressed to the Allgods, while that which follows (viz.) 'The mighty' (mahi: iv. 56) is addressed to Heaven and Earth. But (in the hymn) 'Of the field' (ksetrasya: iv. 57) the (first) three (stanzas) are addressed to the Lord of the Field, while the next stanza, 'Prosperously the steers' (sunam vahah: iv. 57. 4), has Suna as its god. param tu yat A, param yat

5.s: vāyuḥ śunaḥ sūrya evātra sīraḥ śunāsīrau vāyusūryau vadanti | śunāsīraṃ yāska indraṃ tu mene sūryendrau tau manyate śākapūṇiḥ ||
5.d: वायुः शुनः सूर्य एवात्र सीरः शुनासीरौ वायुसूर्यौ वदन्ति | शुनासीरं यास्क इन्द्रं तु मेने सूर्येन्द्रौ तौ मन्यते शाकपूणिः ||
5.e: Suna here is Vayu, Sira is Surya: (for) they say that Suna and Sira are Vayu and Surya. Yaska, however, considered Sunasira to be Indra, (and) Sakapuni thinks those two (Suna and Sira) to be Surya and Indra.

5.s: śunāsīrau pañcamyāṃ tu stutau tau dve tu sītāyai ṣaṣṭhī saptamī ca | śunaṃ naḥ phālāḥ kṛṣiṃ stauti pādaḥ śunaṃ kīnāśāḥ kṛṣijīvānmanuṣyān ||
5.d: शुनासीरौ पञ्चम्यां तु स्तुतौ तौ द्वे तु सीतायै षष्ठी सप्तमी च | शुनं नः फालाः कृषिं स्तौति पादः शुनं कीनाशाः कृषिजीवान्मनुष्यान् ||
5.e: Now these two, Suna and Sira, are praised in the fifth (stanza iv. 57. 5), while there are two (6, 7), the sixth and the seventh (stanzas), to Sita. The verse (pada) Prosperously our shares' (sunam nah phalah iv. 57. 8) praises agriculture; 'Prosperously the ploughers' (sunam kinasah: iv. 57. 8), men who live by agriculture.

5.s: stutaḥ pāde'tra parjanyastṛtīye antyaṃ tvṛṣirdhanakāmo jagāda | kṛṣiṃ vā stauti sarvaṃ hi sūktaṃ samudrādityagnermadhyamasya ||
5.d: स्तुतः पादेऽत्र पर्जन्यस्तृतीये अन्त्यं त्वृषिर्धनकामो जगाद | कृषिं वा स्तौति सर्वं हि सूक्तं समुद्रादित्यग्नेर्मध्यमस्य ||
5.e: Parjanya is here praised in the third verse (iv. 57. 8), while the seer pronounced the last (verse) with a desire of wealth (iv. 57. 8). Or (it may be said) the whole hymn praises agriculture. From the ocean' (samudrat: iv. 58) belongs to the Middle Agni.

5.s: ādityaṃ vā brāhmaṇoktaṃ pradiṣṭam āgneyaṃ vāpyājyasūktaṃ hi dṛṣṭam | apāṃ stutiṃ vā yadi ghṛtastutiṃ gavyameke sauryametadvadanti ||
5.d: आदित्यं वा ब्राह्मणोक्तं प्रदिष्टम् आग्नेयं वाप्याज्यसूक्तं हि दृष्टम् | अपां स्तुतिं वा यदि घृतस्तुतिं गव्यमेके सौर्यमेतद्वदन्ति ||
5.e: As mentioned in Brahmana it is indicated as addressed either to the Sun (aditya) or to Agni; for it appears as an Ajya hymn; or some speak of it as (in) praise of Waters or (in) praise of Ghee, (or) as addressed to Cows, (or) to Surya.

5.s: svarbhānudṛṣṭaṃ sūryasya apahatya tamo'trayaḥ | saptaviṃśatibhiḥ sūktair abodhītyagnimastuvan ||
5.d: स्वर्भानुदृष्टं सूर्यस्य अपहत्य तमोऽत्रयः | सप्तविंशतिभिः सूक्तैर् अबोधीत्यग्निमस्तुवन् ||
5.e: The Atris having dispelled the eclipse of the sun decreed (drstam) by Svarbhanu, praised Agni with the twenty-seven hymns 'He has awoke' (abodhi: v. 1-28).

5.s: traivṛṣṇastrasadasyuśca aśvamedha ṛṇaṃcayaḥ | stūyamānāḥ parīkṣyāḥ syur atriṣvete kvacitkvacit ||
5.d: त्रैवृष्णस्त्रसदस्युश्च अश्वमेध ऋणंचयः | स्तूयमानाः परीक्ष्याः स्युर् अत्रिष्वेते क्वचित्क्वचित् ||
5.e: Traivrsna (Tryaruna), Trasadasyu, Asvamedha, Rnamcaya may be observed as objects of praise in various passages in the (hymns of the) Atris 4.

5.s: aikṣvākustryaruṇo rātrā traivṛṣṇo rathamāsthitaḥ | saṃjagrāhāśvaraśmīṃśca vṛśo jānaḥ purohitaḥ ||
5.d: ऐक्ष्वाकुस्त्र्यरुणो रात्रा त्रैवृष्णो रथमास्थितः | संजग्राहाश्वरश्मींश्च वृशो जानः पुरोहितः ||
5.e: Kinga Tryaruna, son of Trivrsna, of the race of Ikssvaku, was riding in his chariot, and his domestic priest, Vrsa, the son of Jana, took the horses' reins.

5.s: sa brāhmaṇakumārasya ratho gacchañchiro'cchinat | enasvītyabravīccaiva sa rājainaṃ purohitam ||
5.d: स ब्राह्मणकुमारस्य रथो गच्छञ्छिरोऽच्छिनत् | एनस्वीत्यब्रवीच्चैव स राजैनं पुरोहितम् ||
5.e: The chariot, as it went along, cut off the head of Brahman boy, and the king said to his domestic priest, 'You are guilty.'

5.s: so'tharvāṅgirasānmantrān dṛṣṭvā saṃjīvya taṃ śiśum | krodhātsaṃtyajya rājānam anyadeśaṃ samāśritaḥ ||
5.d: सोऽथर्वाङ्गिरसान्मन्त्रान् दृष्ट्वा संजीव्य तं शिशुम् | क्रोधात्संत्यज्य राजानम् अन्यदेशं समाश्रितः ||
5.e: He (Vrsa) having had revealed to him Atharvan spells and having (with them) brought the boy back to life, left the king anger and betook himself to another country. in sisum A, sutam bfn, stutam k.

5.s: haro'vyagnernanāśāsya tasyāpakramaṇādṛṣeḥ | agnau prāstāni havyāni na hyapacyanta kānicit ||
5.d: हरोऽव्यग्नेर्ननाशास्य तस्यापक्रमणादृषेः | अग्नौ प्रास्तानि हव्यानि न ह्यपच्यन्त कानिचित् ||
5.e: In consequence of the departure of the seer, the heat of his (the king's) fire also disappeared, for none of the oblations cast on the fire were (any longer) cooked.

5.s: tataḥ pravyathito rājā so'bhigamya prasādya tam | ābhītvā sa vṛśaṃ jānaṃ punareva purodadhe ||
5.d: ततः प्रव्यथितो राजा सोऽभिगम्य प्रसाद्य तम् | आभीत्वा स वृशं जानं पुनरेव पुरोदधे ||
5.e: Hence the king distressed went to Vrsa Jana, propitiated and brought him back, and again made him his domestic priest.

5.s: sa prasanno vṛśo'nvaicchad dharamagnernṛpakṣaye | avindata piśācīṃ tāṃ jāyāṃ tasya ca bhūpateḥ ||
5.d: स प्रसन्नो वृशोऽन्वैच्छद् धरमग्नेर्नृपक्षये | अविन्दत पिशाचीं तां जायां तस्य च भूपतेः ||
5.e: Vrsa being propitiated sought for the heat a of the fire in the king's house, and he found Pisaci as a wife of the king. sa

5.s: niṣaṇaḥ sa tayā sārdham āsandyāṃ kaśipāvapi | tāmupāmantrayāṃ cakre kametaṃ tvamiti tvṛcā ||
5.d: निषणः स तया सार्धम् आसन्द्यां कशिपावपि | तामुपामन्त्रयां चक्रे कमेतं त्वमिति त्वृचा ||
5.e: Having seated himself with her upon the cushion on a stool, he addressed her with the stanza, 'Whom do you here?' (kam etam tvam: v. 2. 2).

5.s: haraḥ kumārarūpeṇa bruvaṃstāmabhyabhāṣata | vijyotiṣeti coktāyāṃ sahasāgnirudajvalat ||
5.d: हरः कुमाररूपेण ब्रुवंस्तामभ्यभाषत | विज्योतिषेति चोक्तायां सहसाग्निरुदज्वलत् ||
5.e: Speaking of the heat (haras) in the form of a boy a he addressed her (thus). And when he had uttered the (stanza) 'Far with light' (vi jyotisa: v. 2. 9) the fire suddenly flamed up,

5.s: sahamānaḥ samāyāntaṃ prakāśaṃ ca prakāśayan | piśācīmadahattāṃ sa yatra copaviveśa sā ||
5.d: सहमानः समायान्तं प्रकाशं च प्रकाशयन् | पिशाचीमदहत्तां स यत्र चोपविवेश सा ||

5.s: eva eva parāmṛṣṭo bhāllavibrāhmaṇe dvṛcaḥ | nidānasaṃjñake granthe chandogānāmiti śrutiḥ ||
5.d: एव एव परामृष्टो भाल्लविब्राह्मणे द्वृचः | निदानसंज्ञके ग्रन्थे छन्दोगानामिति श्रुतिः ||
5.e: This couplet a is mentioned (paramrsta) in the Brahmana of the Bhallavins: B such is the Vedic passage (sruti) (quoted) in the work entitled Nidana of the Samavedins (chandoga).

5.s: bhavedeva parāmarśaḥ sūktasyāsya vyapekṣayā | bhavanti bāhyā mantrā hi vidhidṛṣṭena coditāḥ ||
5.d: भवेदेव परामर्शः सूक्तस्यास्य व्यपेक्षया | भवन्ति बाह्या मन्त्रा हि विधिदृष्टेन चोदिताः ||
5.e: The mention (of them) is probably (bhaved eva) with reference to this hymn (as a whole); for exoteric (bahya) a formulas are to be found enjoined by the requirements (drsta) of a ceremonial rule (vidhi).

5.s: dṛśyante brāhmaṇe mantrā ekadeśe pradarśitāḥ | jāmadagnyastathaivāprya stokīyāścaitareyake ||
5.d: दृश्यन्ते ब्राह्मणे मन्त्रा एकदेशे प्रदर्शिताः | जामदग्न्यस्तथैवाप्र्य स्तोकीयाश्चैतरेयके ||
5.e: Formulas (thus) appear in Brahmana pointed out in a particular passage (ekadesa): so the Apri stanzas of Jamadagni and the stanzas relating to the drops of ghee (stokiya) b in the Aitareya.

5.s: āpriyaḥ susamiddhāya pañcamaṃ sūktamatra tu | evamṛgvaiśvadevī vā antyā caindrāgnyupottame ||
5.d: आप्रियः सुसमिद्धाय पञ्चमं सूक्तमत्र तु | एवमृग्वैश्वदेवी वा अन्त्या चैन्द्राग्न्युपोत्तमे ||
5.e: Now the fifth hymn here is (made up of) the Apri stanzas 'To the well-kindled' (susamiddhaya: v. 5. 1). The stanza 'Thereon' (edam: v. 26. 9) is optionally (va) a addressed to the All-gods, and the last (stanza) in the last hymn but one (v. 27. 6) is addressed to Indra-Agni. 173] [-Rg-veda v.

5.s: aindrāṇi dvādaśa trīti uśanā tvatra saṃstutaḥ | uśaneti tu pādena saṃ ha yadvāmanena ca ||
5.d: ऐन्द्राणि द्वादश त्रीति उशना त्वत्र संस्तुतः | उशनेति तु पादेन सं ह यद्वामनेन च ||
5.e: There are twelve hymns addressed to Indra (beginning) 'Three' (tri: v. 29-40); but here Usana is praised with the verse (pada) Usana' (usana: v. 29. 9") and also with that (which begins) When together to you two' (sam ha yad vam: v. 31. 8). " .

5.s: indrākutseti caitasyāṃ kutsenendra stutaḥ saha | yattvā sūryeti cātrīṇāṃ pañcarye karma kīrtyate ||
5.d: इन्द्राकुत्सेति चैतस्यां कुत्सेनेन्द्र स्तुतः सह | यत्त्वा सूर्येति चात्रीणां पञ्चर्ये कर्म कीर्त्यते ||
5.e: And in the (stanza) O Indra and Kutsa (indrakutsa: 5. 31. 9) Indra is praised with Kutsa; and in the five stanzas When thee, O Surya' (yat tva surya: v. 40. 5-9) the feat of the Atris is celebrated. * After this

5.s: anasvanteti sūkte'sminn āgneye'trirṛṣiḥ svayam | dānatuṣṭaḥ śaśaṃsaitān rājarṣīniti kecana ||
5.d: अनस्वन्तेति सूक्तेऽस्मिन्न् आग्नेयेऽत्रिरृषिः स्वयम् | दानतुष्टः शशंसैतान् राजर्षीनिति केचन ||
5.e: In a the (hymn) addressed to Agni, With a wagon' (anasvanta: v. 27), the seer Atri himself, pleased with his gifts, proclaimed these (kings) b as royal seers, so say some (authorities).

5.s: āśīradhyeṣaṇāccaibhyo agniṃ prati ca dṛśyate | ayutaṃ ca gavāṃ trīṇi śatānyatha ca viṃśatim ||
5.d: आशीरध्येषणाच्चैभ्यो अग्निं प्रति च दृश्यते | अयुतं च गवां त्रीणि शतान्यथ च विंशतिम् ||
5.e: There also appears (here) a prayer to Agniª on their behalf (ebhyah) in consequence of (their) request (adhyesanat). Ten thousand, three hundred and twenty

5.s: sauvarṇaṃ śakaṭaṃ gobhyāṃ tryaruṇo'dānnṛpo'traye | aśvamedhaḥ śataṃ cokṣṇāṃ trasadasyurdhanaṃ bahu ||
5.d: सौवर्णं शकटं गोभ्यां त्र्यरुणोऽदान्नृपोऽत्रये | अश्वमेधः शतं चोक्ष्णां त्रसदस्युर्धनं बहु ||

5.s: rājñaḥ prati ca tatsūktaṃ babhāṣa iti kecana | ātmā hi nātmane dadyād agrahīnnṛpaterṛṣiḥ ||
5.d: राज्ञः प्रति च तत्सूक्तं बभाष इति केचन | आत्मा हि नात्मने दद्याद् अग्रहीन्नृपतेरृषिः ||
5.e: Others say that he (Atri) addressed this hymn to the kings, for one cannot give to oneself, (and) the seer received (the gifts) from (each) king.

5.s: atreḥ sutamṛṣiṃ babhrum ārtvijyāya ṛṇaṃcayaḥ || sahasradakṣiṇe some vavre taṃ so'pyayājayat ||
5.d: अत्रेः सुतमृषिं बभ्रुम् आर्त्विज्याय ऋणंचयः || सहस्रदक्षिणे सोमे वव्रे तं सोऽप्ययाजयत् ||
5.e: Rnamcaya chose the seer Babhru 4, son of Atri, to officiate as priest at Soma sacrifice in which a thousand sacrificial fees were bestowed. So he ( Babhru) sacrificed for him (Rnamcaya).

5.s: dadau ca rauśamo rājā sahasrāṇi śatāni ca | tasmai catvāri catvāri mahāvīraṃ ca kāñcanam ||
5.d: ददौ च रौशमो राजा सहस्राणि शतानि च | तस्मै चत्वारि चत्वारि महावीरं च काञ्चनम् ||

5.d: यास्कस्तु पूषणं मेने स्तुतमिन्द्रं तु शौनकः | वैश्वानरं भागुरिस्तु मारुत्येष समाश्विना ||

5.d: प्रेति वायुं पूषणं च अर्धर्चेऽग्निरिहोच्यते | प्रथमेऽथ द्वितीये च स्तुता एति दिवौकसः ||

5.s: ā vācaṃ madhyamāṃ stauti tato'nyā tu bṛhaspatim | jyāyāṃsamiti cādityaṃ pra vo vāyurihocyate ||
5.d: आ वाचं मध्यमां स्तौति ततोऽन्या तु बृहस्पतिम् | ज्यायांसमिति चादित्यं प्र वो वायुरिहोच्यते ||

5.s: taṃ pratnatheti saumo vā daivyaindrī vā prajāpateḥ | parokṣavaiśvadevaṃ tad āha kauṣītakiḥ svayam ||
5.d: तं प्रत्नथेति सौमो वा दैव्यैन्द्री वा प्रजापतेः | परोक्षवैश्वदेवं तद् आह कौषीतकिः स्वयम् ||
5.e: 'Him as of old' (tam pratnatha: v. 44. 1) a is addressed either to Soma (or) the Gods, or Indra, (or belongs) to Prajapati. Kausitaki himself has spoken of this (hymn) as one in which the All-gods are indirectly addressed (paroksa).

5.s: teṣu tṛtīyamityuktaṃ devānhuva idaṃ param | devānāṃ patnīriti tu devapatnyo dvṛce stutāḥ ||
5.d: तेषु तृतीयमित्युक्तं देवान्हुव इदं परम् | देवानां पत्नीरिति तु देवपत्न्यो द्वृचे स्तुताः ||
5.e: Among these it is spoken of as the third a after it comes the (hymn) 'I invoke the gods' (devan huve: x. 66). In the couplet 'The Spouses of the Gods' (devaanam patnih: v. 47. 7, 8), the spouses of the gods are praised.

5.s: ayaṃ caturṇāmiti cendravāyū tribhi stutau vāyavā yāhi vāyum | rathaṃ tvṛcā rodasī stūyate'tra yasyā stutā maruto rudrapatnyāḥ ||
5.d: अयं चतुर्णामिति चेन्द्रवायू त्रिभि स्तुतौ वायवा याहि वायुम् | रथं त्वृचा रोदसी स्तूयतेऽत्र यस्या स्तुता मरुतो रुद्रपत्न्याः ||
5.e: And with three a of the four (beginning) 'This' (ayam: v. 51. 4-7) Indra-Vayu are praised, while 'O Vayu, come' (vayav a yahi: v. 51. 5)c (praises) Vayu (only)d. With the stanza 'The car' (ratham v. 56. 8) is here praised Rodasi, whose (husbands) the Maruts-she being the spouse of the Rudras e-are praised (in the whole hymn) f.

5.s: ā rudrāsa iti tvasyāṃ rudrāṇāṃ saṃstuto gaṇaḥ | marutāṃ tu gaṇasyaitan nāma rudrā iti smṛtāḥ ||
5.d: आ रुद्रास इति त्वस्यां रुद्राणां संस्तुतो गणः | मरुतां तु गणस्यैतन् नाम रुद्रा इति स्मृताः ||
5.e: But in the (stanza) Hither, O Rudras' (a rudrasah: v. 57. 1) the host of the Rudras is praised. Now this is the name of the host of the Maruts: they are called Rudras.

5.s: asāvagnirayaṃ cobhāv agnī pārthivamadhyamau | agne marudbhirityasyāṃ marudbhiḥ saha saṃstutau ||
5.d: असावग्निरयं चोभाव् अग्नी पार्थिवमध्यमौ | अग्ने मरुद्भिरित्यस्यां मरुद्भिः सह संस्तुतौ ||
5.e: Now that Agni and this, (viz.) both the middle and the terrestrial Agnis, are praised with the Maruts in the (stanza) 'O Agni, with the Maruts' (agne marudbhih: v. 60. 8)a.

5.s: madhyamā vāka striyaḥ sarvāḥ pumān sarvaśca madhyamaḥ | gaṇāśca sarve maruto guṇabhedātpṛthak pṛthak ||
5.d: मध्यमा वाक स्त्रियः सर्वाः पुमान् सर्वश्च मध्यमः | गणाश्च सर्वे मरुतो गुणभेदात्पृथक् पृथक् ||
5.e: Vac (may be) middle, all female goddesses (striyah) (may be middle), and every male (deity may be) middle, as well as all groups (gana), (such as) the Maruts, respectively according to their different qualities. Amr, W.-This sloka is not found in A, but in

5.s: rājarṣirabhavaddārbhyo rathavītiriti śrutaḥ | sa yakṣyamāṇo rājātrim abhigamya prasādya ca ||
5.d: राजर्षिरभवद्दार्भ्यो रथवीतिरिति श्रुतः | स यक्ष्यमाणो राजात्रिम् अभिगम्य प्रसाद्य च ||
5.e: There was a royal seer famous by the name of Rathaviti Darbhya. That king being about to sacrifice went to Atri and propitiated him. Tf all MSS. and n, : Sarvanukramani, Sadgurusisya, n(gh); cp. Max Muller, Rg-veda2 vol. ii, p.

5.s: ātmānaṃ kāryamarthaṃ ca khyāpayanprāñjali sthitaḥ | avṛṇītarṣimātreyam ārtvijyāyārcanānasam ||
5.d: आत्मानं कार्यमर्थं च ख्यापयन्प्राञ्जलि स्थितः | अवृणीतर्षिमात्रेयम् आर्त्विज्यायार्चनानसम् ||
5.e: And making known his identity and the object he had in view, as he stood with folded hands, he chose the seer Arcananas, the son of Atria, to officiate as (his) priest.

5.s: sa saputro'bhyagacchattaṃ rājānaṃ yajñasiddhaye | śyāvaśvaścātriputrasya putraḥ khalvarcanānasaḥ ||

5.e: He, accompanied by his son, went to the king for the performance of the sacrifice. Now the son of Arcananas, Atri's son, was

5.e: And as the sacrifice was in progress, he saw the illustrious daughter of the king. The thought occurred to him that the princess might become his daughter-in-law. yajne ca hdm'rbfkn, yajne'tha Sadgurusisya (one MS. yajne ca ).

5.d: प्रत्याचष्टे स तं राजा सह संमन्त्र्य भार्यया | अनृऋषिर्नैव जामाता कश्चिद्भवितुमर्हति ||
5.e: The king, after conferring with his wife, refused him (saying), 'No one is worthy to be (our) son-in-law who is not a seer.'

5.s: pratyākhyāta ṛṣistena vṛtte yajñe nyavartata | śyāvāśvasya tu kanyāyā mano naiva nyavartata ||
5.d: प्रत्याख्यात ऋषिस्तेन वृत्ते यज्ञे न्यवर्तत | श्यावाश्वस्य तु कन्याया मनो नैव न्यवर्तत ||
5.e: The seer, being rejected by him, returned, when the sacrifice was over; but the heart of Syavasva returned not from the girl.

5.d: तरन्तपुरमीḻहौ तु राजानौ वैददश्व्यृषी | ताभ्यां तौ चक्रतुः पूजाम् ऋषिभ्यां नृपती स्वयम् ||
5.e: Now the two kings Taranta and Purumilha were seers, sons of Vidadasva. These two kings themselves paid homage to the two seers.

5.s: ṛṣiputraṃ mahiṣyāśca darśayāmāsa taṃ nṛpaḥ | tarantānumatā caiva prādādbahuvidhaṃ vasu ||
5.d: ऋषिपुत्रं महिष्याश्च दर्शयामास तं नृपः | तरन्तानुमता चैव प्रादाद्बहुविधं वसु ||
5.e: And the king (Taranta) showed the seer's son to his royal consort; and with Taranta's approval she gave manifold wealth, tam

5.s: ajāvikaṃ gavāśvaṃ ca śyāvāśvāya śaśīyasī | atriṃ yājyārcito gatvā pitāputrau svamāśramam ||
5.d: अजाविकं गवाश्वं च श्यावाश्वाय शशीयसी | अत्रिं याज्यार्चितो गत्वा पितापुत्रौ स्वमाश्रमम् ||

5.d: अभ्यवादयतामत्रिं महर्षिं दीप्ततेजसम् | श्यावाश्वस्य मनस्यासीन् मन्त्रस्यादर्शनादहम् ||
5.e: And they saluted Atri, the great seer, of brilliant splendour. (But) Syavasva thought: 'Because I have not seen (any)

5.s: na labdhavānahaṃ kanyāṃ hanta sarvāṅgaśobhanām | apyahaṃ mantradarśī syāṃ bhaveddharṣo mahānmama ||
5.d: न लब्धवानहं कन्यां हन्त सर्वाङ्गशोभनाम् | अप्यहं मन्त्रदर्शी स्यां भवेद्धर्षो महान्मम ||
5.e: I have, alas! not obtained the maiden beautiful in all her limbs. Could I but become a seer of formulas, my joy would be great.'

5.s: ityaraṇye cintayataḥ prādurāsīnmarudgaṇaḥ | dadarśa saṃsthitānpārśve tulyarūpānivātmanaḥ ||
5.d: इत्यरण्ये चिन्तयतः प्रादुरासीन्मरुद्गणः | ददर्श संस्थितान्पार्श्वे तुल्यरूपानिवात्मनः ||
5.e: To him as he thus reflected in the forest the host of the Maruts appeared. He saw standing at his (atmanah) side, quite (iva) similar in form tulyarupanivatmanah Am'

5.s: samānavayasaścaiva maruto rukmavakṣasaḥ | tāṃstulyavayaso dṛṣṭvā devānpuruṣavigrahān ||
5.d: समानवयसश्चैव मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसः | तांस्तुल्यवयसो दृष्ट्वा देवान्पुरुषविग्रहान् ||

5.s: śyāvāśvo vismito'pṛcchat ke ṣṭheti marutastadā | tatastu maruto devān rudrasūnūnabudhvata ||
5.d: श्यावाश्वो विस्मितोऽपृच्छत् के ष्ठेति मरुतस्तदा | ततस्तु मरुतो देवान् रुद्रसूनूनबुध्वत ||
5.e: Syavashva, astonished, then asked the Maruts, 'Who are ye?' (ke stha: v. 61. 1). Then, however, he became aware that they were the divine Maruts, the sons of Rudra.

The triplet Like the wind' (yatha vatah: v. 78. 7-9) is with a view to a child (garbha) for himself who like a child (in the womb) slept (in the tree); but the other two stanzasb are to be known as for the Asvinsc. 5.e: Hence (there may be) a disagreement of the formulas with the (application). But the words (pada) occurring in them (the formulas), which have a generally understood meaning (samvijnana), may express what is secondary (guna).

5.d: आसस्राणास इत्यस्यां वायुरिन्द्रश्च संस्तुतौ | इन्द्रः प्राधान्यतो वात्र स्तुतो वायुर्निपातभाक् ||
5.e: In the (stanza) 'Bringing hither' (asasranasah: vi. 37. 3) Vayu and Indra are praised together. B Or else Indra is here predominantly praised, while Vayu is incidental (nipatabhaj).

5.s: ayaṃ devastṛcaṃ saumyam aindrameke pracakṣate | ya ānayaditi tvasya tṛco'dhīti bṛbustutiḥ ||
5.d: अयं देवस्तृचं सौम्यम् ऐन्द्रमेके प्रचक्षते | य आनयदिति त्वस्य तृचोऽधीति बृबुस्तुतिः ||
5.e: The triplet 'This god' (ayam devah: vi. 44. 22-24), which is addressed to Soma, some say is addressed to Indraa. But the triplet 'Above' (adhi: 31-33) of the (hymn) 'Who brought' (ya anayat: vi. 45)b is (in) praise of Brbu. 108 ab is found in B and

5.s: pitaraṃ stauti śaṃyuśca tṛcasyāntye pade svakam | svāduṣkilāyamiti tu saumyaḥ pañcarca uttaraḥ ||
5.d: पितरं स्तौति शंयुश्च तृचस्यान्त्ये पदे स्वकम् | स्वादुष्किलायमिति तु सौम्यः पञ्चर्च उत्तरः ||
5.e: And Samyu a praises his father in the last verse (pada) of the triplet. The five stanzas (beginning) 'Sweet, indeed, is this' (svadus kilayam vi. 47. 1-5) which follow (the Indra hymns) are addressed to Soma.

5.s: indraḥ pradhānato vātra stutaḥ somo nipātabhāk | indrasyendrayo'nupānīyāḥ śrūyante hyaitareyake ||
5.d: इन्द्रः प्रधानतो वात्र स्तुतः सोमो निपातभाक् | इन्द्रस्येन्द्रयोऽनुपानीयाः श्रूयन्ते ह्यैतरेयके ||
5.e: Or else Indra is here predominantly praised, while Soma is incidental; for in the Aitareya (Brahmana) a they are stated to be Anupaniya stanzas addressed to Indra. Iroab is nearly identical with

5.s: agavyūti stauti devān pādo bhūmimathottaraḥ | bṛhaspatiṃ tṛtīyastu indramevottamaṃ padam ||
5.d: अगव्यूति स्तौति देवान् पादो भूमिमथोत्तरः | बृहस्पतिं तृतीयस्तु इन्द्रमेवोत्तमं पदम् ||
5.e: (In) Destitute of pasture' (agavyuti: vi. 47. 20) one verse (pada) praises the Gods, the next one (the second) the Earth, the third Brhaspati, the last verse (pada) Indra.

5.s: vanaspate vīḍvaṅgaḥ paraṃ yat tadācāryā bhāvavṛttaṃ vadanti | ṛcastu tisrastu rathābhimarśanā upeti tisro dundubheḥ saṃstavo'tra ||
5.d: वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गः परं यत् तदाचार्या भाववृत्तं वदन्ति | ऋचस्तु तिस्रस्तु रथाभिमर्शना उपेति तिस्रो दुन्दुभेः संस्तवोऽत्र ||
5.e: The (verse) which follows, O Lord of Wood, be firm in body' (vanaspate vidvangah: vi. 47. 26%), the teachers state to be evolutionary (bhavavrtta). But the (whole) three stanzas (26-28) relate to the stroking of the car, while the three here (beginning) 'Forth' (upa: 29-31) are (in) praise of the Drum. param

5.s: samaśvaparṇā iti cāryamaindraṃ daśādito'gnestṛṇapāṇikasya | tṛcaḥ paro mārutaḥ pṛśnisūkte dvṛcaḥ paro vaiśvadevaḥ punaśca ||
5.d: समश्वपर्णा इति चार्यमैन्द्रं दशादितोऽग्नेस्तृणपाणिकस्य | तृचः परो मारुतः पृश्निसूक्ते द्वृचः परो वैश्वदेवः पुनश्च ||
5.e: And the hemistich Together, winged with steeds' (sam asvaparnah: vi. 47. 31) is addressed to Indra. The ten (stanzas) at the beginning of the Trnapani hymn (vi. 48. 1-10) are to Agni ; the following triplet (11-13) in (this) hymn to Prsni is addressed to the Maruts, and, again, the following couplet (14, 15) is addressed to the All-gods. cd The text of 113 ed and 114 follows the reading of

5.s: ādityo vā māruta eva vā syād ā mā pūṣanniti pauṣṇāścatasraḥ | dvṛcaṃ paraṃ mārutaṃ tatra vidyād antyā dyubhvoḥ kīrtanā pṛśnaye vā ||
5.d: आदित्यो वा मारुत एव वा स्याद् आ मा पूषन्निति पौष्णाश्चतस्रः | द्वृचं परं मारुतं तत्र विद्याद् अन्त्या द्युभ्वोः कीर्तना पृश्नये वा ||
5.e: Or it may be addressed to the Adityas or to the Maruts. The four (stanzas) To me, O Pusan' (a ma Pusan: vi. 48. 16-19) one should know to be addressed to Pusan, (and) the following couplet there (20, 21) to be addressed to the Maruts; the last Rg-veda vi. 48-] BRHADDEVATAv. 115- [196 (stanza) is a celebration of Heaven and Earth or is (meant) for PrSni (22). 114'.

5.s: stuṣe sūktāni vai catvāri vaiśvadevānyataḥ param | dvitīyāgniṃ caturthī ca vāyuṃ pañcamyathāśvinau ||
5.d: स्तुषे सूक्तानि वै चत्वारि वैश्वदेवान्यतः परम् | द्वितीयाग्निं चतुर्थी च वायुं पञ्चम्यथाश्विनौ ||
5.e: After this the four hymns ' I praise' (stuse : vi. 49- 52) are addressed to the All-gods : the second stanza (vi. 49. 2) (praises) Agni, and the fourth (49. 4) Vayu, then the fifth (49. 5) the Asvins, but the seventh here praises Vac (49. 7), the eighth 49. 8) PUsan, the ninth (49. 9) Tvastr, 'Of the world' (bhuvanasya : 49. 10) Rudra, then the two next (49. 11, 12) 116.

5.s: stautyṛk tu saptamī vācam atra pūṣaṇamaṣṭamī | tvaṣṭāraṃ navamo rudraṃ bhuvanasyetyathottare ||
5.d: स्तौत्यृक् तु सप्तमी वाचम् अत्र पूषणमष्टमी | त्वष्टारं नवमो रुद्रं भुवनस्येत्यथोत्तरे ||

5.s: mārutyau yo rajāṃsīti viṣṇumeva jagāvṛṣiḥ | abhyandrayeti ca sāvitrī raudasyāgnevyutāśvinī ||
5.d: मारुत्यौ यो रजांसीति विष्णुमेव जगावृषिः | अभ्यन्द्रयेति च सावित्री रौदस्याग्नेव्युताश्विनी ||

5.s: agnīparjanyāvanayo sauryau codu tyadityṛcau | vayaṃ catvāri pauṣṇāni tvaindrāpauṣṇasya cottaram ||
5.d: अग्नीपर्जन्यावनयो सौर्यौ चोदु त्यदित्यृचौ | वयं चत्वारि पौष्णानि त्वैन्द्रापौष्णस्य चोत्तरम् ||
5.e: O Agni and Parjanya' (agniparjanyau: vi. 52. 16) a belongs to those two (deities), and the two stanzas Upward that' (ud u tyat: vi. 51. 1, 2) are addressed to Surya. 'We' (vayam vi. 53-56) are four (hymns) addressed to Pusan, as well as that which comes next (58) to the one addressed to Indra-Pusan (57).

5.s: rathītamaṃ kapardinaṃ raudrameke pracakṣate | aindrāgne pra nu voceti iyaṃ sārasvataṃ stuṣe ||
5.d: रथीतमं कपर्दिनं रौद्रमेके प्रचक्षते | ऐन्द्राग्ने प्र नु वोचेति इयं सारस्वतं स्तुषे ||
5.e: Some declare the stanza 'Him chief of charioteers, with braided hair' (rathitaman kapardinam: vi. 55. 2) to be addressed to Rudra. 'I will now proclaim' (pra nu voca: vi. 59, 60) are two hymns addressed to Indra-Agni. 'She' (iyam: vi. 61) is addressed to Sarasvati; 'I praise' (stuse: vi. 62) 119 ab is found in

5.s: āśvine coṣase caiva mārutaṃ tu vapurnviti | upeti ca dvṛce'śvibhyām ārādhanaṃ ca śaṃsati ||
5.d: आश्विने चोषसे चैव मारुतं तु वपुर्न्विति | उपेति च द्वृचेऽश्विभ्याम् आराधनं च शंसति ||

5.s: maitrāvaruṇamevaikaṃ viśveṣāṃ vaḥ satāmiti | śruṣṭīti caindrāvaraṇaṃ samaindrāvaiṣṇavaṃ param ||
5.d: मैत्रावरुणमेवैकं विश्वेषां वः सतामिति | श्रुष्टीति चैन्द्रावरणं समैन्द्रावैष्णवं परम् ||
5.e: There is one to Mitra -Varuna, (viz.) 'Among all beings your' (visvesam vah satam: vi. 67). 'Obediently' (srusti: vi. 68) is addressed to Indra -Varuna; the following one, 'Together' (sam: vi. 69) is addressed to Indra -Visnu. samaindra ° hd, samkemdra, sam vamaidra f.

5.s: dyāvāpṛthivyau savitā indrāsomau bṛhaspatiḥ | pṛthakpṛthak paraiḥ sūktaiḥ somārudreti tau stutau ||
5.d: द्यावापृथिव्यौ सविता इन्द्रासोमौ बृहस्पतिः | पृथक्पृथक् परैः सूक्तैः सोमारुद्रेति तौ स्तुतौ ||
5.e: Heaven and Earth (70), Savitr (71), Indra-Soma (72), Brhaspati (73) are respectively praised in the following hymns; (in) O Soma and Rudra' (somarudra: vi. 74) those two (gods) are praised.

5.s: cakraṃ ratho maṇirbhāryā bhūmiraśvo gajastathā | etāni sapta ratnāni sarveṣāṃ cakravartinām ||
5.d: चक्रं रथो मणिर्भार्या भूमिरश्वो गजस्तथा | एतानि सप्त रत्नानि सर्वेषां चक्रवर्तिनाम् ||
5.e: Discus, car, jewel, wife, territory, horse, and elephantthese are the seven treasures of all emperors (cakravartin).

5.s: abhyāvartī cāyamānaḥ prastokaścaiva sārñjayaḥ | ājagmaturbharadvājaṃ jitau vāraśikhairyudhi ||
5.d: अभ्यावर्ती चायमानः प्रस्तोकश्चैव सार्ञ्जयः | आजग्मतुर्भरद्वाजं जितौ वारशिखैर्युधि ||
5.e: Abhyavartin Cayamana a and Prastoka, son of Srnjaya, having been conquered in fight by the Varasikhas, came to

5.s: abhigamyocatustau taṃ prasādyākhyāya nāmanī | yudhi vāraśivairbrahmann āvāṃ viddhi vinirjitau ||
5.d: अभिगम्योचतुस्तौ तं प्रसाद्याख्याय नामनी | युधि वारशिवैर्ब्रह्मन्न् आवां विद्धि विनिर्जितौ ||
5.e: Having approached and propitiated him and mentioning their names, the two said to him: 'O Brahman, know that we have been vanquished by the Varasikhas in fight.

5.s: bhavatpurohitāvāvāṃ kṣatrabandhūñjayevahi | kṣatraṃ tadapi vijñeyaṃ brahma yatpāti śāśvatam ||
5.d: भवत्पुरोहितावावां क्षत्रबन्धूञ्जयेवहि | क्षत्रं तदपि विज्ञेयं ब्रह्म यत्पाति शाश्वतम् ||
5.e: With you as our domestic priest we could conquer the warriors (ksatrabandhun).' That is to be recognized as ksatra (warrior caste) which protects the everlasting brahma (priestly caste).

5.s: ṛṣistau tu tathetyuktvā pāyuṃ putramabhāṣata | adharṣaṇīyau śatrūṇāṃ kuruṣvaitau nṛpāviti ||
5.d: ऋषिस्तौ तु तथेत्युक्त्वा पायुं पुत्रमभाषत | अधर्षणीयौ शत्रूणां कुरुष्वैतौ नृपाविति ||
5.e: The seer saying 'yes' to them, addressed his son Payu: 'Make these two kings unassailable to their enemies.' tau tu

5.s: pitaraṃ sa tathetyuktvā yuddhopakaraṇaṃ tayoḥ | jīmūtasyeti sūktena pṛthaktvenānvamantrayat ||
5.d: पितरं स तथेत्युक्त्वा युद्धोपकरणं तयोः | जीमूतस्येति सूक्तेन पृथक्त्वेनान्वमन्त्रयत् ||
5.e: Saying 'yes' to his father, he consecrated their implements of war individually with the hymn 'Of a thunder cloud' (jimutasya: vi. 75).

5.s: prathamā tvasya sūktasya yoddhāraṃ stauti varmiṇam | dhanuṣaśca dvitīyā tu tṛtīyā jyābhimantriṇī ||
5.d: प्रथमा त्वस्य सूक्तस्य योद्धारं स्तौति वर्मिणम् | धनुषश्च द्वितीया तु तृतीया ज्याभिमन्त्रिणी ||
5.e: The first (stanza) of this hymn praises the warrior in his coat of mail (1), the second is (in praise) of the bow (2), the third consecrates the bowstring (3).

5.s: stautyṛgārtnī tu iṣudhiṃ stauti pañcamī | ardhena sārathiḥ ṣaṣṭhyā raśmayo'rdhena saṃstutaḥ ||
5.d: स्तौत्यृगार्त्नी तु इषुधिं स्तौति पञ्चमी | अर्धेन सारथिः षष्ठ्या रश्मयोऽर्धेन संस्तुतः ||
5.e: The fourth stanza praises the ends of the bow (4), the fifth praises the quiver (5). With half of the sixth the charioteer, with the (other) half the reins are praised (6). 200 stotyrgarni caturthi 4, stauti cana caturtho Bn.

5.s: aśvāṃstu saptamī stauti āyudhāgāramaṣṭamī | navamī rathagopāṃstu daśamī raṇadevatāḥ ||
5.d: अश्वांस्तु सप्तमी स्तौति आयुधागारमष्टमी | नवमी रथगोपांस्तु दशमी रणदेवताः ||
5.e: The seventh praises the horses ( 7 ), the eighth the arsenal (8), the ninth the guards of the car (9), the tenth the deities of battle (10).

5.s: iṣuṃ caikādaśī stauti dvādaśī kavacastutiḥ | trayodaśī kaśāṃ stauti hastatrāṇaṃ caturdaśī ||
5.d: इषुं चैकादशी स्तौति द्वादशी कवचस्तुतिः | त्रयोदशी कशां स्तौति हस्तत्राणं चतुर्दशी ||
5.e: The eleventh praises the arrow ( 11 ), the twelfth is a praise of the cuirass ( 12 ), the thirteenth praises the goad (13), the fourteenth the handguard ( 14 ) .

5.s: prathame pañcadaśyāstu pāde digdha iṣu stutaḥ | ayomukhī dvitīye tu ardhe'straṃ vāruṇaṃ pare ||
5.d: प्रथमे पञ्चदश्यास्तु पादे दिग्ध इषु स्तुतः | अयोमुखी द्वितीये तु अर्धेऽस्त्रं वारुणं परे ||
5.e: In the first verse of the fifteenth ( stanza ) the poisoned arrow is praised (159), in the second (152) the iron-tipped (arrow), but in the following half (of the stanza) the missile of Varuna (1500).

5.s: ṣoḻaśyāṃ tvasya sūktasya dhanurmukta iṣu stutaḥ | saptadaśyāṃ tu yuddhādeḥ kavacasya tu badhyataḥ ||
5.d: षोḻअश्यां त्वस्य सूक्तस्य धनुर्मुक्त इषु स्तुतः | सप्तदश्यां तु युद्धादेः कवचस्य तु बध्यतः ||
5.e: In the sixteenth ( stanza) of this hymn the arrow discharged from the bow is praised (16) ; in the seventeenth (there is praise) of the beginning of the fight ( 17 ), while the eighteenth is to be known as (in) praise of the mail of him who ties it on (badhyatah); the last ( 19 ) is (in) praise of him who is about to fight; and in the last verse ( 19 ) the seer utters prayers on his own behalf. 134. solasyam B, solasya A.

5.s: stutiraṣṭādaśī jñeyā yuyutso stutiruttamā | āśāste cottame pāde ṛṣirātmana aśiṣaḥ ||
5.d: स्तुतिरष्टादशी ज्ञेया युयुत्सो स्तुतिरुत्तमा | आशास्ते चोत्तमे पादे ऋषिरात्मन अशिषः ||

5.s: sūktanānena tu stutvā saṃgrāmāṅgānyṛṣistayoḥ | tataḥ prasthāpayāmāsa punarvāraśikhānprati ||
5.d: सूक्तनानेन तु स्तुत्वा संग्रामाङ्गान्यृषिस्तयोः | ततः प्रस्थापयामास पुनर्वारशिखान्प्रति ||

5.s: etattyatte catasṛbhī rājño sāhāyyakāmyayā | bharadvājo'bhituṣṭāva protastena puraṃdaraḥ ||
5.d: एतत्त्यत्ते चतसृभी राज्ञो साहाय्यकाम्यया | भरद्वाजोऽभितुष्टाव प्रोतस्तेन पुरंदरः ||
5.e: With the four stanzas 'This here of thee' (etat tyat te: vi. 27. 4-7) Bharadvaja praised (Indra) from a desire of aiding the king (Cayamana). Pleased thereby the Fort-destroyer, catasrbhi m'bfkrn (aghm), ca tisrbhi n (be).

5.s: abhyāvartinamabhyetya haryupīyānadītaṭe | sahitaścāyamānena jaghānainānchacīpatiḥ ||
5.d: अभ्यावर्तिनमभ्येत्य हर्युपीयानदीतटे | सहितश्चायमानेन जघानैनान्छचीपतिः ||

5.s: tau tu vāraśikhāñjitvā tato'bhyāvartisārñjayau | bharadvājāya gurave dadaturvividhaṃ vasu ||
5.d: तौ तु वारशिखाञ्जित्वा ततोऽभ्यावर्तिसार्ञ्जयौ | भरद्वाजाय गुरवे ददतुर्विविधं वसु ||

5.s: bharadvājaśca gargaśca dṛṣṭāvindreṇa vai pathi | dvayān prastoka ityābhir dānaṃ tadvai śaśaṃsatuḥ ||
5.d: भरद्वाजश्च गर्गश्च दृष्टाविन्द्रेण वै पथि | द्वयान् प्रस्तोक इत्याभिर् दानं तद्वै शशंसतुः ||
5.e: Bharadvaja and Garga, being seen by Indra on the road, proclaimed that gift with the (stanzas) 'Two' (dvayan: vi. 27. 8) (and) Prastoka' (prastokah: vi. 47. 22). II. dvayan Am', dvau ca B.

5.s: ṛṣirapyabhituṣṭāva dānaṃ tatra ca tasya tu | ṛcaikayā dvayām̐ agne dattaṃ saṃkīrtayan svayam ||
5.d: ऋषिरप्यभितुष्टाव दानं तत्र च तस्य तु | ऋचैकया द्वयाम्̐ अग्ने दत्तं संकीर्तयन् स्वयम् ||
5.e: The seer on his part praised the gift of that (Cayamana), himself proclaiming what had been given (by him) with the one stanza, 'Two, O Agni' (dvayan agne: vi. 27. 8). This sloka is not found in A or

5.s: prasaṅgāttviha yāḥ sūkte devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ | tā eva sūktabhājastu mene rathītara stutau ||
5.d: प्रसङ्गात्त्विह याः सूक्ते देवताः परिकीर्तिताः | ता एव सूक्तभाजस्तु मेने रथीतर स्तुतौ ||
5.e: The deities who in this hymn a are occasionally (prasangat) celebrated, Rathitara regarded as hymn-owning (suktabhaj) in praise (stutau).

5.s: prājāpatyo marīcirhi mārīcaḥ kaśyapo muniḥ | tasya devyo'bhavañjāyā dākṣāyaṇyastrayodaśa ||
5.d: प्राजापत्यो मरीचिर्हि मारीचः कश्यपो मुनिः | तस्य देव्योऽभवञ्जाया दाक्षायण्यस्त्रयोदश ||

5.s: aditiditirdanuḥ kālā danāyuḥ siṃhikā muniḥ | krodhā viśvā variṣṭā ca surabhirvinatā tathā ||
5.d: अदितिदितिर्दनुः काला दनायुः सिंहिका मुनिः | क्रोधा विश्वा वरिष्टा च सुरभिर्विनता तथा ||
5.e: Aditia, Diti, Danu, Kala, Danayu, Simhika, Muni, Krodha, Visva and Varistha, Surabhi and Vinata,

5.s: kadrūścaiveti duhitaḥ kaśyapāya dadau sa ca | tāsu devāsurāścaiva gandharvoragarākṣasāḥ ||
5.d: कद्रूश्चैवेति दुहितः कश्यपाय ददौ स च | तासु देवासुराश्चैव गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः ||

5.s: vayāṃsi va piśācāśca jajñire'nyāśca jātayaḥ | tatraikā tvaditirdevī dvādaśajanayatsutān ||
5.d: वयांसि व पिशाचाश्च जज्ञिरेऽन्याश्च जातयः | तत्रैका त्वदितिर्देवी द्वादशजनयत्सुतान् ||
5.e: Birds, Pisacas, and other classes (of beings) were produced. Now among these (daughters) the one goddess Aditi produced twelve sons.

5.s: bhagaścaivāryamāṃśaśca mitro varuṇa eva ca | dhātā caiva vidhātā ca vivasvāṃśca mahādyutiḥ ||
5.d: भगश्चैवार्यमांशश्च मित्रो वरुण एव च | धाता चैव विधाता च विवस्वांश्च महाद्युतिः ||
5.e: (These were) Bhaga, Aryaman, and Amsa, Mitra and Varuna, Dhatr and Vidhatr, and Vivasvat of great brilliance,

5.s: tvaṣṭā pūṣā tathaivendro dvādaśo viṣṇurucyate | dvandvaṃ tasyāstu tajjajñe mitraśca varuṇaśca ha ||
5.d: त्वष्टा पूषा तथैवेन्द्रो द्वादशो विष्णुरुच्यते | द्वन्द्वं तस्यास्तु तज्जज्ञे मित्रश्च वरुणश्च ह ||
5.e: Tvastr, Pusan, and also Indra; the twelfth is called Visnu. (Thus) that pair was born of her-Mitra and Varuna.

5.s: tayorādityayoḥ sattre dṛṣṭvāpsarasamurvaśīm | retaścaskanda tatkumbhe nyapatadvāsatīvare ||
5.d: तयोरादित्ययोः सत्त्रे दृष्ट्वाप्सरसमुर्वशीम् | रेतश्चस्कन्द तत्कुम्भे न्यपतद्वासतीवरे ||

5.s: tenaiva tu muhūrtena vīryavantau tapasvinau | agastyaśca vasiṣṭhaśca tatrarṣī saṃbabhūvataḥ ||
5.d: तेनैव तु मुहूर्तेन वीर्यवन्तौ तपस्विनौ | अगस्त्यश्च वसिष्ठश्च तत्रर्षी संबभूवतः ||
5.e: Now at that same moment two vigorous ascetics, the seers Agastya a and Vasistha, there came into being. a On the story of the birth of Agastya see Sieg, Sagenstoffe, pp. 105-108.

5.s: bahudhā patite śukre kalaśe'tha jale sthale || sthale vasiṣṭhastu muniḥ saṃbhūta ṛṣisattamaḥ ||
5.d: बहुधा पतिते शुक्रे कलशेऽथ जले स्थले || स्थले वसिष्ठस्तु मुनिः संभूत ऋषिसत्तमः ||
5.e: Now the semen having fallen in various ways-in a jar, in water, on the ground-the sage Vasistha, best of seers, was produced on the ground; patite sukre mrfkn, patitam retah bs.

5.s: kumbhe tvagastyaḥ saṃbhūto jale matsyo mahādyutiḥ | udiyāya tato'gastyaḥ śamyāmātro mahāyaśāḥ ||
5.d: कुम्भे त्वगस्त्यः संभूतो जले मत्स्यो महाद्युतिः | उदियाय ततोऽगस्त्यः शम्यामात्रो महायशाः ||

5.s: mānena saṃmito yasmāt tasmānmānya ihocyate | yadvā kumbhādṛṣirjātaḥ kumbhenāpi hi mīyate ||
5.d: मानेन संमितो यस्मात् तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते | यद्वा कुम्भादृषिर्जातः कुम्भेनापि हि मीयते ||
5.e: Because he was meted with a measure, he is here called Manya; or else (because) the seer was born from a jar. For measurement is made with a jar also: hi

5.s: kumbha ityabhidhānaṃ tu parimāṇasya lakṣyate | tato'psu guhyamāṇāsu vasiṣṭhaḥ puṣkare sthitaḥ ||
5.d: कुम्भ इत्यभिधानं तु परिमाणस्य लक्ष्यते | ततोऽप्सु गुह्यमाणासु वसिष्ठः पुष्करे स्थितः ||

5.s: nāmāsya guṇato jajñe vasateḥ śraiṣṭhyakarmaṇaḥ | adṛśyamṛṣibhirhīndraṃ so'paśyattapasā purā ||
5.d: नामास्य गुणतो जज्ञे वसतेः श्रैष्ठ्यकर्मणः | अदृश्यमृषिभिर्हीन्द्रं सोऽपश्यत्तपसा पुरा ||
5.e: His name arose, with reference to his virtue (gunatah), from the root vas expressive of pre-eminence: for he once upon a time, by means of austerity, saw Indra who was invisible to (other) seers.

5.s: somabhāgānatho tasmai provāca harivāhanaḥ | ṛṣayo vā indramiti brāhmaṇāttaddhi dṛśyate ||
5.d: सोमभागानथो तस्मै प्रोवाच हरिवाहनः | ऋषयो वा इन्द्रमिति ब्राह्मणात्तद्धि दृश्यते ||
5.e: The Lord of Bay Steeds (Indra) then proclaimed to him (that he should receive) shares in Soma. B For this appears from the Brahmana (passage) 'The seers (saw not) Indra' (rsayo va indram). somabhaganatha Am', somabhagamstatas B.

5.s: vasiṣṭhaśca vasiṣṭhāśca brāhmaṇā brahmakarmaṇi | sarvakarmasu yajñeṣu dakṣiṇīyatamāstathā ||
5.d: वसिष्ठश्च वसिष्ठाश्च ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मकर्मणि | सर्वकर्मसु यज्ञेषु दक्षिणीयतमास्तथा ||
5.e: Vasistha and the Vasisthas thus (became) Brahmans in the office of Brahman priest, most worthy of fees in all rites at sacrifices. vasisthasca vasisthasca B, vasisthasca vasisthasca Am'.

5.s: tasmādye'dyāpi vāsiṣṭhāḥ sadasyāḥ syustu karhicit | arhayeddakṣiṇābhistān bhāllaveyī śrutistviyam ||
5.d: तस्माद्येऽद्यापि वासिष्ठाः सदस्याः स्युस्तु कर्हिचित् | अर्हयेद्दक्षिणाभिस्तान् भाल्लवेयी श्रुतिस्त्वियम् ||
5.e: Therefore one should honour with fees all such descendants of Vasistha who may at any time even to-day be present at a sacrificial assembly, so (says) a sacred text of the Bhallavins. ye'dyapi Am 1, adyapi B.

5.s: ṛṣistu maitrāvaruṇiḥ sūktaiḥ ṣoḻaśabhiḥ paraiḥ | tuṣṭāvāgnimiti tvagnim āpryastatra juṣasva naḥ ||
5.d: ऋषिस्तु मैत्रावरुणिः सूक्तैः षोḻअशभिः परैः | तुष्टावाग्निमिति त्वग्निम् आप्र्यस्तत्र जुषस्व नः ||
5.e: Now the seer, the son of Mitra-Varuna (Vasistha), with the following sixteen a hymns (beginning) 'Agni' (agnim: vii. 1. 1) praised Agni; Enjoy our' (jusasva nah: vii. 2) here are Apri stanzas.

5.s: prāgnaye'tha pra samrājo dvitīyaṃ prāgnaye tṛcam | vaiśvānarīyāṇyetāni tve haindrāṇi parāṇyataḥ ||
5.d: प्राग्नयेऽथ प्र सम्राजो द्वितीयं प्राग्नये तृचम् | वैश्वानरीयाण्येतानि त्वे हैन्द्राणि पराण्यतः ||
5.e: Then 'Forth to Agni' (pragnaye: vii. 5), 'Forth of the sovereign lord' (pra samrajah: vii. 6), the second Forth to Agni' (pragnaye: vii. 13) which consists of three stanzas-these are addressed to Vaisvanara. Then those which follow, (beginning) 'In thee, indeed' (tve ha: vii. 18), are addressed to Indra, 162. being fifteen hymns (vii. 18-32): praise of the Maruts is incidental (in them). In the (stanza) 'No one Sudass' (nakih sudasah vii. 32. 10) the gift of Paijavana (Sudas)

5.s: daśa pañca ca sūktāni nipāto marutāṃ stutiḥ | nakiḥ sudāsa ityasyāṃ dānaṃ paijavanasya tu ||
5.d: दश पञ्च च सूक्तानि निपातो मरुतां स्तुतिः | नकिः सुदास इत्यस्यां दानं पैजवनस्य तु ||

5.s: vasiṣṭhena caturbhistu dve napturiti kīrtitam || saṃvādaṃ sūktamaindraṃ vā śvityañcastu pracakṣate ||
5.d: वसिष्ठेन चतुर्भिस्तु द्वे नप्तुरिति कीर्तितम् || संवादं सूक्तमैन्द्रं वा श्वित्यञ्चस्तु प्रचक्षते ||

5.s: vasiṣṭhāgastyayoratra kīrtyate tanayaiḥ saha | indreṇa caiva saṃvādo mahimā janma karma ca ||
5.d: वसिष्ठागस्त्ययोरत्र कीर्त्यते तनयैः सह | इन्द्रेण चैव संवादो महिमा जन्म कर्म च ||
5.e: Here is proclaimed a dialogue of Vasistha and Agastya with their sons and also with Indra, and (their) greatness, birth, and action (are celebrated).

5.s: parāṇi preti catvāri vaiśvadevāni tatra tu | stotyṛgabjāmahiṃ tatra mā no'hiṃ budhnyameva ca ||
5.d: पराणि प्रेति चत्वारि वैश्वदेवानि तत्र तु | स्तोत्यृगब्जामहिं तत्र मा नोऽहिं बुध्न्यमेव च ||
5.e: The following four (hymns) 'Forth' (pra: vii. 34-37) are addressed to the All-gods. There, however, the stanza 'Born in the waters' (abjam: vii. 34. 16) praises the Dragon (ahi), and there 'May us not' (ma nah: vii. 34. 17) (praises) the Dragon of the Deep (ahi budhnya).

5.s: ahirāhanti meghānsa eti vā teṣu madhyamaḥ | yo'hiḥ sa budhnyo vudhne hi ṇo'ntarikṣe'bhijāyate ||
5.d: अहिराहन्ति मेघान्स एति वा तेषु मध्यमः | योऽहिः स बुध्न्यो वुध्ने हि णोऽन्तरिक्षेऽभिजायते ||
5.e: The Dragon (ahi) strikes (ahanti) the clouds, or he goes in the midst among them. The Dragon is of the deep (budhnya), for he is born in the deep (budhna), the air.

5.s: udu ṣya savituḥ sūktaṃ śaṃ no vājinadaivataḥ | dvṛco'rdharcaśca bhāgo'tra bhagamugra iti śrutiḥ ||
5.d: उदु ष्य सवितुः सूक्तं शं नो वाजिनदैवतः | द्वृचोऽर्धर्चश्च भागोऽत्र भगमुग्र इति श्रुतिः ||
5.e: On high that' (ud u syah: vii. 38) is a hymn of Savitr. Here the couplet Blessed for us' (sam nah: vii. 38. 7, 8) has Steeds as its divinities, and the hemistich 'On Bhaga the mighty' (bhagam ugrah: vii. 38. 6 cd) is addressed to Bhaga, so a sacred text (states). I.

5.s: pādaścaiva tṛtīyo'tra pañcamyāmahidaivataḥ | yathārdharco bhagamugras tathā nūnaṃ bhago'pi ca ||
5.d: पादश्चैव तृतीयोऽत्र पञ्चम्यामहिदैवतः | यथार्धर्चो भगमुग्रस् तथा नूनं भगोऽपि च ||
5.e: And the third verse in the fifth (stanza) here (vii. 38. 5°) a has the Dragon for its divinity. B As the hemistich 'On Bhaga the mighty' (bhagam ugrah: vii. 38.6 cd), so also is Now Bhaga' (nunam bhagah: vii. 38.

5.s: sa hi ratnāni savitā suvātīti bhagaḥ sa vā | vaiśvadevāni pañcordhvaḥ pañcarco bhagadaivataḥ ||
5.d: स हि रत्नानि सविता सुवातीति भगः स वा | वैश्वदेवानि पञ्चोर्ध्वः पञ्चर्चो भगदैवतः ||

5.s: prātarjitamuṣasyāntyā draṣṭṛbhyo'trāśireva vā | eke tu drātarityasyāṃ bhagameva pracakṣate ||
5.d: प्रातर्जितमुषस्यान्त्या द्रष्टृभ्योऽत्राशिरेव वा | एके तु द्रातरित्यस्यां भगमेव प्रचक्षते ||
5.e: (beginning) 'Winning at morn' (pratarjitam : vii. 41.2-6). The last (stanza) is addressed to Dawn (vii. 41. 7), or else a prayer a for the seers (drastr) b is here (expressed ). Some, however, pronounce Bhaga only to be (the deity) in the ( stanza) - At morn' (pratal : vii. 41.1 ) .

5.s: ādāvante tu ṛṣayaḥ kīrtayanti prasaṅgataḥ | sūkte'smindevatāstvanyā anyāstatra bhavanti ca ||
5.d: आदावन्ते तु ऋषयः कीर्तयन्ति प्रसङ्गतः | सूक्तेऽस्मिन्देवतास्त्वन्या अन्यास्तत्र भवन्ति च ||
5.e: Now the seers at the beginning and end (of hymns) proclaim (deities) in an occasional manner & (prasangatah) : (thus) in this hymn there are some deities (here) and others (there) in that place (tatra)b.

5.s: sālokyātsāhacaryādvā saṃstavādathavā punaḥ | gaṇasthānādbhaktito vā kīrtyante'nyāstu devatāḥ ||
5.d: सालोक्यात्साहचर्याद्वा संस्तवादथवा पुनः | गणस्थानाद्भक्तितो वा कीर्त्यन्तेऽन्यास्तु देवताः ||
5.e: Other deities are proclaimed because they belong to the same world or because they are associated, or else again because they share praise (samstavat), because of the sphere of (their accompanying) troop (gana)b, or because of (common) attribute (bhaktital)..

5.s: dādhikramatha sāvitraṃ raudramityanupūrvaśaḥ | dādhike prathamāyāstu devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ||
5.d: दाधिक्रमथ सावित्रं रौद्रमित्यनुपूर्वशः | दाधिके प्रथमायास्तु देवताः परिकीर्तिताः ||
5.e: Next (come) one (hymn) addressed to Dadhikra (vii. 44), one to Savitr (vii. 45), one to Rudra (vii. 46) in succession. But the deities proclaimed as belonging to the first (stanza) of (the hymn) addressed to Dadhikra (vii. 44. 1)

5.s: tā jñeyā āpa āpyaṃ syād ārbhavaḥ prathamastṛcaḥ | uttamā vaiśvadevī vā ārbhavī vā nigadyate ||
5.d: ता ज्ञेया आप आप्यं स्याद् आर्भवः प्रथमस्तृचः | उत्तमा वैश्वदेवी वा आर्भवी वा निगद्यते ||

5.s: vaiśvadeve tathā śāstre ārbhavaṃ śasyate hi tat | daśame'hni samastaṃ samudrajyeṣṭhā apāṃ stutiḥ ||
5.d: वैश्वदेवे तथा शास्त्रे आर्भवं शस्यते हि तत् | दशमेऽह्नि समस्तं समुद्रज्येष्ठा अपां स्तुतिः ||
5.e: For it is thus that this entire (hymn) addressed to the Rbhus is chanted on the tenth day in the litany to the All-gods. "Whose chief the sea' (samudrajyesthah vii. 49) is (in) praise of the Waters.

6.s: ā māmiti tu sūktena pratyṛcaṃ devatā stutāḥ | mitravaruṇāvagniśca devā nadyastathaiva ca ||
6.d: आ मामिति तु सूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं देवता स्तुताः | मित्रवरुणावग्निश्च देवा नद्यस्तथैव च ||
6.e: Now with the hymn Guard me' (a mam: vii. 50) the deities are praised in successive stanzas: B Mitra-Varuna (1), and Agni (2), the (All)-gods (3), as well as the Rivers (4). m'r,

6.s: tṛcāvādityadevatyau rodasyoḥ preti yastṛcaḥ | vāstoṣpatyaścatasrastu sapta prasvāpinyaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
6.d: तृचावादित्यदेवत्यौ रोदस्योः प्रेति यस्तृचः | वास्तोष्पत्यश्चतस्रस्तु सप्त प्रस्वापिन्यः स्मृताः ||
6.e: Two triplets (vii. 51, 52) have the Adityas for their deities. The triplet which (begins) Forth' (pra: vii. 53. 1-3) is to the Two Worlds (rodasi). There are (then) four (stanzas: vii. 54. 1-3, 55. 1) addressed to Vastospati; the seven (following: vii. 55. 2-8) are traditionally held to be lullaby stanzas.

6.s: paraṃ catvāri sūktāni mārutāni ka īmiti | teṣāṃ tu pitaraṃ devaṃ tryambakaṃ stautyṛguttamā ||
6.d: परं चत्वारि सूक्तानि मारुतानि क ईमिति | तेषां तु पितरं देवं त्र्यम्बकं स्तौत्यृगुत्तमा ||
6.e: After this there are four hymns addressed to the Maruts (beginning) 'Who, pray?' (ka im: vii. 56-59); the last stanza of these (vii. 59. 12) praises Tryambaka, the divine father. param Am', tatah B.

6.s: stutau tu mitrāvaruṇau sūktairyaditi saptabhiḥ | aśvinau tu parairdevāv aṣṭabhiḥ prati vāmiti ||
6.d: स्तुतौ तु मित्रावरुणौ सूक्तैर्यदिति सप्तभिः | अश्विनौ तु परैर्देवाव् अष्टभिः प्रति वामिति ||
6.e: With the seven hymns beginning 'When' (yat: vii. 60-66) Mitra-Varuna are praised; but with the following eight (beginning) 'To meet your' (prati vam: vii. 67-74) the divine Asvins.

6.s: yadadyaikotsūryastisra udvetītyardhapañcamāḥ | sauryastaccakṣuriti tu gīyate cakṣurdevatā ||
6.d: यदद्यैकोत्सूर्यस्तिस्र उद्वेतीत्यर्धपञ्चमाः | सौर्यस्तच्चक्षुरिति तु गीयते चक्षुर्देवता ||
6.e: (In) 'When to-day' (yad adya: vii. 60) one (1), (in) 'Aloft the sun' (ut suryah: vii. 62) three (1-3), (in) 'Aloft he goes' (ud veti: vii. 63) four and a half (1-5 ab) are addressed to Surya, while (in) 'That eye' (tac caksuh: vii. 66. 16) a the eye (of the sun) is sung as the deity.

6.s: ādityānāṃ tadvo adya dve ṛcau śaunako'bravīt | anyāḥ sarvā ṛcaḥ sauryo yadadyādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
6.d: आदित्यानां तद्वो अद्य द्वे ऋचौ शौनकोऽब्रवीत् | अन्याः सर्वा ऋचः सौर्यो यदद्याद्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ||
6.e: Saunaka has stated that the two stanzas 'Thus of you to-day' (tad vo adya: vii. 66. 12, 13) belong to the Adityas, while all the other stanzas, ' When to-day' (yad adya: vii. 66. 4-11) and the rest, are proclaimed (by him) a to be addressed to Surya. .

6.s: ime cetāra ityādyāḥ satre mitro mitaḥ stutaḥ | aryamṇo varuṇasyāpi mitrasyaitā nava smṛtāḥ ||
6.d: इमे चेतार इत्याद्याः सत्रे मित्रो मितः स्तुतः | अर्यम्णो वरुणस्यापि मित्रस्यैता नव स्मृताः ||
6.e: These chastisers' (ime cetarah vii. 60. 5) and the rest... these nine are traditionally held to belong to Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuna.

6.s: yadadya sūra ityādyā daśādityā ṛcaḥ smṛtāḥ | savitā vāditirmitro varuṇaścāryamā bhagaḥ ||
6.d: यदद्य सूर इत्याद्या दशादित्या ऋचः स्मृताः | सविता वादितिर्मित्रो वरुणश्चार्यमा भगः ||
6.e: The ten stanzas beginning When to-day the sun's' (yad adya surah: vii. 66. 4-13) are traditionally held to be addressed to the Adityas; or else Savitr, Aditi, Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman, Bhaga

6.s: stutā udu tyadityetās tisraḥ sauryastataḥ parāḥ | āśīstaccakṣurityetām ācāryaḥ śaunako'bravīt ||
6.d: स्तुता उदु त्यदित्येतास् तिस्रः सौर्यस्ततः पराः | आशीस्तच्चक्षुरित्येताम् आचार्यः शौनकोऽब्रवीत् ||

6.s: uṣāstu saptabhirvyuṣāḥ sūktānyebhyaḥ parāṇi tu | catvārīndrāvaruṇeti indrāvaruṇayo stutiḥ ||
6.d: उषास्तु सप्तभिर्व्युषाः सूक्तान्येभ्यः पराणि तु | चत्वारीन्द्रावरुणेति इन्द्रावरुणयो स्तुतिः ||
6.e: Now Dawn (is praised) with the seven (hymns) 'Forth the Dawn' (vy usah: vii. 75-81); but the four hymns following these, 'O Indra and Varuna' (indravaruna: vii. 82-85), are (in) praise of Indra-Varuna.

6.s: udu jyotiriti tvasminn ardharce madhyama stutaḥ | varuṇasya gṛhānnātrau vasiṣṭhaḥ svapna ācarat ||
6.d: उदु ज्योतिरिति त्वस्मिन्न् अर्धर्चे मध्यम स्तुतः | वरुणस्य गृहान्नात्रौ वसिष्ठः स्वप्न आचरत् ||
6.e: In the hemistich Aloft the light' (ud u jyotih vii. 76. 1 ab) the Middle (Agni) is praised. During a the night Vasistha in a dream b approached the house of Varuna. - 11 ab is not found in A or

6.s: prāviveśātha taṃ tatra śvā nadannabhyadhāvata | krandantaṃ sārameyaṃ sa dhāvantaṃ daṣṭusudyatam ||
6.d: प्राविवेशाथ तं तत्र श्वा नदन्नभ्यधावत | क्रन्दन्तं सारमेयं स धावन्तं दष्टुसुद्यतम् ||
6.e: He then entered. A dog there ran at him, barking. B Pacifying the hound which was making a din and running (up) with intent to bite, he lulled him to sleep (vyasusvapat) with the two (stanzas) When, O bright one' (yad arjuna: vii. 55. 2, 3). ( He sent him b as well as the other attendants of Varuna to sleep.

6.s: yadarjuneti ca dvābhyāṃ sāntvayitvā vyasuṣvapat | sa taṃ prasvāpayāmāsa janamanyaṃ ca vāruṇam ||
6.d: यदर्जुनेति च द्वाभ्यां सान्त्वयित्वा व्यसुष्वपत् | स तं प्रस्वापयामास जनमन्यं च वारुणम् ||

6.s: tatastu varuṇo rājā svaiḥ pāśaiḥ pratyabadhyata | sa baddhaḥ pitaraṃ sūktaiś caturbhirita uttaraiḥ ||
6.d: ततस्तु वरुणो राजा स्वैः पाशैः प्रत्यबध्यत | स बद्धः पितरं सूक्तैश् चतुर्भिरित उत्तरैः ||
6.e: Then king Varuna bound a him with his fetters. Bound (thus) he (Vasistha) praised his father (Varuna) with the next (itah) b following four (hymns) 'The wise' (dhira: vii. 86-89). Then his father released him. A As soon as the (stanza) Thee in the fixed' (dhruvasu tva: vii. 88. 7) had been uttered, the fetters dropped (pramocire)c from him. svaih pasaih pratyabadhyata Am' (prati om ' ), svanpasanpratyamuncata Bn.

6.s: abhituṣṭāva dhīreti mumocairna tataḥ pitā | dhruvāsu tveti coktāyāṃ pāśā asmātpramocire ||
6.d: अभितुष्टाव धीरेति मुमोचैर्न ततः पिता | ध्रुवासु त्वेति चोक्तायां पाशा अस्मात्प्रमोचिरे ||

6.s: parāṇi trīṇi saktāni vāyavyāni pra vīrayā | atra tāstvaindravāyavyā stutau yāsu dvivatstutiḥ ||
6.d: पराणि त्रीणि सक्तानि वायव्यानि प्र वीरया | अत्र तास्त्वैन्द्रवायव्या स्तुतौ यासु द्विवत्स्तुतिः ||
6.e: The next three hymns, Forth with longing for the heroes' (pra viraya: vii. 90-92), are addressed to Vayu. Now in this praise those (stanzas) are addressed to Indra-Vayu in which there is praise in the dual (dvivat). tastvai॰ Am', tascai ° B.

6.s: pra vīrayoktā vāyavyā prāugītyaitareyake | padasya vyatyayaṃ kṛtvā vāyoḥ prādhānyamucyate ||
6.d: प्र वीरयोक्ता वायव्या प्राउगीत्यैतरेयके | पदस्य व्यत्ययं कृत्वा वायोः प्राधान्यमुच्यते ||
6.e: Forth with longing for the heroes' (pra viraya: vii. is spoken of in the Aitareya (Brahmana) a as a stanza addressed to Vayu belonging to the Prauga litany (praagi): the predominance of Vayu is (thereby) expressed in contravention (vyatyayam krtva) of one of its verses (pada).

6.s: te satyena tṛco yāvat taraścaturṛcaḥ punaḥ | uśantaikā pra sotā carga dvayoretā nava smṛtāḥ ||
6.d: ते सत्येन तृचो यावत् तरश्चतुरृचः पुनः | उशन्तैका प्र सोता चर्ग द्वयोरेता नव स्मृताः ||
6.e: 'These with true' (te satyena: vii. 90. 5-7) being a triplet, 'As long as strength' (yavat tarah: vii. 91. 4-7), again, being a quatrain, 'Eager' (usanta: vii. 91. 2), being one, and the stanza Forth the presser' (pra sota: vii. 92. 2)-these are traditionally held to be the nine (stanzas) belonging to the two (Indra-Vayu).

6.s: endrāgne śucimityete preti sārasvate pare | ṛcā sarasvān sa iti janīyantaśca tisṛbhiḥ ||
6.d: एन्द्राग्ने शुचिमित्येते प्रेति सारस्वते परे | ऋचा सरस्वान् स इति जनीयन्तश्च तिसृभिः ||
6.e: The two (hymns) 'The pure' (sucim: vii. 93,94) are addressed to Indra-Agni; the two following, 'Forth' (pra: vii. 95, 96), are addressed to Sarasvati. Sarasvat (is praised) with the stanza 'He' (sah: vii. 95. 3) and with the three 'Longing for wives' (janiyantah: vii. 96. 4-6).

6.s: rājā varṣasahasrāya dīkṣiṣyannāhuṣaḥ purā | cacāraikarathenemāṃ bruvan sarvāḥ samudragāḥ ||
6.d: राजा वर्षसहस्राय दीक्षिष्यन्नाहुषः पुरा | चचारैकरथेनेमां ब्रुवन् सर्वाः समुद्रगाः ||
6.e: King Nahusa a in former days wishing to consecrate himself for a thousand years, travelled over this (earth) with a single chariot, saying to all

6.s: yakṣye vahata bhāgānme dvandvaśo vāthavaikaśaḥ | pratyūcustaṃ nṛpaṃ nadyaḥ svalpavīryāḥ kathaṃ vayam ||
6.d: यक्ष्ये वहत भागान्मे द्वन्द्वशो वाथवैकशः | प्रत्यूचुस्तं नृपं नद्यः स्वल्पवीर्याः कथं वयम् ||
6.e: 'I am about to offer sacrifice; bring me shares (for it), either in pairs or singly.' The rivers replied to the king: How can we, who have but very little power,

6.s: vahema bhāgātsarvāṃste satre vāryasahasrike | sarasvatīṃ prapadyasva sā te vakṣyati nāhuṣa ||
6.d: वहेम भागात्सर्वांस्ते सत्रे वार्यसहस्रिके | सरस्वतीं प्रपद्यस्व सा ते वक्ष्यति नाहुष ||

6.s: tathetyuktvā jagāmāśu āpagāṃ sa sarasvatīm | sā cainaṃ pratijagrāha duduhe ca payo ghṛtam ||
6.d: तथेत्युक्त्वा जगामाशु आपगां स सरस्वतीम् | सा चैनं प्रतिजग्राह दुदुहे च पयो घृतम् ||
6.e: Saying 'So be it,' he quickly went to the river Sarasvati; and she received him and yielded (duduhe) (him) milk (and) ghee. jagamasu Am', jagamatha B.

6.s: etadatyadbhutaṃ karma sarasvatyā nṛpaṃ prati | vāruṇiḥ kīrtayāmāsa prathamasya dvitīyayā ||
6.d: एतदत्यद्भुतं कर्म सरस्वत्या नृपं प्रति | वारुणिः कीर्तयामास प्रथमस्य द्वितीयया ||
6.e: This exceedingly marvellous act of the Sarasvati towards the king, the son of Varuna (Vasistha) proclaimed with the second (stanza) of the first (of the two hymns, viz. vii. 95. 2). No MS. marks the end of the varga; but that it ends here is indicated by the fact that the figure u is in b placed after 26 ab, which in that MS. by mistake ends similarly, viz. prathamasya trtiyaya (see critical note on 26).

6.s: yajñe bārhaspatyamaindraṃ vaiṣṇave tu pare tataḥ | urumaindryaśca tisraḥ syuḥ pārjanye tisra uttare ||
6.d: यज्ञे बार्हस्पत्यमैन्द्रं वैष्णवे तु परे ततः | उरुमैन्द्र्यश्च तिस्रः स्युः पार्जन्ये तिस्र उत्तरे ||
6.e: 'In the sacrifice' (yajne: vii. 97) is addressed to Brhaspati; (then comes) (hymn) addressed to Indra (vii. 98); but the two following (99, 100) after that are addressed to Visnu, and the vii. 104 three (stanzas) 'Wide' (urum: vii. 99. 4-6) should be (regarded as) addressed to Indra as well. The two next (hymns) Three' (tisrah: 101, 102) are addressed to Parjanya.

6.s: stautīndraṃ prathamā tvatra dvitīyādyā bṛhaspatim | yajña ādyendramevāstaud antyā tvindrābṛhaspatī ||
6.d: स्तौतीन्द्रं प्रथमा त्वत्र द्वितीयाद्या बृहस्पतिम् | यज्ञ आद्येन्द्रमेवास्तौद् अन्त्या त्विन्द्राबृहस्पती ||
6.e: Now the first (stanza) here (vii. 97. 1) praises Indra, the second and the rest (2, 4-8) (praise) Brhaspati. B In 'At the sacrifice' (yajne: vii. 97) the first (stanza) praised Indra alone, but the last both Indra and Brhaspati. is the reading of Am1; instead of this line

6.s: tṛtīyā navamī caiva stautīndrābrahmaṇaspati | saṃvatsaraṃ tu maṇḍūkān aindrāsomaṃ paraṃ tu yat ||
6.d: तृतीया नवमी चैव स्तौतीन्द्राब्रह्मणस्पति | संवत्सरं तु मण्डूकान् ऐन्द्रासोमं परं तु यत् ||
6.e: The third and the ninth (vii. 97. 3, 9) praise Indra and Brahmanaspati. (The hymn) For a year' (samvatsaram: vii. 103) (praises) the frogs; but that which follows (vii. 104) is addressed to Indra-Soma.

6.s: ṛṣirdadarśa rākṣoghnaṃ putraśokapariplutaḥ | hate putraśate tasmin saudāsairduḥkhitastadā ||
6.d: ऋषिर्ददर्श राक्षोघ्नं पुत्रशोकपरिप्लुतः | हते पुत्रशते तस्मिन् सौदासैर्दुःखितस्तदा ||
6.e: The seer, when his hundred sons had been slain by the followers of Sudas, full of pain and overwhelmed with grief for his sons, saw (this hymn) for the destruction of demons II.

6.s: ye pākaśaṃsamṛksaumyā āgneyī tat uttarā | ekādaśī vaiśvadevī saumyastasyāḥ paro dvṛcaḥ ||
6.d: ये पाकशंसमृक्सौम्या आग्नेयी तत् उत्तरा | एकादशी वैश्वदेवी सौम्यस्तस्याः परो द्वृचः ||
6.e: The stanza 'Who the simple' (ye pakasamsam: vii. 104. 9) is addressed to Soma; the next (10) after that is addressed to Agni; the eleventh is addressed to the All-gods (11); the couplet which follows it (12, 13) is addressed to Soma.

6.s: yadi vāhamṛgāgneyī aindrī yo meti tu smṛtā | grāvṇī pra yā jigātoti vi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ tu mārutī ||
6.d: यदि वाहमृगाग्नेयी ऐन्द्री यो मेति तु स्मृता | ग्राव्णी प्र या जिगातोति वि तिष्ठध्वं तु मारुती ||
6.e: The stanza 'As if I' (yadi vaham: vii. 104. 14) is addressed to Agni, while Who me' (yo ma: 16) is traditionally held to be addressed to Indra; 'She who strides forth' (pra ya jigati: 17) is addressed to the pressing stones, while 'Spread out' (vi tisthadhvam: 18) is addressed to the Maruts.

6.s: pra vartayeti pañcendrya pendrāsomī tvṛguttamā | ṛṣistvāśiṣamāśāste mā no rakṣa iti tvṛci ||
6.d: प्र वर्तयेति पञ्चेन्द्र्य पेन्द्रासोमी त्वृगुत्तमा | ऋषिस्त्वाशिषमाशास्ते मा नो रक्ष इति त्वृचि ||
6.e: Five (stanzas, beginning) Hurl forth' (pra vartaya: vii. 104. 19-22, 24) are addressed to Indra, while the last stanza is addressed to Indra-Soma. In the stanza 'May not the demon us' (ma no raksas: 23) the seer invokes a blessing

6.s: divi caiva pṛthivyāṃ ca tathā pālanamātmanaḥ | ulūkayātuṃ jahyetān nānārūpānniśācarān ||
6.d: दिवि चैव पृथिव्यां च तथा पालनमात्मनः | उलूकयातुं जह्येतान् नानारूपान्निशाचरान् ||

6.s: pañcadaśyāṃ tu sūktasya aṣṭamyāṃ caiva vāruṇiḥ | duḥkhaśokaparītātmā śapate vilapanniva ||
6.d: पञ्चदश्यां तु सूक्तस्य अष्टम्यां चैव वारुणिः | दुःखशोकपरीतात्मा शपते विलपन्निव ||
6.e: Now in the fifteenth and in the eighth ( stanza) of the hymn the son of Varuna (Vasistha), while as it were lamenting, his soul being overwhelmed with pain and grief, utters a curse. suktasya astamyam hd, (°sya )

6.s: hate putraśate tasmin vasiṣṭho duḥkhitastadā | rakṣobhūtena śāpāttu sudāseneti vai śrutiḥ ||
6.d: हते पुत्रशते तस्मिन् वसिष्ठो दुःखितस्तदा | रक्षोभूतेन शापात्तु सुदासेनेति वै श्रुतिः ||
6.e: Vasistha was at that time pained, as his hundred sons had been slain by Sudasa a who, in consequence of a curse, had been transformed into a demon (raksas); such is the sacred tradition.

6.s: aṣṭama maṇḍala kaṇvaścaiva pragāthaśca ghoraputrau babhūvatuḥ | guruṇā tāvanujñātāv ūṣatuḥ sahitau vane ||
6.d: अष्टम मण्डल कण्वश्चैव प्रगाथश्च घोरपुत्रौ बभूवतुः | गुरुणा तावनुज्ञाताव् ऊषतुः सहितौ वने ||

6.s: vasatostu tayostatra kaṇvapatnyā śiraḥ svapat | kṛtvā kanīyānkaṇvasya utsaṅge nānvabudhyata ||
6.d: वसतोस्तु तयोस्तत्र कण्वपत्न्या शिरः स्वपत् | कृत्वा कनीयान्कण्वस्य उत्सङ्गे नान्वबुध्यत ||
6.e: Now while these two dwelt there the younger (brother) of Kanva (i.e. Pragatha), having placed his head while asleep (svapat) a on the lap of Kanva's wife, did not awake.

6.s: śaptukāmastu taṃ kaṇvaḥ kruddhaḥ pāpābhiśaṅkayā | bodhayāmāsa pādena didhakṣanniva tejasā ||
6.d: शप्तुकामस्तु तं कण्वः क्रुद्धः पापाभिशङ्कया | बोधयामास पादेन दिधक्षन्निव तेजसा ||
6.e: Now Kanva, enraged by suspicion of a sin (and) wishing to curse him, awakened him with his foot, as though about to consume him with his fiery energy.

6.s: viditvā tasya taṃ bhāvaṃ pragāthaḥ prāñjali sthitaḥ | mātṛtve ca pitṛtve ca varayāmāsa tāvubhau ||
6.d: विदित्वा तस्य तं भावं प्रगाथः प्राञ्जलि स्थितः | मातृत्वे च पितृत्वे च वरयामास तावुभौ ||
6.e: Pragatha, becoming aware of his intention, stood with folded hands and chose the couple for his mother and father. tam

6.s: sa ghauro vātha kāṇvo vā vaṃśajairbahubhiḥ saha | dadarśānyaiśca sahita ṛṣirmaṇḍalamaṣṭamam ||
6.d: स घौरो वाथ काण्वो वा वंशजैर्बहुभिः सह | ददर्शान्यैश्च सहित ऋषिर्मण्डलमष्टमम् ||
6.e: The seer, being (thus) the son of either Ghora or Kanva, saw, in company with many other members of his family, the eighth Mandala.

6.s: mācidaindrāṇi catvāri anvasya sthūramityṛci | tuṣṭāvāṅgirasī nārī vasantī śāśvatī patim ||
6.d: माचिदैन्द्राणि चत्वारि अन्वस्य स्थूरमित्यृचि | तुष्टावाङ्गिरसी नारी वसन्ती शाश्वती पतिम् ||
6.e: There are four hymns addressed to Indra (beginning) 'Not at all' (ma cit: viii. 1-4) in the stanza 'Downward his mighty' (anv asya sthuram: viii. 1. 34), Sasvati, daughter of Angiras, living (vasanti) a as his wife (nari), praised her husband.

6.s: striyaṃ santaṃ pumāṃsaṃ tam āsaṅgaṃ kṛtavānṛṣiḥ | svasya dānaṃ stuhītyṛgbhiś caturbhiḥ parikīrtitam ||
6.d: स्त्रियं सन्तं पुमांसं तम् आसङ्गं कृतवानृषिः | स्वस्य दानं स्तुहीत्यृग्भिश् चतुर्भिः परिकीर्तितम् ||
6.e: The seer turned that Asanga, who had been a woman, into a man (again). With the four b stanzas Praise' (stuhi: viii. 1. 30-33) his own gift (to the seer) is proclaimed (by Asanga).

6.s: śikṣetyṛgbhyāṃ tu kāśyasya vibhindoḥ parikīrtitam | pākasthāmnastu bhojasya caturbhiryamiti stutam ||
6.d: शिक्षेत्यृग्भ्यां तु काश्यस्य विभिन्दोः परिकीर्तितम् | पाकस्थाम्नस्तु भोजस्य चतुर्भिर्यमिति स्तुतम् ||
6.e: But with the two stanzas Bestow' (siksa: viii. 2. 41, 42) that of Vibhindu, king of Kasi (kasya)a, is proclaimed, while with the four (stanzas) 'Which' (yam: viii. 3. 21-24) the (gift) of the liberal Pakasthaman is praised.

6.s: pauṣṇau preti pragāthau dvau manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ | aindramevātha pūrvaṃ tu gālavaḥ pauṣṇamuttaram ||
6.d: पौष्णौ प्रेति प्रगाथौ द्वौ मन्यते शाकटायनः | ऐन्द्रमेवाथ पूर्वं तु गालवः पौष्णमुत्तरम् ||
6.e: The two pragatha couplets (beginning) Forth' (pra: viii. 4. 15-18) Sakatayana thinks are addressed to Pusan; Galava, however, (thinks) the former (15, 16) is addressed to Indra only, the latter (17, 18) to Pusan.

6.s: aindrāṇāmiha sūktānām uttamasyottame tṛce | dānaṃ rājñaḥ kuruṅgasya sthūraṃ rāya iti stutam ||
6.d: ऐन्द्राणामिह सूक्तानाम् उत्तमस्योत्तमे तृचे | दानं राज्ञः कुरुङ्गस्य स्थूरं राय इति स्तुतम् ||
6.e: In the last triplet of the last of the Indra hymns here (viii. 4. 19-21), the gift of king Kurunga is praised (with the words) 'Abundant wealth' (sthuram radhah: 19).

6.s: dūrādityāśvine sūkte saptatriṃśattamī yathā | ityardharco dvṛcaścāntyaḥ kaśordānastutiḥ smṛtā ||
6.d: दूरादित्याश्विने सूक्ते सप्तत्रिंशत्तमी यथा | इत्यर्धर्चो द्वृचश्चान्त्यः कशोर्दानस्तुतिः स्मृता ||
6.e: In the hymn addressed to the Asvins, 'From afar' (durat: viii. 5), the thirty-seventh stanza, (that is) the hemistich 'As' (yatha: 37), and the final couplet (38, 39) are traditionally held to be (in) praise of the gifts of Kasu.

6.s: mahānaindraṃ pratnavatyām agniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ stutam | manyate śākapūṇistu bhārmyaśvaścaiva mudgalaḥ ||
6.d: महानैन्द्रं प्रत्नवत्याम् अग्निं वैश्वानरं स्तुतम् | मन्यते शाकपूणिस्तु भार्म्यश्वश्चैव मुद्गलः ||
6.e: 'Great' (mahan: viii. 6) is addressed to Indra: in (the stanza) containing (the word) 'ancient' (pratna: viii. 6. 30), Sakapuni, as well as Mudgala, son of Bhrmyasva, thinks Agni Vaisvanara is praised.

6.s: tṛce tu śatamityasmin dānaṃ tairindiraṃ smṛtam | paraṃ nu mārutaṃ preti ā nastrīṇyāśvināni ca ||

6.e: But in the triplet 'A hundred' (satam: viii. 6. 46-48) the gift of Tirindira a is recorded. 'Forth' (pra: viii. 7), the following (hymn), is addressed to the Maruts; and the three 'Hither to us (a nah viii. 8-10) are addressed to the Asvins.

6.s: tvamāgneyaṃ ya indreti ṣaḻaindrāṇyuttamasya tu | upottamāyāmardharce devo vāstoṣpati stutaḥ ||
6.d: त्वमाग्नेयं य इन्द्रेति षḻऐन्द्राण्युत्तमस्य तु | उपोत्तमायामर्धर्चे देवो वास्तोष्पति स्तुतः ||
6.e: Thou' (tvam: viii. 11) is addressed to Agni. O Indra' (ya indra: viii. 12. 1) are six (12-17) addressed to Indra; but in a hemistich of the last (stanza) but one of the last (viii. 17. 14 ab) the god Vastospati is praised. viii.

6.s: idamādinyadevatyaṃ tisṛbhistvaditi stutā | ṣaṣṭhyā caturthyā saptamyā utetyācinyagaṣṭamī ||
6.d: इदमादिन्यदेवत्यं तिसृभिस्त्वदिति स्तुता | षष्ठ्या चतुर्थ्या सप्तम्या उतेत्याचिन्यगष्टमी ||
6.e: 'This' (idam: viii. 18) has the Adityas as its deities: with three (of its stanzas), the sixth, the fourth, and the seventh, Aditi is praised; the eighth stanza, 'And' (uta), is addressed to the Asvins.

6.s: stutāḥ śamiti pacchastu agnisūryānilāstrayaḥ | varuṇāryamamitrāṇāṃ pragātho yamiti stutiḥ ||
6.d: स्तुताः शमिति पच्छस्तु अग्निसूर्यानिलास्त्रयः | वरुणार्यममित्राणां प्रगाथो यमिति स्तुतिः ||
6.e: (In) 'Blessing' (sam: viii. 18. 9) the three (gods) Fire (agni), Sun (surya), Wind (anila)a are (respectively) praised in successive verses (pac-chah). The pragatha couplet 'Whom' (yam: viii. 19. 34, 35) is (in) praise of Varuna, Aryaman, and Mitra pachastva ° A, pacchosyam, sachasyom, sasthasoma k, sachasyom. - 0 mitranam Am'

6.s: āgneye stutī rājarṣes trasadasyoradāditi | pañcāśataṃ vadhūnāṃ ca gavāṃ tistraśca saptatīḥ ||
6.d: आग्नेये स्तुती राजर्षेस् त्रसदस्योरदादिति | पञ्चाशतं वधूनां च गवां तिस्त्रश्च सप्ततीः ||

6.s: aśvoṣṭrāṇāṃ tathaivāsau vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca | ratnāni vṛṣabhaṃ śyāvaṃ tāsāmagnesaraṃ patim ||
6.d: अश्वोष्ट्राणां तथैवासौ वासांसि विविधानि च | रत्नानि वृषभं श्यावं तासामग्नेसरं पतिम् ||

6.e: Having wedded, the seer as he went on his way proclaimed (all) this to Indra, and with the hymn 'We' (vayam: viii. 21) (praised) Sakra. Pleased thereby the Lord of Saci 0samsa ca m ebfkn, 0samsa ha r.

6.d: ऋषे वरं वृणीष्वेति प्रह्वस्तमृषिरब्रवीत् | काकुत्स्थकन्याः पञ्चाशद् युगपद्रमये प्रभो ||
6.e: (said), 'O seer, choose a boon.' Humbly the seer replied to him: 'I (will) enjoy, O Lord, simultaneously the fifty maidens a of the race of

6.e: When Sobhari, son of Kanva, was sacrificing with members of his family in Kuruksetra, rats devoured (his) corn and various oblations. (So) he (Sobhari) praised Indra, Citra, (and) Sarasvati, B with the stanza 'Or Indra' (indro va: viii. 21. 17), proclaiming (Citra's) power of giving. sobharescaiva Am', saubharescaiva B.

6.s: ākhavaḥ so'bhituṣṭāva indraṃ citraṃ sarasvatīm | indro vetyanayarcā sa dānaśaktiṃ prakāśayan ||

6.s: ākhurājo'bhimānācca praharṣitamanāḥ svayam | saṃstuto devayaccitra ṛṣaye tu gavāṃ dadau ||

6.d: अयुतानां सहस्रं वै निजग्राह स्तुवन्नृषिः | ऋषिं चोवाच हृष्टात्मा नाहमर्हाम्यृषे स्तुतिम् ||

6.s: tiryagyonau samutpanno devatā stotumarhasi | tamantyayāpunaścāstaud o tyaṃ sūktena cāśvinau ||
6.d: तिर्यग्योनौ समुत्पन्नो देवता स्तोतुमर्हसि | तमन्त्ययापुनश्चास्तौद् ओ त्यं सूक्तेन चाश्विनौ ||

6.s: īḻiṣvetyetadāgneyaṃ sakhāyaścaindramuttaram | yathā varo suṣāmyā ity uttamastvauṣasastṛcaḥ ||
6.d: ईḻइष्वेत्येतदाग्नेयं सखायश्चैन्द्रमुत्तरम् | यथा वरो सुषाम्या इत्य् उत्तमस्त्वौषसस्तृचः ||
6.e: The (hymn) 'Laud thou' (ilisva: viii. 23) is addressed to Agni, and the next one 'O friends' (sakhayah: viii. 24) is addressed to Indra, but the last triplet, As to Varo-susaman' (yatha varo susamne: viii. 24. 28-30), is addressed to Dawn.

6.s: aṣṭau tu sahitāstvetā devatā bibhidurbalam | uṣāścendraśca somaśca agniḥ sūryo bṛhaspatiḥ ||
6.d: अष्टौ तु सहितास्त्वेता देवता बिभिदुर्बलम् | उषाश्चेन्द्रश्च सोमश्च अग्निः सूर्यो बृहस्पतिः ||
6.e: Now it is these eight deities altogether who cleft Vala: Usas and Indra and Soma, Agni, Surya, Brhaspatia, astau tu

6.s: aṅgirāḥ saramā caiva tā vāmityuttarasya tu | ādau maitrāvaruṇyastu nava dvādaśa tūttarāḥ ||
6.d: अङ्गिराः सरमा चैव ता वामित्युत्तरस्य तु | आदौ मैत्रावरुण्यस्तु नव द्वादश तूत्तराः ||
6.e: Angiras and Sarama. Now at the beginning of the next hymn 'You two as such' (ta vam: viii. 25) there are nine (stanzas) addressed to Mitra-Varuna, but the next twelve a viii.

6.s: vaiśvadevyo varū rājā yaccādādṛṣaye vasu | kīrtitaṃ tattṛce tvasminn ṛjramukṣaṇyāyane ||
6.d: वैश्वदेव्यो वरू राजा यच्चादादृषये वसु | कीर्तितं तत्तृचे त्वस्मिन्न् ऋज्रमुक्षण्यायने ||

6.s: aśvinau dadatuḥ prītau tadihoktaṃ suṣāmaṇi | āśvinaṃ tu yuvoryukṣva vāyavyā uttarāstu yāḥ ||
6.d: अश्विनौ ददतुः प्रीतौ तदिहोक्तं सुषामणि | आश्विनं तु युवोर्युक्ष्व वायव्या उत्तरास्तु याः ||
6.e: (What) the Asvins, being pleased, bestowed on Susaman, is told here: (viz.) "Of you two' (yuvoh: viii. 26) is addressed to the Asvins: 'Do thou yoke

6.s: yaṃ savarṇā manurnāma lebhe putraṃ vivasvataḥ | vaiśvadevāni pañcaitāny agnirukthe jagāda saḥ ||
6.d: यं सवर्णा मनुर्नाम लेभे पुत्रं विवस्वतः | वैश्वदेवानि पञ्चैतान्य् अग्निरुक्थे जगाद सः ||
6.e: Manu, as he was named, whom Savarna a obtained as a son from Vivasvat, uttered the five hymns (27-31) addressed to the 228 All-gods (and beginning) Agni at the laudation' (agnir ukthe: viii. 27).

6.s: babhrureka iti tvetā liṅgato dvipadā daśa | stūyante devatā hyāsu karmabhiḥ svaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak ||
6.d: बभ्रुरेक इति त्वेता लिङ्गतो द्विपदा दश | स्तूयन्ते देवता ह्यासु कर्मभिः स्वैः पृथक्पृथक् ||
6.e: 'Brown is one' (babhrur ekah: viii. 29)-these are ten dvipadas with characteristic marks (lingatah); for in them the deities are praised, each separately, by their activities.

6.s: stutāḥ karmaguṇaiḥ svaiḥ svair devatā yatra tatra tu | pṛthakkarmastutirnāma vaiśvadevaṃ tadeva tu ||
6.d: स्तुताः कर्मगुणैः स्वैः स्वैर् देवता यत्र तत्र तु | पृथक्कर्मस्तुतिर्नाम वैश्वदेवं तदेव तु ||
6.e: Now where the deities are praised by their respective actions and qualities, there is what is called separate praise of action (prthak-karma-stuti). Such (hymn) is addressed to the All-gods. , follows the reading of Am1; the reading of Bis: prthakkarmastutivyuktam tadvidyadvaisvadaivatam .

6.s: tāsāṃ babhruriti tvādyā saumyāgneyī tvṛguttarā | tvāṣṭrī caindrī ca raudrī ca pauṣṇī vaiṣṇavyṛgāśvinī ||
6.d: तासां बभ्रुरिति त्वाद्या सौम्याग्नेयी त्वृगुत्तरा | त्वाष्ट्री चैन्द्री च रौद्री च पौष्णी वैष्णव्यृगाश्विनी ||
6.e: Now of these (dvipadas) the first 'Brown' (babhruh: viii. 29. 1) is addressed to Soma, but the next stanza (2) is addressed to Agni; (then comes) one addressed to Tvastr (3), and Indra (4) and Rudra (5), Pusan (6), Visnu (7), a stanza addressed to the Asvins (8); 72. the ninth is addressed to Mitra-Varuna (9), the tenth stanza is (in) praise of the Atris. And in connexion with the institutor of the sacrifice (in) Who' (yah: viii. 31) the sacrifice (ijya) b is here praised.

6.s: navamī maitrāvaruṇī ṛgdaśamyatrisaṃstavaḥ | yajamānaprasaṅgācca ya ijyātra prakīrtitā ||
6.d: नवमी मैत्रावरुणी ऋग्दशम्यत्रिसंस्तवः | यजमानप्रसङ्गाच्च य इज्यात्र प्रकीर्तिता ||

6.s: yo jayati dvṛce śakro yajatāṃ patirīḻitaḥ | tasya dyumān dvṛce yajvā catasṛṣvapi makṣviti ||
6.d: यो जयति द्वृचे शक्रो यजतां पतिरीḻइतः | तस्य द्युमान् द्वृचे यज्वा चतसृष्वपि मक्ष्विति ||

6.e: In 'Downward' (adhah: viii. 33. 19) a girl addressed Indra (who appeared) with the characteristics of a woman; for the chastiser of Paka (Indra) made love to that Danava maiden

6.s: jyeṣṭhāṃ svasāraṃ vyaṃsasya tasyaiva yuvakāmyayā | agninetyāśvinaṃ sūktam aindrasūkte pare tataḥ ||
6.d: ज्येष्ठां स्वसारं व्यंसस्य तस्यैव युवकाम्यया | अग्निनेत्याश्विनं सूक्तम् ऐन्द्रसूक्ते परे ततः ||

6.s: aindrāgnaṃ paramāgneyam aindrāgnaṃ vāruṇe pare | uttare vāruṇe tvantya ā vāmitvāśvinastṛcaḥ ||
6.d: ऐन्द्राग्नं परमाग्नेयम् ऐन्द्राग्नं वारुणे परे | उत्तरे वारुणे त्वन्त्य आ वामित्वाश्विनस्तृचः ||
6.e: The following (38) is addressed to Indra-Agni, (then) one to Agni (39), one to Indra-Agni (40); the following two (41, 42) are addressed to Varuna; but in the latter (42) Varuna hymn the last triplet 'Hither you two' (a vam: viii. 42. 4-6) is addressed to the Asvins.

6.s: sūkte ime samāgneye tābhyāmaindre tataḥ pare | vaśāyāśvyāta yatprādāt kānīnastu pṛthuśravāḥ ||
6.d: सूक्ते इमे समाग्नेये ताभ्यामैन्द्रे ततः परे | वशायाश्व्यात यत्प्रादात् कानीनस्तु पृथुश्रवाः ||
6.e: The two hymns, 'These' (ime: viii. 43), 'With fuel' (sam-: viii. 44), are addressed to Agni; the two which then follow after these (45, 46) are addressed to Indra. Now what Kanita Prthusravas gave to Vasa Asvya a viii.

6.s: tadatra saṃstutaṃ dānam ā sa ityevamādibhiḥ | ā naḥ pragāthau vāyavyau sūktasyopottamā ca yā ||
6.d: तदत्र संस्तुतं दानम् आ स इत्येवमादिभिः | आ नः प्रगाथौ वायव्यौ सूक्तस्योपोत्तमा च या ||

6.s: mitrāryamāṇau marutaḥ sunītho gha dvṛce stutāḥ | dvicatvāriṃśakātprītas triśokāya puraṃdaraḥ ||
6.d: मित्रार्यमाणौ मरुतः सुनीथो घ द्वृचे स्तुताः | द्विचत्वारिंशकात्प्रीतस् त्रिशोकाय पुरंदरः ||
6.e: In the couplet Well led indeed' (sunitho gha: viii. 46. 4, 5), Mitra-Aryaman (and) the Maruts are praised. Pleased by (the hymn) containing forty-two stanzas (viii. 45) the Fort-destroyer (Indra), after cutting through the mountain with his bolt, gave to Trisoka the cows which had been carried off by the Asuras. The seer has stated this himself in the (stanza), Who clave' (yah krntat: viii. 45. 30).

6.s: giriṃ nikṛtya vajreṇa gā daśavasurairhṛtāḥ | yaḥ tṛntaditi caitasyām ṛṣistu svayamabravīt ||
6.d: गिरिं निकृत्य वज्रेण गा दशवसुरैर्हृताः | यः तृन्तदिति चैतस्याम् ऋषिस्तु स्वयमब्रवीत् ||

6.s: stutā navamyā tvaditira mahītyādityadaivate | antyā mañcoṣase'pi syuḥ saumyaṃ svādoriti smṛtam ||
6.d: स्तुता नवम्या त्वदितिर महीत्यादित्यदैवते | अन्त्या मञ्चोषसेऽपि स्युः सौम्यं स्वादोरिति स्मृतम् ||
6.e: In (the hymn) 'Great' (mahi: viii. 47), of which the Adityas are the deities, Aditi is praised with the ninth (stanza). The last five (stanzas: 14-18) should be (considered as addressed) to Dawn as well (api). Of the sweet' (svadoh: viii. 48) is traditionally held to be addressed to Soma.

6.s: parāṇyaṣṭau tu sūktāni ṛṣīṇāṃ tigmatejasām | aindrāṇyatra tu ṣaḍviṃśaḥ pragātho bahudaivataḥ ||
6.d: पराण्यष्टौ तु सूक्तानि ऋषीणां तिग्मतेजसाम् | ऐन्द्राण्यत्र तु षड्विंशः प्रगाथो बहुदैवतः ||
6.e: Now the following eight hymns (viii. 49-56), by seers of ardent brilliance, are addressed to Indra; but the twenty- 232 sixth pragatha couplet here (viii. 54. 3, 4) is addressed to many deities. paranyastau tu Am', parani castau B.

6.s: ṛgantyāgneracetyagniḥ sūryamantyaṃ padaṃ jagau | praskaṇvaśca pṛṣadhrasya prādādyadvasu kiṃcana ||
6.d: ऋगन्त्याग्नेरचेत्यग्निः सूर्यमन्त्यं पदं जगौ | प्रस्कण्वश्च पृषध्रस्य प्रादाद्यद्वसु किंचन ||
6.e: The last stanza, Agni has appeared' (acety agnih: viii. 56. 5), is to Agni; the last verse (pada) a sang of Surya (viii. 56. 5). Whatever wealth Praskanva gave to

6.s: tadūbhūrīditi sūktābhyām akhilaṃ tviha saṃstutam | aindrāṇyubhayamityatra ṣaḻāgneyātparāṇi tu ||
6.d: तदूभूरीदिति सूक्ताभ्याम् अखिलं त्विह संस्तुतम् | ऐन्द्राण्युभयमित्यत्र षḻआग्नेयात्पराणि तु ||

6.s: nipātamāha devānāṃ dātā ma hati bhāguriḥ || ṛcaṃ yāskastṛcaṃ tvetaṃ manyate vaiśvadevatam | ādityadaivataṃ sūktaṃ tyānnvityatra paraṃ tu yat ||
6.d: निपातमाह देवानां दाता म हति भागुरिः || ऋचं यास्कस्तृचं त्वेतं मन्यते वैश्वदेवतम् | आदित्यदैवतं सूक्तं त्यान्न्वित्यत्र परं तु यत् ||
6.e: Yaska, however, considers this triplet (viii. 65. 10-12) to be addressed to the All-gods. But the hymn which here follows, 'Now these' (tyan nu: viii. 67), has the Adityas as its divinities.

6.s: dhīvarāḥ sahasā mīnān dṛṣṭvā sārasvate jale | jālaṃ prakṣipya tānbaddhvod akṣipansalilātsthalam ||
6.d: धीवराः सहसा मीनान् दृष्ट्वा सारस्वते जले | जालं प्रक्षिप्य तान्बद्ध्वोद् अक्षिपन्सलिलात्स्थलम् ||
6.e: Fishermen, having by chance seen fish in the water of the Sarasvati, cast a net, caught them, and threw them upon a the dry land out of the water.

6.s: śarīrapātabhītāste tuṣṭuvuścāditeḥ sutān | mumucustāṃstataste ca prasannāstān samudire ||
6.d: शरीरपातभीतास्ते तुष्टुवुश्चादितेः सुतान् | मुमुचुस्तांस्ततस्ते च प्रसन्नास्तान् समुदिरे ||
6.e: And they, frightened by the fall of their bodies, praised the sons of Aditi. And they (the Adityas) then released them, and graciously conversed with them (the

6.s: dhīvarāḥ kṣudbhayaṃ mā vo bhūt svargaṃ prāptyatheti ca | uteti mātā tatraiṣāṃ tṛcenābhiṣṭutāditiḥ ||
6.d: धीवराः क्षुद्भयं मा वो भूत् स्वर्गं प्राप्त्यथेति च | उतेति माता तत्रैषां तृचेनाभिष्टुतादितिः ||
6.e: (saying) 'O fishermen, be not afraid of hunger,' and 'Ye shall obtain heaven.' In that hymn (tatra: viii. 67), Aditi, the mother of these (Adityas), is praised with the triplet And' (uta viii. 67. 10-12).

6.s: mātṛtvādabhisaṃbandhāt stūyetaiṣāṃ stutau stutau | aindrāṇyā tvā rathaṃ trīṇi stautyṛtūnupa meti ṣaṭ ||
6.d: मातृत्वादभिसंबन्धात् स्तूयेतैषां स्तुतौ स्तुतौ | ऐन्द्राण्या त्वा रथं त्रीणि स्तौत्यृतूनुप मेति षट् ||
6.e: Because she is their mother she may be praised in every praise of them owing to (this) connexion. 'Hither thee as a car' (a tva ratham: viii. 68-70) are three hymns addressed to Indra; (the stanza) 'Near to me six' (upa ma sat: viii. 68. 14) a praises the seasons.

6.s: kakṣīśvamedhayoratra pañca dānastutiḥ parāḥ | apādindrasya cāgneśca viśveṣāṃ caiva saṃstavaḥ ||
6.d: कक्षीश्वमेधयोरत्र पञ्च दानस्तुतिः पराः | अपादिन्द्रस्य चाग्नेश्च विश्वेषां चैव संस्तवः ||
6.e: The five following (stanzas) in this hymn (atra) are (in) praise of the gifts of Rksa and Asvamedha (viii. 68. 15-19). The first hemistich (11%) of the couplet 'He has drunk' (apat : viii. 69. 11, 12) is (in) praise of Indra, Agni, and the All-(gods); the rest (11 ed, 12) has Varuna as its divinity. Thou' (tvam: viii. 71, 72) are two (hymns) addressed to Agni; or the latter hymn (72) is (in) praise of oblations, rksasvamedhayoratra hd (rksasvamedhayor S), asrasvamedhayoratra m'r, arcapatya- svamedhaya, arttapatvyasvamedhaya f.

6.s: dvṛcasya prathamo'rdharcaḥ śeṣo varuṇadaivataḥ | tvamāgneye'thavā sūktam uttaraṃ haviṣāṃ stutiḥ ||
6.d: द्वृचस्य प्रथमोऽर्धर्चः शेषो वरुणदैवतः | त्वमाग्नेयेऽथवा सूक्तम् उत्तरं हविषां स्तुतिः ||

6.s: payaḥ paśvoṣadhīnāṃ ca tathārūpaṃ hi dṛśyate | udityāśvinamāgneye pare sūkte viśoviśaḥ ||
6.d: पयः पश्वोषधीनां च तथारूपं हि दृश्यते | उदित्याश्विनमाग्नेये परे सूक्ते विशोविशः ||

6.s: ṛgbhyāmahamiti dvābhyāṃ stautyātmānamṛṣiḥ svayam | ātmānamātmanā stutvā stauti dānaṃ śrutarvaṇaḥ ||
6.d: ऋग्भ्यामहमिति द्वाभ्यां स्तौत्यात्मानमृषिः स्वयम् | आत्मानमात्मना स्तुत्वा स्तौति दानं श्रुतर्वणः ||
6.e: With the two stanzas 'I' (aham: viii. 74. 13, 14) the seer praises himself. viii. 90 B Having praised himself, he praises the gift of Srutarvan 95 ed and 96 ab are not found in A, but in B and

6.s: ātmādānābhisaṃbandhāt paruṣṇīṃ ca mahānadīm | parayā paruṣṇīmindraṃ tribhiḥ sūktairimaṃ nviti ||
6.d: आत्मादानाभिसंबन्धात् परुष्णीं च महानदीम् | परया परुष्णीमिन्द्रं त्रिभिः सूक्तैरिमं न्विति ||

6.s: ayaṃ kṛtnuridaṃ saumyaṃ troṇyaindrāṇi parāṇyataḥ | nahīti teṣāṃ prathame vaiśvadevyṛgavīvṛdhat ||
6.d: अयं कृत्नुरिदं सौम्यं त्रोण्यैन्द्राणि पराण्यतः | नहीति तेषां प्रथमे वैश्वदेव्यृगवीवृधत् ||
6.e: This active' (ayam krtnuh: viii. 79) is addressed to Soma. The three following this (beginning) 'Truly not' (nahi: viii. 80-82) are addressed to Indra. In the first of these (80) the stanza He has exalted' (avivrdhat: 10) is addressed to the All-gods. r.
