6.s: devānāmiti devānāṃ preṣṭamāgneyamuttaram | trīṇyāśvinātyā ma iti aindrāṇi tamitīti ca ||
6.d: देवानामिति देवानां प्रेष्टमाग्नेयमुत्तरम् | त्रीण्याश्विनात्या म इति ऐन्द्राणि तमितीति च ||
6.e: 'Of the gods' (devanam: viii. 83) is to the Gods; the next, 'The dearest' (prestham: viii. 84), is addressed to Agni. 'Hither to my' (a me viii. 85-87) are three addressed to the Asvins, and 'Him' (tam: viii. 88-90) are similarly (iti) (three) addressed to Indra.

6.s: apālātrisutā tvāsīt kanyā tvagdoṣiṇī purā | tāmindraścakame dṛṣṭvā vijane piturāśrame ||
6.d: अपालात्रिसुता त्वासीत् कन्या त्वग्दोषिणी पुरा | तामिन्द्रश्चकमे दृष्ट्वा विजने पितुराश्रमे ||

6.s: tapasā bubudhe sā tu sarvamindrakīrṣitam | udakumbhaṃ samādāya apāmardhe jagāma sā ||
6.d: तपसा बुबुधे सा तु सर्वमिन्द्रकीर्षितम् | उदकुम्भं समादाय अपामर्धे जगाम सा ||
6.e: Now by penance she became aware of all Indra's intentions. Taking a water-pot she went to fetch water.

6.s: daṣṭvā somamapāmante tuṣṭāvarcā vane tu tam | kanyā vāriti caitasyām eṣo'rthaḥ kathitastataḥ ||
6.d: दष्ट्वा सोममपामन्ते तुष्टावर्चा वने तु तम् | कन्या वारिति चैतस्याम् एषोऽर्थः कथितस्ततः ||
6.e: Seeing Soma at the edge of the water, she praised him with a stanza in the forest. This matter is related in the (stanza) 'A maiden to the water' (kanya vah: viii. 91. 1).

6.s: sā suṣāva mukhe somaṃ sutvendraṃ cājuhāva tam | asau ya eṣītyanayā papāvindraśca tanmukhāt ||
6.d: सा सुषाव मुखे सोमं सुत्वेन्द्रं चाजुहाव तम् | असौ य एषीत्यनया पपाविन्द्रश्च तन्मुखात् ||
6.e: She pressed Soma in her mouth; B and having pressed it she invoked Indra with the (stanza), 'Thou that goest' (asau ya esi: viii. 91. 2); and Indra drank it from her mouth, bc sa

6.s: apūpāṃścaiva saktūṃ'śca bhakṣayitvā sa tadgṛhāt | ṛgbhistuṣṭāva sā cainaṃ jagādainaṃ tṛcena tu ||
6.d: अपूपांश्चैव सक्तूंऽश्च भक्षयित्वा स तद्गृहात् | ऋग्भिस्तुष्टाव सा चैनं जगादैनं तृचेन तु ||

6.s: sulomāmanavadyāṅgīṃ kuru māṃ śakra sutvacam | tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā prītastena purandaraḥ ||
6.d: सुलोमामनवद्याङ्गीं कुरु मां शक्र सुत्वचम् | तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रीतस्तेन पुरन्दरः ||
6.e: 'Make me, O Sakra, to have abundant hair, (and) to be faultless-limbed, (and) fair-skinned.' B Hearing this speech of hers, the Fort-destroyer was pleased with it.

6.s: rathachidreṇa tāmindraḥ śakaṭasya yugasya ca | prakṣipya niścakarṣa triḥ sutvak sātu tato'bhavat ||
6.d: रथछिद्रेण तामिन्द्रः शकटस्य युगस्य च | प्रक्षिप्य निश्चकर्ष त्रिः सुत्वक् सातु ततोऽभवत् ||
6.e: Indra passing (praksipya) her through the carriage aperture (between the body) of the car and the yoke, drew her forth three times. Then she became fair-skinned.

6.s: tasyāstvagapahatā yā pūrvā sā śalyako'bhavat | uttarā tvabhavadgodhā kṛkalāsastvaguttamā ||
6.d: तस्यास्त्वगपहता या पूर्वा सा शल्यकोऽभवत् | उत्तरा त्वभवद्गोधा कृकलासस्त्वगुत्तमा ||
6.e: Her first skin which was cast off became a porcupine (salyaka), but the next became an alligator (godha), and the last a chameleon (krkalasa). 106 ab follows the reading of Am1; the reading of Bn is: tasyam tvaci vyapetayam sarvasyam salyako'bhavat | ( sarva0 bfkn, purva0 r ) The reading of A is favoured by that of Sadgurusisya: tasyah purvahata ya tvagjatih sa salyako'bhavat |

6.s: itihāsamidaṃ sūktam āhaturyāskabhāgurī | kanyeti śaunakastvaindraṃ pāntamityuttare ca ye ||
6.d: इतिहासमिदं सूक्तम् आहतुर्यास्कभागुरी | कन्येति शौनकस्त्वैन्द्रं पान्तमित्युत्तरे च ये ||
6.e: Yaska and Bhaguri call this hymn a story (itihasa), while Saunaka calls 'A maiden' (kanya: viii. 91) (hymn) addressed to Indra, as well as the two which come next (beginning) 'As one who drinks' (pantam: viii. 92, 93). itihasamidam Am', itihasamimam B.

6.s: uttamā tvārbhavī proktā uttarasyaitareyake | chāndomike tṛtīye tad ārbhavaṃ śasyate yataḥ ||
6.d: उत्तमा त्वार्भवी प्रोक्ता उत्तरस्यैतरेयके | छान्दोमिके तृतीये तद् आर्भवं शस्यते यतः ||
6.e: But the last ( stanza) of the latter (viii. 93. 34 ) is pronounced in the Aitareya (Brahmana) a to be addressed to the Rbhus; for on the third Chandoma (day ) b this hymn is chanted (sasyate) as one addressed to the Rbhus.

6.s: mārutaṃ gauḥ paraṃ sūktam ātvaindrāṇi parāṇi ṣaṭ | sūkte dvitīya eteṣām itihāsaṃ pracakṣate | apakramya tu devebhyaḥ somo vṛtrabhayārditaḥ ||
6.d: मारुतं गौः परं सूक्तम् आत्वैन्द्राणि पराणि षट् | सूक्ते द्वितीय एतेषाम् इतिहासं प्रचक्षते | अपक्रम्य तु देवेभ्यः सोमो वृत्रभयार्दितः ||
6.e: The following hymn, The cow' (gaul : viii. 94), is addressed to the Maruts; the following six, 'Hither to thee ' (a tva : viii. 95-100), are addressed to Indra. B In the second hymn of these (96) they say there is a story (itihasa) : a Soma, oppressed by fear of Vxtra, fled from the gods; a

6.s: nadīmaṃśumatīṃ nāmnā abhyatiṣṭhatkurūnprati | taṃ bṛhaspatinaikena abhyavādvṛtrahā saha ||
6.d: नदीमंशुमतीं नाम्ना अभ्यतिष्ठत्कुरून्प्रति | तं बृहस्पतिनैकेन अभ्यवाद्वृत्रहा सह ||

6.s: yotsyamānaḥ susaṃhṛṣṭair marudbhirvividhāyudhaiḥ | dṛṣṭvā tānāyataḥ somaḥ svabalena vyavasthitaḥ ||
6.d: योत्स्यमानः सुसंहृष्टैर् मरुद्भिर्विविधायुधैः | दृष्ट्वा तानायतः सोमः स्वबलेन व्यवस्थितः ||

6.s: manvāno vṛtramāyāntaṃ jighāṃsumarisenayā | vyavasthitaṃ dhanuṣmantaṃ tamuvāca bṛhaspatiḥ ||
6.d: मन्वानो वृत्रमायान्तं जिघांसुमरिसेनया | व्यवस्थितं धनुष्मन्तं तमुवाच बृहस्पतिः ||

6.s: marutpatirayaṃ soma ehi devānpunarvibho | śrutvā devagurorvākyam anarthaṃ vṛtraśaṅkayā ||
6.d: मरुत्पतिरयं सोम एहि देवान्पुनर्विभो | श्रुत्वा देवगुरोर्वाक्यम् अनर्थं वृत्रशङ्कया ||
6.e: This is the Lord of the Maruts, O Soma; come back to the gods, O Lord.' B Hearing the speech of the preceptor of the gods, which was unavailing because he believed it was Vrtra, soma ehi m'r,

6.s: so'bravīnneti taṃ śakraḥ svarga eva balādbalī | iyāya devānādāya taṃ papurvidhivatsurāḥ ||
6.d: सोऽब्रवीन्नेति तं शक्रः स्वर्ग एव बलाद्बली | इयाय देवानादाय तं पपुर्विधिवत्सुराः ||

6.s: jaghnuḥ pītvā ca daityānāṃ samare navatīrnava | tadetadapyavetyasmiṃs tṛce sarvaṃ nigadyate ||
6.d: जघ्नुः पीत्वा च दैत्यानां समरे नवतीर्नव | तदेतदप्यवेत्यस्मिंस् तृचे सर्वं निगद्यते ||
6.e: And having drunk (him) they slew in battle nine times ninety a demons. All this is related in the triplet 'Down' (ava: viii. 96. 13-15). ava

6.s: indraṃ ca marutaścaiva tathaiva ca bṛhaspatim | tṛcasya devatā hyetā indramevāha śaunakaḥ ||
6.d: इन्द्रं च मरुतश्चैव तथैव च बृहस्पतिम् | तृचस्य देवता ह्येता इन्द्रमेवाह शौनकः ||
6.e: (The seer praises) Indra, and the Maruts, and also Brhaspatia: for these are the deities of the triplet; Saunaka says that Indra alone (is the deity).

6.s: aindrābārhaspatya ukto brāhmaṇe tvaitareyake | tṛcenendramapaśyaṃstaṃ nemo'yamiti bhārgavaḥ ||
6.d: ऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्य उक्तो ब्राह्मणे त्वैतरेयके | तृचेनेन्द्रमपश्यंस्तं नेमोऽयमिति भार्गवः ||
6.e: But in the Aitareya (Brahmana) a it (the triplet) is said to be addressed to Indra-Brhaspati. With the triplet 'Here I' (ayam: viii. 100. 1-3) Nema, son of Bhrgu, praised

6.s: tuṣṭāvendro dvṛcenāyam ahaṃ paśya ca māmṛṣe | sa hi stuvannema eko nendrī astīti cābravīt ||
6.d: तुष्टावेन्द्रो द्वृचेनायम् अहं पश्य च मामृषे | स हि स्तुवन्नेम एको नेन्द्री अस्तीति चाब्रवीत् ||
6.e: And Indra (then) with a couplet (4, 5) (says), Here I am, behold me, seer.' B For Nema, being alone (eka) while praising (Indra), had also said, 'There is no Indra

6.s: tadākarṇyendra ātmānam ṛgbhyāṃ tuṣṭāva darśayan | ṛṣistaṃ dṛṣṭvā suprīto viśvettā ta iti dvṛce ||
6.d: तदाकर्ण्येन्द्र आत्मानम् ऋग्भ्यां तुष्टाव दर्शयन् | ऋषिस्तं दृष्ट्वा सुप्रीतो विश्वेत्ता त इति द्वृचे ||
6.e: Indra, on hearing that, praised himself with two stanzas (4, 5) as he showed himself. The seer on seeing him was greatly rejoiced, and in the couplet "All this of thee' (visvet ta te: viii. 100. 6, 7)

6.s: vividhāni ca karmāṇi dānamaindraṃ ca śaṃsati | manojavāstu sauparṇī samudraṃ vajrasaṃstavaḥ ||
6.d: विविधानि च कर्माणि दानमैन्द्रं च शंसति | मनोजवास्तु सौपर्णी समुद्रं वज्रसंस्तवः ||

6.s: vācaṃ sarvagatāṃ devīṃ stauti yadvāgiti dvṛce | trīllokānabhitapyemān vṛtrastasthau svayā tviṣā ||
6.d: वाचं सर्वगतां देवीं स्तौति यद्वागिति द्वृचे | त्रील्लोकानभितप्येमान् वृत्रस्तस्थौ स्वया त्विषा ||
6.e: In the couplet 'When Vac' (yad vak: 10, 11) he (the seer) praises the divine all-pervading Vac. Having a tormented these three worlds Vrtra remained (unassailable) by reason of his fury.

6.s: taṃ nāśakaddhantumindro viṣṇumabhyetya so'bravīt | vṛtraṃ haniṣye tiṣṭhasva vikramyādya mamāntike ||
6.d: तं नाशकद्धन्तुमिन्द्रो विष्णुमभ्येत्य सोऽब्रवीत् | वृत्रं हनिष्ये तिष्ठस्व विक्रम्याद्य ममान्तिके ||
6.e: Him Indra could not slay. Going to Visnu he said, 'I wish to slay Vrtra; stride forth to-day and stand at my side.

6.s: udyatasyaiva vajrasya dyaurdadātu mamāntaram | tatheti viṣṇustaccakre dyauścāsya vivaraṃ dadau ||
6.d: उद्यतस्यैव वज्रस्य द्यौर्ददातु ममान्तरम् | तथेति विष्णुस्तच्चक्रे द्यौश्चास्य विवरं ददौ ||
6.e: May Dyaus make room (antara) for my outstretched bolt.' Saying 'Yes,' Visnu did so, and Dyaus gave him an opening (vivara).

6.s: tadetadakhilaṃ proktaṃ sakhe viṣṇaviti tvṛci | maitrāvaruṇyaḥ sūktādyāś catasrastvṛdhagityṛcaḥ ||
6.d: तदेतदखिलं प्रोक्तं सखे विष्णविति त्वृचि | मैत्रावरुण्यः सूक्ताद्याश् चतस्रस्त्वृधगित्यृचः ||
6.e: All this is proclaimed in the stanza 'Friend Visnu' (sakhe visno: viii. 100. 12). But the first four stanzas of the hymn (beginning) Specially' (rdhak: viii. 101. 1-4) are addressed to Mitra-Varuna; proktam B 9, sarva A.

6.s: preti mitrāya pādāśca aryamṇo varuṇasya ca | trayaścaturthaḥ sarveṣām ādityānāmiti stutiḥ ||
6.d: प्रेति मित्राय पादाश्च अर्यम्णो वरुणस्य च | त्रयश्चतुर्थः सर्वेषाम् आदित्यानामिति स्तुतिः ||

6.s: parā tvādityadevatyā ā ma ityaśvino dvṛcaḥ | vāyavye saurye uṣasyā prabhāṃ vā candrasūryayoḥ ||
6.d: परा त्वादित्यदेवत्या आ म इत्यश्विनो द्वृचः | वायव्ये सौर्ये उषस्या प्रभां वा चन्द्रसूर्ययोः ||
6.e: But the following stanza (6) has the Adityas as its deities. 'Hither to me' (a me: 7, 8) is a couplet addressed to the Asvins; there are (then) two addressed to Vayu (9, 10), two to Surya (11, 12), one to Usas (13), or (the seer here praises) the light a of the sun and moon.

6.s: pāvamānī prajā heti mātetyṛgbhyāṃ tu gau stutā | tvamagne bṛhadāgneye pare'gnistvṛci saṃstutaḥ ||
6.d: पावमानी प्रजा हेति मातेत्यृग्भ्यां तु गौ स्तुता | त्वमग्ने बृहदाग्नेये परेऽग्निस्त्वृचि संस्तुतः ||
6.e: 'Generations truly' (praja ha: 14) is addressed to Pavamana, while with the two stanzas 'The mother' (mata: 15, 16) the Cow is praised. 'Thou, O Agni, great' (tvam agne brhat: 'Thou, ix. 67 viii. 102, 103) are two hymns addressed to Agni. But in a stanza of the latter (pare) is praised Agni, 128. the Middle, together with the Maruts and Rudras, (viz. in) Come, O Agni' (agne yahi: viii. 103. 14). B Or in the first hemistich, 'Generations truly' (praja ha: viii. 101. 14), Agni is here named, in B only.

6.s: marudbhiḥ saha rudraiśca āgne yāhīti madhyamaḥ | prajā hetyapi vārdharce prathame'gnirihocyate ||
6.d: मरुद्भिः सह रुद्रैश्च आग्ने याहीति मध्यमः | प्रजा हेत्यपि वार्धर्चे प्रथमेऽग्निरिहोच्यते ||

6.s: pāde tṛtīya ādityas turīye madhyama stutaḥ | ruhasye brāhmaṇe'pyevaṃ vyākhyataṃ hyaitareyake ||
6.d: पादे तृतीय आदित्यस् तुरीये मध्यम स्तुतः | रुहस्ये ब्राह्मणेऽप्येवं व्याख्यतं ह्यैतरेयके ||

6.s: navama maṇḍala pavamāna stutaḥ somo navame tviha maṇḍale | pavamānavadāpryastu samiddha iti saṃstutāḥ ||
6.d: नवम मण्डल पवमान स्तुतः सोमो नवमे त्विह मण्डले | पवमानवदाप्र्यस्तु समिद्ध इति संस्तुताः ||
6.e: Now Soma Pavamana is praised here in the ninth Mandala. (In the hymn) 'Kindled' (samiddhah: ix. 5) the Apri deities (apryah) are praised like Pavamana.

6.s: atra āyūṃṣīti cāsu tisṛṣvagnirnipātabhāk | avitā na iti tvasmiṃs tṛce pūṣṇā saha stutaḥ ||
6.d: अत्र आयूंषीति चासु तिसृष्वग्निर्निपातभाक् | अविता न इति त्वस्मिंस् तृचे पूष्णा सह स्तुतः ||
6.e: And in the three stanzas 'O Agni, life' (agna ayumsi: ix. 66. 19-21), Agni is incidental (nipatabhaj), while in the triplet 'Our protector' (avita nah: ix. 67. 10-12) he (Pavamana) a is praised together with Pusan. * Pusan is directly mentioned in 10, indirectly as kapardin in II, and aghrni in 12; ayam somah pavate occurs in II, ayam pavate in 12; cp. Sarvanukramani: avita nas tisrah pausnyo va, that is, the three stanzas 10-12 are addressed to Pusan or Pavamana. ..

6.s: āgneyyau dve ṛcāvatra yatta ityuttare tataḥ | ubhābhyāmiti sāvitrī āgnisāvitryṛguttarā ||
6.d: आग्नेय्यौ द्वे ऋचावत्र यत्त इत्युत्तरे ततः | उभाभ्यामिति सावित्री आग्निसावित्र्यृगुत्तरा ||
6.e: Then two later stanzas in this hymn (atra), 'which of thee' (yat te: ix. 67. 23, 24), are addressed to Agni; 'By both of these' (ubhabhyam: 25) is addressed to Savitr; the next stanza (26) is addressed to Agni and Savitra. savitri

6.s: punantu māṃ vaiśvadevī āgneyī tvṛgupa priyam | uttare ca va ityete svādhyāyādhyetṛ saṃstavaḥ ||
6.d: पुनन्तु मां वैश्वदेवी आग्नेयी त्वृगुप प्रियम् | उत्तरे च व इत्येते स्वाध्यायाध्येतृ संस्तवः ||
6.e: May they purify me' (punantu ma: ix. 67. 27) is addressed to the All-gods, while the stanza 'Near to the friend' (upa priyam: 29) is addressed to Agni, and the two next, Who' (yah: 31, 32), are (in) praise of the student of recitation (svadhyayadhyetr). a uttare ca ya

6.s: sūkte nirukte srakve'gnī rakṣohā dharmasaṃstavaḥ | sūryaḥvaccātmavaccāpi pavitramiti cocyate ||
6.d: सूक्ते निरुक्ते स्रक्वेऽग्नी रक्षोहा धर्मसंस्तवः | सूर्यःवच्चात्मवच्चापि पवित्रमिति चोच्यते ||
6.e: In the hymn 'At the rim' (srakve: ix. 73), when interpreted (nirukte), the demon-slaying Agnib (is spoken of), and 'The filter' (pavitram: ix. 83) is called a praise of the Kettle (gharma) as (representing) the Sun (surya) and the Soul (atman).

6.s: ārbhavastu bhavetpāda ṛbhurdhīra iti smṛtaḥ | nipātaistu tribhiḥ pādais trayo devā ihoditāḥ ||
6.d: आर्भवस्तु भवेत्पाद ऋभुर्धीर इति स्मृतः | निपातैस्तु त्रिभिः पादैस् त्रयो देवा इहोदिताः ||
6.e: The verse 'Deft, wise' (rbhur dhirah: ix. 87. 3) should be held to be addressed to Rbhu. Now three gods are here b mentioned incidentally (nipata) in three verses (pada)

6.s: brahmā devānāṃ tisroktās tribhistvetairdvṛcairdvṛcaiḥ | sūryavaccātmavaccāpi stūyate soma eva vā ||
6.d: ब्रह्मा देवानां तिस्रोक्तास् त्रिभिस्त्वेतैर्द्वृचैर्द्वृचैः | सूर्यवच्चात्मवच्चापि स्तूयते सोम एव वा ||

6.s: anāvṛṣṭyāṃ tu vartantyāṃ papraccharṣīñchacīpatiḥ | kāle durge mahatyasmin karmaṇā kena jīvatha ||
6.d: अनावृष्ट्यां तु वर्तन्त्यां पप्रच्छर्षीञ्छचीपतिः | काले दुर्गे महत्यस्मिन् कर्मणा केन जीवथ ||
6.e: Now while a drought was prevailing, the Lord of Saci asked (the) seersa, 'In this great time of distress, by what activity do you live

6.s: śakaṭaṃ śākinī gāvaḥ kṛṣirasyandanaṃ vanam | samudraḥ parvato rājā evaṃ jīvāmahe vayam ||
6.d: शकटं शाकिनी गावः कृषिरस्यन्दनं वनम् | समुद्रः पर्वतो राजा एवं जीवामहे वयम् ||
6.e: 'A cart, a field, kine, tillage, water that does not flow away (asyandana), a forest, the sea, a mountain, a king-by these means (evam) we live

6.s: stuvanneva śaśaṃsāsya ṛṣirāṅgirasaḥ śiśuḥ | nānānīyena sūktena ṛṣīṇāmeva saṃnidhau ||
6.d: स्तुवन्नेव शशंसास्य ऋषिराङ्गिरसः शिशुः | नानानीयेन सूक्तेन ऋषीणामेव संनिधौ ||
6.e: In praising (Indra) the seer Sisu, son of Angiras, declared (this) to him with the hymn Variously' (nananam: ix. 112) in the presence of the (other) seers.

6.s: tānindrastvāha sarvāṃstu tapadhvaṃ sumahattapaḥ | na hyṛte tapasaḥ śakyam idaṃ kṛchraṃ vyapohitum ||
6.d: तानिन्द्रस्त्वाह सर्वांस्तु तपध्वं सुमहत्तपः | न ह्यृते तपसः शक्यम् इदं कृछ्रं व्यपोहितुम् ||
6.e: Now to all of them Indra said: 'Do ye perform very severe penance; for without penance this distress cannot be removed.'

6.s: atha te vai tapastepuḥ sarve svargajigīṣavaḥ | tataste tapasogreṇa pāvamānīrṛco'bruvan ||
6.d: अथ ते वै तपस्तेपुः सर्वे स्वर्गजिगीषवः | ततस्ते तपसोग्रेण पावमानीरृचोऽब्रुवन् ||
6.e: Now all of them, desirous of obtaining heaven, performed penance. Then in consequence of fierce austerity they pronounced stanzas relating to (Soma) Pavamana (pavamani).

6.s: anasūyuradhīyānaḥ śuśrūṣustapasānvitaḥ | daśa pūrvāparān vaṃśyān punātyātmānameva ca ||
6.d: अनसूयुरधीयानः शुश्रूषुस्तपसान्वितः | दश पूर्वापरान् वंश्यान् पुनात्यात्मानमेव च ||
6.e: One who is not envious, is studious, obedient, and practises penance, purifies ten ascendants and descendants as well as himself.

6.s: pāpaṃ yaccākarotkiṃcan manovāgdehabhojanaiḥ | pūtaḥ sa tasmātsarvasmāt svādhyāyaphalamaśnute ||
6.d: पापं यच्चाकरोत्किंचन् मनोवाग्देहभोजनैः | पूतः स तस्मात्सर्वस्मात् स्वाध्यायफलमश्नुते ||
6.e: And whatever sin he has committed with mind, speech, body, and food-purified from all that, he enjoys the fruit of Vedic study a yacca

6.s: pāvamānyaḥ paraṃ brahma śukraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanam | gāyatryo'nte'tra yaścāsāṃ prāṇānāyamya tanmanāḥ ||
6.d: पावमान्यः परं ब्रह्म शुक्रं ज्योतिः सनातनम् | गायत्र्योऽन्तेऽत्र यश्चासां प्राणानायम्य तन्मनाः ||
6.e: The Pavamani Gayatrisa are the supreme Brahma, the bright, eternal light. He who here at his latter end (ante), restraining his breathe, intent on them, a m'r, hd.-This sloka is not found in B, but in A and

6.s: pāvamānaṃ pitṝndevān dhyāyedyaśca sarasvatīm | pitṝṃstasyopavarteta kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakam ||
6.d: पावमानं पितॄन्देवान् ध्यायेद्यश्च सरस्वतीम् | पितॄंस्तस्योपवर्तेत क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकम् ||

6.s: etatsūktaśataṃ saumyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ sacaturdaśam | pāvamānamiti khyātam anuvākāstu sapta vai ||
6.d: एतत्सूक्तशतं सौम्यं मण्डलं सचतुर्दशम् | पावमानमिति ख्यातम् अनुवाकास्तु सप्त वै ||
6.e: This Mandala, addressed to Soma, containing one hundred and fourteen hymns, is called 'Pavamana,' and seven lessons (anuvaka) are (contained in it)a.

6.s: daśama maṇḍala saptāgneyāni sūktāni dadarśātha ḍati tritaḥ | pra ketuneti tvāṣṭrastu triśirāḥ sūktamuttaram ||
6.d: दशम मण्डल सप्ताग्नेयानि सूक्तानि ददर्शाथ डति त्रितः | प्र केतुनेति त्वाष्ट्रस्तु त्रिशिराः सूक्तमुत्तरम् ||
6.e: Trita saw seven hymns addressed to Agni (beginning), 'Before' (agre: x. 1-7), but Trisiras, son of Tvastr, the next hymn (beginning) 'Forth with his banner' (pra ketuna: x. 8).

6.s: ṛcastvasya ṣaḻāgneyyas tṛcastvasyeti yaḥ paraḥ | tenendramabhituṣṭāva svaprānta iti naḥ śrutiḥ ||
6.d: ऋचस्त्वस्य षḻआग्नेय्यस् तृचस्त्वस्येति यः परः | तेनेन्द्रमभितुष्टाव स्वप्रान्त इति नः श्रुतिः ||
6.e: Now six (stanzas) of this (hymn) are addressed to Agni (x. 8. 1-6), while with the triplet which follows, 'Of him' (asya: 7-9), he praised Indra at the end of a dream: such is our sacred tradition.

6.s: abhavatsa hi devānāṃ purodhāḥ priyakāmyayā | asurāṇāṃ svasuḥ putras triśirā viśvarūpadhṛk ||
6.d: अभवत्स हि देवानां पुरोधाः प्रियकाम्यया | असुराणां स्वसुः पुत्रस् त्रिशिरा विश्वरूपधृक् ||
6.e: Trisiras, who could assume all forms (visvarupadhrk), being the son of a sister of the Asuras, became the domestic priest of the gods from a desire of (rendering) a service (to the former). sa hi

6.s: tamṛṣiṃ prahitaṃ tvindro deveṣu bubudhe'suraiḥ | so'sya vajreṇa tānyāśu śirāṃsi trīṇyathāchidat ||
6.d: तमृषिं प्रहितं त्विन्द्रो देवेषु बुबुधेऽसुरैः | सोऽस्य वज्रेण तान्याशु शिरांसि त्रीण्यथाछिदत् ||
6.e: Now Indra became aware that the seer (Trisiras) had been sent by the Asuras among the gods. He then with his bolt quickly struck off a those three heads of his.

6.s: tasya yatsomapānaṃ tu mukhaṃ so'bhūtkapiñjalaḥ | kalaviṅkaḥ surāpāṇam annādaṃ tittiristvabhūt ||
6.d: तस्य यत्सोमपानं तु मुखं सोऽभूत्कपिञ्जलः | कलविङ्कः सुरापाणम् अन्नादं तित्तिरिस्त्वभूत् ||
6.e: The mouth with which he drank Soma became a francoline partridge (kapinjala); that with which he drank Sura (became) a sparrow (kalavinka); while that with which he ate food became a partridge (tittiri).

6.s: taṃ vāgabhyavadadbrāhmī brahmahāsi śatakrato | prapannaṃ hatavānyasmād viśvarūpaṃ parāṅmukham ||
6.d: तं वागभ्यवदद्ब्राह्मी ब्रह्महासि शतक्रतो | प्रपन्नं हतवान्यस्माद् विश्वरूपं पराङ्मुखम् ||
6.e: Him (Indra) divine (brahmi) Speech (vac) addressed: 'Thou art Brahman-slayer, Lord of a hundred powers (satakratu), since thou hast slain Visvarupa who sought refuge (prapanna) with averted face.'

6.s: tamabhyasiñcatsūktena ṛṣirāpa iti svayam | sindhudvīpo'panuttyarthaṃ tasyāślīlasya pāpmanaḥ ||
6.d: तमभ्यसिञ्चत्सूक्तेन ऋषिराप इति स्वयम् | सिन्धुद्वीपोऽपनुत्त्यर्थं तस्याश्लीलस्य पाप्मनः ||
6.e: Him (Indra) the seer Sindhudvipa a himself besprinkled, to the accompaniment of the hymn (suktena) 'O Waters' (apah: x. 9), for the removal of that unpropitious sin.

6.s: maithunārthamabhīpsantīṃ pratyācaṣṭe yamī yamaḥ | tado ciditi saṃvādo vivasvatsutayostayoḥ ||
6.d: मैथुनार्थमभीप्सन्तीं प्रत्याचष्टे यमी यमः | तदो चिदिति संवादो विवस्वत्सुतयोस्तयोः ||
6.e: Yama rejects Yami who solicits him with a view to sexual intercourse: the dialogue, 'Hither, indeed' (o cit: x. 10), of those two children of Vivasvat is (descriptive of) that. tado ciditi Am', o citsakhayam (the fuller pratika) B.

6.s: vṛṣāgneye havirdhāne yuje vāmatra saṃstute | pareyivāṃsamityatra stūyate madhyamo yamaḥ ||
6.d: वृषाग्नेये हविर्धाने युजे वामत्र संस्तुते | परेयिवांसमित्यत्र स्तूयते मध्यमो यमः ||
6.e: The two (hymns beginning) 'The bull' (vrsa: x. 11, 12) are addressed to Agni. In the hymn (atra) 'I yoke for you' (yuje vam: x. 13) the two oblation carts are praised together. In 'Him who has passed away' (pareyivamsam: x. 14) the Middle Yama a is praised.

6.s: atharvāṇo'tha bhṛgavo'ṅgirasaḥ pitaraḥ saha | ṣaṣṭyāṃ devagaṇāstatra saṃstūyante dyubhaktayaḥ ||
6.d: अथर्वाणोऽथ भृगवोऽङ्गिरसः पितरः सह | षष्ट्यां देवगणास्तत्र संस्तूयन्ते द्युभक्तयः ||
6.e: Then the Atharvans, the Bhrgus, the Angirases, the Fathers are praised together in the sixth (stanza) there (x. 14. 6), as groups of gods (devagana) connected with heaven (dyubhakti).

6.s: pitṛbhiścāṅgirobhiśca saṃstuto dṛśyate yamaḥ | mantreṣu bahuśaḥ pāde vivasvantaṃ pitā hi saḥ ||
6.d: पितृभिश्चाङ्गिरोभिश्च संस्तुतो दृश्यते यमः | मन्त्रेषु बहुशः पादे विवस्वन्तं पिता हि सः ||
6.e: Yama is frequently seen praised with the Fathers and the Angirases in the formulas; for in the verse 'Vivasvat' (vivasvantam x. 14. 5) he (himself appears as) Father.

6.s: saṃskāryapretasaṃyuktaiḥ pitṛbhi stūyate yamaḥ | prehi prehiti tisṛṣu pretāśiṣa udāhṛtāḥ ||
6.d: संस्कार्यप्रेतसंयुक्तैः पितृभि स्तूयते यमः | प्रेहि प्रेहिति तिसृषु प्रेताशिष उदाहृताः ||
6.e: Yama is praised with the Fathers in conjunction with the deceased man who is to be hallowed (samskarya). In the three (stanzas) Go forth, go forth' (prehi prehi: x. 14. 7-9) prayers for the deceased man are uttered.

6.s: pitṝṇāṃ hi patirdevo yamastasmātsa sūktabhāk | ati drava tṛce śvānau paraṃ pitryamudīratām ||
6.d: पितॄणां हि पतिर्देवो यमस्तस्मात्स सूक्तभाक् | अति द्रव तृचे श्वानौ परं पित्र्यमुदीरताम् ||
6.e: The god Yama is Lord of the Fathers; therefore he owns the hymn (sukta-bhaj). In the triplet 'Run past' (ati drava: x. 14. 10-12) the two dogs (are praised). The following (hymn) 'Let them arise' (ud iratam: x. 15) is addressed to the Fathers.

6.s: uttareṇa tu sūktena śmaśāne karma śaṃsati | pitṛdevāsurāṇāṃ ca abhavannagnayastrayaḥ | havyakavyavahau cobhau saharakṣāśca nāma yaḥ ||
6.d: उत्तरेण तु सूक्तेन श्मशाने कर्म शंसति | पितृदेवासुराणां च अभवन्नग्नयस्त्रयः | हव्यकव्यवहौ चोभौ सहरक्षाश्च नाम यः ||
6.e: But with the following hymn (the seer) proclaims the rite in the burning ground. There were three Agnis belonging (respectively) to the Fathers, x. 17 the Gods, and the Asuras: the two who bear oblations (havya) and food offerings (kavya) and he who is called Saharaksas.

6.s: tatra mainamiti tvetat kavyavāhanasaṃstutiḥ | itarāṇi tu daivasya stutirnāsyāsurasya ca ||
6.d: तत्र मैनमिति त्वेतत् कव्यवाहनसंस्तुतिः | इतराणि तु दैवस्य स्तुतिर्नास्यासुरस्य च ||
6.e: Now with regard to these (tatra) the (hymn) 'Not him' (mainam x. 16) is (in) praise of the bearer of food offerings (kavya). Other (hymns), however, are (in) praise of the divine (Agni), not of this one (connected with the Fathers), nor of the demoniac one (asura).

6.s: abhavanmithunaṃ tvaṣṭuḥ saraṇyūstriśirāḥ saha | sa vai saraṇyūṃ prāyacchat svayameva vivasvate ||
6.d: अभवन्मिथुनं त्वष्टुः सरण्यूस्त्रिशिराः सह | स वै सरण्यूं प्रायच्छत् स्वयमेव विवस्वते ||
6.e: Tvastra had twin children, Saranyu as well as Trisiras. He himself gave Saranyu in marriage to Vivasvat. trisirah saha hm'bfks ( Rg-veda), (0yusa )

6.s: tataḥ saraṇyvāṃ jajñāte yamasyayau vivasvataḥ | tau cāpyubhau yamāveva jyāyāṃstābhyāṃ tu vai yamaḥ ||
6.d: ततः सरण्य्वां जज्ञाते यमस्ययौ विवस्वतः | तौ चाप्युभौ यमावेव ज्यायांस्ताभ्यां तु वै यमः ||
6.e: Then Yama and Yami were begotten on Saranyu by Vivasvat. And these two also were twins, but the elder of the two was Yama.

6.s: .. iti vṛhaddevatāyāṃ ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ ||
6.d: .. इति वृहद्देवतायां षष्ठोऽध्यायः ||

7.s: suṣṭvā bhartuḥ parokṣaṃ tu saraṇyūḥ sadṛśīṃ striyam | nikṣipya mithunaṃ tasyām aśvā bhūtvāpacakrame ||
7.d: सुष्ट्वा भर्तुः परोक्षं तु सरण्यूः सदृशीं स्त्रियम् | निक्षिप्य मिथुनं तस्याम् अश्वा भूत्वापचक्रमे ||
7.e: Now Saranyu having created, in the absence of her husband, a female similar (to herself) and having entrusted to her the pair (of children), turned herself into a mare and departed.

7.s: avijñānādvivasvāṃstu tasyāmajanayanmanum | rājarṣirabhavatso'pi vivasvāniva tejasā ||
7.d: अविज्ञानाद्विवस्वांस्तु तस्यामजनयन्मनुम् | राजर्षिरभवत्सोऽपि विवस्वानिव तेजसा ||
7.e: But Vivasvat, in ignorance (of this ), begot Manu on that (substitute). He (Manu) became a royal seer, like Vivasvat in brilliance. tasyamajanayan m'bfkrns, tasyam prajanayan hd.

7.s: sa vijñāya tvapakrāntāṃ saraṇyūmaśvarūpiṇīm | tvaṣṭrīṃ prati jagāmāśu vājī bhūtvā salakṣaṇaḥ ||
7.d: स विज्ञाय त्वपक्रान्तां सरण्यूमश्वरूपिणीम् | त्वष्ट्रीं प्रति जगामाशु वाजी भूत्वा सलक्षणः ||
7.e: When, however, he (Vivasvat) had become aware that Saranyu had departed in the shape of a mare, he quickly went after the daughter of Tvastr, having turned himself into a horse with similar characteristics (to hers).

7.s: saraṇyūśca vivasvantaṃ viditvā hayarūpiṇam | maithunāyopacakrāma tāṃ ca tatrāruroha saḥ ||
7.d: सरण्यूश्च विवस्वन्तं विदित्वा हयरूपिणम् | मैथुनायोपचक्राम तां च तत्रारुरोह सः ||
7.e: And Saranyu, recognizing Vivasvat in the form of a steed, approached him for sexual intercourse, and he covered her there. saranyusca Am', saranyustam Bn, sarabyustu s, saranyusca s (Atharva-veda).

7.s: tatastayostu vegena śukraṃ tadapatadbhuvi | upājighracca sā tvaśvā tacchukraṃ garbhakāmyayā ||
7.d: ततस्तयोस्तु वेगेन शुक्रं तदपतद्भुवि | उपाजिघ्रच्च सा त्वश्वा तच्छुक्रं गर्भकाम्यया ||
7.e: Then in their agitation the semen fell on the ground. And the mare, through desire of offspring, smelt the semen. vegena MSS. rs, yogena 8 (Atharva-veda).

7.s: āghātamātrācchukrāttu kumārau saṃbabhūvatuḥ | nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca yau stutāvaśvināviti ||
7.d: आघातमात्राच्छुक्रात्तु कुमारौ संबभूवतुः | नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च यौ स्तुतावश्विनाविति ||
7.e: Now from the semen which had just been smelt there came into being two youths, Nasatya and Dasra, who are praised as 'Asvins'. aghratamatracchukrattu rnf (°chu ° f), °matrachakrattu, °macasuklattu h, °matra- sukratu, °matrakukra hai, aghranamatracchukram tat s.

7.s: itihāsamimaṃ yāskaḥ saraṇyūdevate dvṛce | vivasvataśca tvaṣṭuśca tvaṣṭeti saha manyate ||
7.d: इतिहासमिमं यास्कः सरण्यूदेवते द्वृचे | विवस्वतश्च त्वष्टुश्च त्वष्टेति सह मन्यते ||
7.e: Yaska regards this as a story a of Vivasvat and Tvastr together in the couplet 'Tvastr' (tvasta: x. 17. 1, 2) which has Saranyu for its deity. a

7.s: pūṣeti pādau pauṣṇau dvāv āgneyāvuttarau tu yau | syāttṛtīyo'pi vā pauṣṇastisraścānyāḥ parāstu yāḥ ||
7.d: पूषेति पादौ पौष्णौ द्वाव् आग्नेयावुत्तरौ तु यौ | स्यात्तृतीयोऽपि वा पौष्णस्तिस्रश्चान्याः परास्तु याः ||
7.e: The two verses (beginning) Pusan' (pusa: x. 17. 3) are addressed to Pusan, but the two next (3) to Agni; even the third (3) may optionally (va) be addressed to Pusan; and the other three (stanzas) which follow (4-6) are also (addressed to him).

7.s: apāṃ stutistvṛgatraikā tṛcātsārasvatātparā | stutaḥ parokṣaḥ somastu drapsa ityuttare tṛce ||
7.d: अपां स्तुतिस्त्वृगत्रैका तृचात्सारस्वतात्परा | स्तुतः परोक्षः सोमस्तु द्रप्स इत्युत्तरे तृचे ||
7.e: But one (stanza) in this hymn (atra), which follows the triplet addressed to Sarasvati (7-9), is (in) praise of the Waters (10), while in the next triplet, 'The drop' (drapsah: 11-13), Soma is praised indirectly (paroksa).

7.s: abdevatāśīrvādo vā payasvatyuttarā tu yā | catasrastāstutirmṛtyor antye klṛptāśca karmaṇi ||
7.d: अब्देवताशीर्वादो वा पयस्वत्युत्तरा तु या | चतस्रस्तास्तुतिर्मृत्योर् अन्त्ये क्लृप्ताश्च कर्मणि ||
7.e: But the next (stanza), 'Rich in milk' (payasvati: 14)a, has the waters for its deities or is a benediction. The (next) four (stanzas: x. 18. 1-4) are (in) praise of Death and are applicable (klpta) in the funeral (antya) ceremony.

7.s: mṛtaśiṣṭebhya āśāste ime jyogjīvanaṃ punaḥ | imaṃ jīvebhya āśāste tebhyaḥ paridhikarmaṇi ||
7.d: मृतशिष्टेभ्य आशास्ते इमे ज्योग्जीवनं पुनः | इमं जीवेभ्य आशास्ते तेभ्यः परिधिकर्मणि ||
7.e: The (stanza) 'These' (ime: x. 18. 3) prays for long life for those who have escaped death; For the living this' (imam jivebhyah: 4) again prays (for it) for them in the ceremony with the barrier (paridhi)a.

7.s: yathā dhātryuttarā tvāṣṭrī tato yānyā imāstviti | strīṇāmāśiṣamāśāste tayaivāñjanakarmaṇi ||
7.d: यथा धात्र्युत्तरा त्वाष्ट्री ततो यान्या इमास्त्विति | स्त्रीणामाशिषमाशास्ते तयैवाञ्जनकर्मणि ||
7.e: 'As' (yatha: x. 18. 5) is addressed to Dhatr; the next to Tvastr (6), then with another (7), 'These wives' (imah), he (the seer) utters a prayer for the women in the ceremony with collyrium (anjana). tayaivanjanakarmani B, taya paridhikarmani A: the latter reading is probably due to a clerical error repeating the last word of the preceding sloka, which in that case (though occurring in B only) must have been original. The preceding sloka mentions the stanza which refers to the paridhi, the present sloka mentions the one which refers to anjana.This sloka is wanting in

7.s: udīrṣva nārītyanayā mṛtaṃ patnyanurohati | bhrātā kanīyānpretasya nigadya pratiṣedhati ||
7.d: उदीर्ष्व नारीत्यनया मृतं पत्न्यनुरोहति | भ्राता कनीयान्प्रेतस्य निगद्य प्रतिषेधति ||
7.e: With the (stanza) 'Rise up, O woman' (ud irsva nari: x. 18. 8) the wife ascends (the funeral pyre) after her dead (husband). The younger brother of the departed, repeating (the stanza), prohibits (her). x.

7.s: kuryādetatkarma hotā devaro na bhavedyadi | pretānugamanaṃ na syād iti brāhmaṇaśāsanāt ||
7.d: कुर्यादेतत्कर्म होता देवरो न भवेद्यदि | प्रेतानुगमनं न स्याद् इति ब्राह्मणशासनात् ||
7.e: The Hotr ought to perform this rite, should there be no brother-in-law, because Brahmana enjoins that (the widow) should not follow the departed (husband). This sloka is not found in A, but in B and

7.s: varṇānāmitareṣāṃ ca strīdharmo'yaṃ bhavenna vā | śāntyarthaṃ dhanurādāne pretasyarcaṃ dhanurjapet | yasmādetāḥ prayujyante śmaśāne cāntyakarmaṇi ||
7.d: वर्णानामितरेषां च स्त्रीधर्मोऽयं भवेन्न वा | शान्त्यर्थं धनुरादाने प्रेतस्यर्चं धनुर्जपेत् | यस्मादेताः प्रयुज्यन्ते श्मशाने चान्त्यकर्मणि ||
7.e: This law regarding women may or may not apply to the other castes. In taking the bow (from the hand) of the departed man, one should mutter (the stanza) The bow' (dhanuh: x. 18. 9) a for the sake of averting evil. And because these (stanzas) are employed on the burning ground at the funeral ceremony, The first line of 15 is found in B and

7.s: tasmādvadettṛcasvāsya devatāṃ mṛtyumeva tu | mantreṣu hyanirukteṣu devatāṃ karmato vadet ||
7.d: तस्माद्वदेत्तृचस्वास्य देवतां मृत्युमेव तु | मन्त्रेषु ह्यनिरुक्तेषु देवतां कर्मतो वदेत् ||

7.s: mantreṣu hyanirukteṣu devatāṃ karmato vadet || mantrataḥ karmataścaiva prajāpatirasaṃbhave | parāścatasro yāstvatra upa sarpeti pārthivī ||
7.d: मन्त्रेषु ह्यनिरुक्तेषु देवतां कर्मतो वदेत् || मन्त्रतः कर्मतश्चैव प्रजापतिरसंभवे | पराश्चतस्रो यास्त्वत्र उप सर्पेति पार्थिवी ||
7.e: When there is lack (of a deity) from the (evidence of the) formula and the ceremony as well, Prajapati is (the deity). Now as to the following four (stanzas: x. 18. 10-13) here, 'Approach' (upa sarpa: 10) is addressed to the Earth.

7.s: tāsāṃ prayogaḥ pretasya asthisaṃcayakarmaṇi | pratīcīne yathāhāni apahṛtyetarāṇi tu ||
7.d: तासां प्रयोगः प्रेतस्य अस्थिसंचयकर्मणि | प्रतीचीने यथाहानि अपहृत्येतराणि तु ||
7.e: Their application is in the ceremony of collecting the bones a of the departed. Now with the last (stanza) 'In the future' (praticine: x. 18. 14) he (the seer) expresses a prayer (in saying), 'As having taken away (my) other days, the Fathers placed (me) in (past) days, B (so) they also restored me, about to die (prayantam), to life in days to come'. B is: 18 cd follows the reading of Am1 (for,

7.s: ahaḥsu pitaro dadhur ityāśāste'ntyayāśiṣaḥ | ahaḥ svāgāmiṣu ca māṃ prayantaṃ samajīvayan ||
7.d: अहःसु पितरो दधुर् इत्याशास्तेऽन्त्ययाशिषः | अहः स्वागामिषु च मां प्रयन्तं समजीवयन् ||

7.s: ni vartadhvamitīdaṃ tu gavāṃ kecidapāṃ viduḥ | ardharcaḥ prathamāyāstu agnīṣomīya uttaraḥ ||
7.d: नि वर्तध्वमितीदं तु गवां केचिदपां विदुः | अर्धर्चः प्रथमायास्तु अग्नीषोमीय उत्तरः ||
7.e: Now the (hymn) Turn back' (ni vartadhvam: x. 19) is (in praise) of Cows; some regard it as (in praise) of the Waters. The latter hemistich of the first (stanza: 1°) is, however, addressed to Agni-Soma.

7.s: aindrī ṣaṣṭhī dvitīyāyām ubhau devau nipātitau | daśākṣaraṃ tu śāntyarthaṃ mānasaṃ sūktamucyate ||
7.d: ऐन्द्री षष्ठी द्वितीयायाम् उभौ देवौ निपातितौ | दशाक्षरं तु शान्त्यर्थं मानसं सूक्तमुच्यते ||
7.e: The sixth (stanza) is addressed to Indra (x. 19. 6), while in the second both the gods a are incidentally mentioned (2). Now the hymn which contains a line of ten syllables (x. 20. 1) is described as intended to avert evil (and) as connected with mind (manasa). suktamucyate Am', suktamuttaram B. a 'Both the gods' (ubhau devau) is rather vague: the two mentioned in the second stanza are Indra and Agni. The Sarvanukramani makes no reference to the deities of Rg-veda x. 19. 2 and 6. Meyer, Rgvidhana, p. xxviii, thinks this line is here regarded This hymn begins with a single verse instead of a stanza: as a whole hymn. b bhadram no api vataya manah. The Sarvanukramani remarks: adya ekapada, pada eva va santyarthah. On this pada cp. Oldenberg, Prolegomena, p. 511. 21°=Rgvidhana iii. 8. 6ª; cp. the whole sloka there: dasaksaram tu Santyartham bhadram na iti samsmaret; nityam japec chucir bhutva: manasam vindate sukham.

7.s: trīṇyaindrāṇi kuhetyatra āgneyābhyāṃ parāṇi tu | tṛco'trāstyāśvinastveka aindrāṇāmuttame yuvam ||
7.d: त्रीण्यैन्द्राणि कुहेत्यत्र आग्नेयाभ्यां पराणि तु | तृचोऽत्रास्त्याश्विनस्त्वेक ऐन्द्राणामुत्तमे युवम् ||
7.e: Now here after two hymns addressed to Agni (x. 20, 21) there follow three addressed to Indra (beginning) 'Where?' (kuha: x. 22-24). Now in the last of the hymns to Indra there is one triplet 'Ye two' (yuvam: x. 24. 4-6) addressed to the Asvins.

7.s: bhadraṃ saumyaṃ pra hi pauṣṇaṃ trīṇyaindrāṇi parāṇyasat | teṣāmādyena mattaḥ san svāni karmāṇi śaṃsati ||
7.d: भद्रं सौम्यं प्र हि पौष्णं त्रीण्यैन्द्राणि पराण्यसत् | तेषामाद्येन मत्तः सन् स्वानि कर्माणि शंसति ||
7.e: 'Happy' (bhadram: x. 25) is addressed to Soma; 'Forth indeed' (pra hi: x. 26) is addressed to Pusan. The three following (beginning) 'It shall be' (asat: x. 27-29) are addressed to Indra: with the first (27) of these (Indra), being exhilarated, proclaims his deeds; II.

7.s: yathā carati bhūteṣu yathā varṣati pāti ca || sūkte tadasminnaṣṭābhir ṛgbhiruktamabhūrviti ||
7.d: यथा चरति भूतेषु यथा वर्षति पाति च || सूक्ते तदस्मिन्नष्टाभिर् ऋग्भिरुक्तमभूर्विति ||

7.s: sapteti maruta stauti stauti vajramṛguttarā | agnimindraṃ ca somaṃ ca pīvānaṃ meṣamarcati .. ||
7.d: सप्तेति मरुत स्तौति स्तौति वज्रमृगुत्तरा | अग्निमिन्द्रं च सोमं च पीवानं मेषमर्चति .. ||
7.e: (The stanza) 'Seven' (sapta: x. 27. 15) praises the Maruts, the next stanza (16) praises the Bolt; (the stanza) 'The fatted ram' (pivanam mesam: 17) adores Agni, Indra and Soma:

7.s: pūrvo'rdharco'parastasyāḥ parjanyaṃ vāyunā saha | vi krośanāsa ityagnim uttarā sūryameva tu ||
7.d: पूर्वोऽर्धर्चोऽपरस्तस्याः पर्जन्यं वायुना सह | वि क्रोशनास इत्यग्निम् उत्तरा सूर्यमेव तु ||
7.e: (that is) its first hemistich (does so: 17 ab), while its second one (adores) Parjanya with Vayu (17 cd). 'Crying aloud' (vi kro- sanasah: 18) (praises) Agni, but the next (stanza) Surya (19). rdharco'paras B, rdharcottarasa Am'.

7.s: etau me'yaṃ ya ityete stutiścaivendravajrayoḥ | vṛkṣevṛkṣe dhanuścendraṃ devānāmiti tu trayaḥ ||
7.d: एतौ मेऽयं य इत्येते स्तुतिश्चैवेन्द्रवज्रयोः | वृक्षेवृक्षे धनुश्चेन्द्रं देवानामिति तु त्रयः ||
7.e: 'These two of mine' (etau me: x. 27. 20) and 'This which' (ayam yah: 21)-these two (stanzas) are (in) praise of Indra and the Bolt; and 'To every tree' (vrkse-vrkse: 22) (praises) the Bow of Indra. But (in) 'Of the Gods' (devanam: 23) the three 27 ab follows the reading of

7.s: śītoṣṇavarṣadātāraḥ parjanyānilabhāskarāḥ | antye sūryonilau cobhau stūyete ca pade saha ||
7.d: शीतोष्णवर्षदातारः पर्जन्यानिलभास्कराः | अन्त्ये सूर्योनिलौ चोभौ स्तूयेते च पदे सह ||

7.s: sā te jīvāturityasyām indro vā sūrya eva vā | viśvo anyastu saṃvāda ṛṣeḥ śakrasya caiva hi ||
7.d: सा ते जीवातुरित्यस्याम् इन्द्रो वा सूर्य एव वा | विश्वो अन्यस्तु संवाद ऋषेः शक्रस्य चैव हि ||
7.e: In the (stanza) 'This is thy life' (sa te jivatuh: 24) either Indra or Surya (is praised). But 'Every other' (visvo hy anyah: x. 28) is a dialogue of the seer and of Sakra (Indra).

7.s: yugmāḥ śakrasya vijñeyā vasukrasyetarā ṛcaḥ | snuṣendrasyāgatāndevān dṛṣṭvā śakramanāgatam ||
7.d: युग्माः शक्रस्य विज्ञेया वसुक्रस्येतरा ऋचः | स्नुषेन्द्रस्यागतान्देवान् दृष्ट्वा शक्रमनागतम् ||
7.e: The even (stanzas) are to be recognized as Sakra's, the other stanzas as Vasukra's. B The daughter-in-law of Indra, seeing the gods had come, but Sakra had not come 3098 follows the reading of B; the reading of Am1 is: yugma eva tu sakrasya ayugma eva tu

7.s: yajñaṃ parokṣavatprāha śvaśuro nāgato mama | yadyāgacched bhakṣayetsa dhānāḥ somaṃ pibedapi ||
7.d: यज्ञं परोक्षवत्प्राह श्वशुरो नागतो मम | यद्यागच्छेद् भक्षयेत्स धानाः सोमं पिबेदपि ||

7.s: iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā tatkṣaṇādetya vajradhṛk | tiṣṭhanvedyāmuttarasyām uccairāha sa roruvat ||
7.d: इति तस्या वचः श्रुत्वा तत्क्षणादेत्य वज्रधृक् | तिष्ठन्वेद्यामुत्तरस्याम् उच्चैराह स रोरुवत् ||
7.e: The Bolt-bearer on hearing this speech of hers, came that very moment, and standing on the northern altar (uttara vedi), said aloud: 'He bellowing loud' (sa roruvat: x. 28. 2). r.

7.s: tṛtīyayā caturthyā ca pra devatretyapāṃ stutau | apāṃnapādityanena nāmnāgnirmadhyama stutaḥ ||
7.d: तृतीयया चतुर्थ्या च प्र देवत्रेत्यपां स्तुतौ | अपांनपादित्यनेन नाम्नाग्निर्मध्यम स्तुतः ||
7.e: In the praise of Waters (beginning) 'Forth to the gods' (pra devatra: x. 30) the Middle Agni is praised by the name of 260 "Child of Waters' (apam napat) with the third and the fourth (stanza).

7.s: eti yadvaiśvadevaṃ tu tasya pretyaindramuttaram | vaiśvadevī pra metyekā saṃ metyendro dvṛcaḥ paraḥ ||
7.d: एति यद्वैश्वदेवं तु तस्य प्रेत्यैन्द्रमुत्तरम् | वैश्वदेवी प्र मेत्येका सं मेत्येन्द्रो द्वृचः परः ||
7.e: Now (the hymn) which (begins) Hither' (a: x. 31) is addressed to the All-gods; the one next to that, 'Forth' (pra: x. 32), is addressed to Indra. One (stanza) 'Onward me' (pra ma x. 33. 1) is addressed to the All-gods; the following couplet 'Together me' (sam ma: 2, 3) is addressed to Indra.

7.s: kuruśravaṇamarcataḥ pare dve trāsadasyavam | mṛte mitrātithau rājñi tannapātamṛṣiḥ paraiḥ ||
7.d: कुरुश्रवणमर्चतः परे द्वे त्रासदस्यवम् | मृते मित्रातिथौ राज्ञि तन्नपातमृषिः परैः ||
7.e: Cp. Rg-veda x. 33. 7 upamasravo napan mitratither ihi. See also Sarvanukramani: mrte mitralithau rajni.. rsir upamasravasam putram asya (kurusravanasya) vyasokayat.

7.s: upamaśravasaṃ yasya caturbhiḥ sa vyaśokayat | prāvepā iti sūktaṃ yat tadakṣastutirucyate ||
7.d: उपमश्रवसं यस्य चतुर्भिः स व्यशोकयत् | प्रावेपा इति सूक्तं यत् तदक्षस्तुतिरुच्यते ||

7.s: atrākṣāndvādaśī stauti navamyādyā ca saptamī | trayodaśī kṛṣiṃ stauti kitavaṃ cānuśāsati | akṣāṃstu śeṣā nindanti abudhraṃ vaiśvadevate ||
7.d: अत्राक्षान्द्वादशी स्तौति नवम्याद्या च सप्तमी | त्रयोदशी कृषिं स्तौति कितवं चानुशासति | अक्षांस्तु शेषा निन्दन्ति अबुध्रं वैश्वदेवते ||
7.e: Here the twelfth (stanza) praises the Dice, the ninth, the first, and the seventh (x. 34. 1, 7, 9, 12). A The thirteenth a praises tillage (13) and admonishes the gambler. But the remaining (stanzas) blame the Dice. Two (hymns x. 44 beginning) 'They are awake' (abudhram: x. 35, 36) are addressed to the All-gods.

7.s: sāvitrameke manyante maho agne stavaṃ param | ācāryāḥ śaunako yāsko gālavaścottamāmṛcam ||
7.d: सावित्रमेके मन्यन्ते महो अग्ने स्तवं परम् | आचार्याः शौनको यास्को गालवश्चोत्तमामृचम् ||
7.e: Some consider the praise at the end (para), 'Of the great Agni' (maho agneh: x. 36. 12-14), to be addressed to Savitr; the teachers Saunaka, Yaska, and Galava (consider) the last (14) stanza (to be such). This sloka is not found in A, but in B and

7.s: namaḥ sauryamaindramasmin saurye ṣaṣṭyā tu yā stutāḥ | nipātinyastāḥ sūktānte vaiśvadevo'tra tu dvṛcaḥ ||
7.d: नमः सौर्यमैन्द्रमस्मिन् सौर्ये षष्ट्या तु या स्तुताः | निपातिन्यस्ताः सूक्तान्ते वैश्वदेवोऽत्र तु द्वृचः ||
7.e: 'Obeisance' (namah: x. 37) is addressed to Surya, 'In this' (asmin x. 38) to Indra. But (the deities) who are praised in the sixth (stanza) of the hymn to Surya (x. 37. 6) are incidental; at the end of this (atra) hymn there is a couplet addressed to the All-gods (x. 37. II, 12).

7.s: āśvināni tu yastrīṇi aindrāṇyasteva su pra ca | aindrāṇāmuttamāyāstu stuto'rdharca bṛhaspatiḥ ||
7.d: आश्विनानि तु यस्त्रीणि ऐन्द्राण्यस्तेव सु प्र च | ऐन्द्राणामुत्तमायास्तु स्तुतोऽर्धर्च बृहस्पतिः ||
7.e: Now there are three hymns addressed to the Asvins (beginning) Which' (yah: x. 39-41), and there are (three) addressed to Indra (beginning) 'As the archer far' (asteva su 262 pra- x. 42-44), but in a hemistich (116) of the last stanza of the Indra hymns (42-44) Brhaspati b is praised.

7.s: pare divasparyāgneye prathamasyottamena tu | dyāvāpṛthivyau viśve ca paccho'rdharccena saṃstutāḥ ||
7.d: परे दिवस्पर्याग्नेये प्रथमस्योत्तमेन तु | द्यावापृथिव्यौ विश्वे च पच्छोऽर्धर्च्चेन संस्तुताः ||
7.e: The two following (hymns), 'From heaven' (divas pari: x. 45, 46), are addressed to Agni, but with the last hemistich of the former (x. 45. 12 cd) Heaven and Earth (12) and the All- (gods: 12) are praised in the respective verses (pacchah). •ttamena tu B, °tama tu ya Am'.

7.s: āsītkākṣīvatī ghoṣā pāparogeṇa durbhagā | uvāsa ṣaṣṭi varṣāṇi pitureva gṛhe purā ||
7.d: आसीत्काक्षीवती घोषा पापरोगेण दुर्भगा | उवास षष्टि वर्षाणि पितुरेव गृहे पुरा ||

7.s: ātasthe mahatīṃ cintāṃ na putro na patirmama | jarāṃ prāptāṃ mudhātasmāt prapadye'haṃ śubhaspatī ||
7.d: आतस्थे महतीं चिन्तां न पुत्रो न पतिर्मम | जरां प्राप्तां मुधातस्मात् प्रपद्येऽहं शुभस्पती ||
7.e: She fell into great grief (thinking), 'Without son or husband I have reached old age in vain; I (will) therefore resort to the Lords of Light (subhaspati). mahatim cintam fm'bn, mahati cinta, mahi cimta .

7.s: yathaitau māmakastāta ārādhyāvāpa yauvanam | āyurārogyamaiśvaryaṃ sarvabhūtahatthe viṣam ||
7.d: यथैतौ मामकस्तात आराध्यावाप यौवनम् | आयुरारोग्यमैश्वर्यं सर्वभूतहत्थे विषम् ||
7.e: Since my father, by propitiating them, obtained youth, long life, health, power, poison for slaying all

7.s: rūpavatāṃ ca saubhāgyam ahaṃ tasya sutā yadi | samāpi mantrāḥ prāduḥsyur yaistoṣyete mayāśvinau ||
7.d: रूपवतां च सौभाग्यम् अहं तस्य सुता यदि | समापि मन्त्राः प्रादुःस्युर् यैस्तोष्येते मयाश्विनौ ||
7.e: I, his daughter, (would obtain) beauty and good fortune, if to me also were revealed formulas in which the Asvins shall be praised & by me.' rupavattam ca rn, rupavantam ca 1, rupatta caiva f, rupata caiva m k.

7.s: cintayantīti sūkte dve yo vāṃ pari dadarśa sā | stutau tāvaśvinau devau prītau tasyā bhagāntaram ||
7.d: चिन्तयन्तीति सूक्ते द्वे यो वां परि ददर्श सा | स्तुतौ तावश्विनौ देवौ प्रीतौ तस्या भगान्तरम् ||
7.e: As she reffected thus, she saw the two hymns 'Your encircling' (yo vama pari-: x. 39, 40). The two divine ASvins being praised, were pleased. Entering her organ (bhaga) they made her ageless, free from disease, and beautiful (subhaga). They gave her a husband and the sage Suhastya as a son. 46.

7.s: praviśya vijarārogāṃ subhagāṃ cakratuśca tau | bhartāraṃ dadatustasyai suhastyaṃ ca sutaṃ munim ||
7.d: प्रविश्य विजरारोगां सुभगां चक्रतुश्च तौ | भर्तारं ददतुस्तस्यै सुहस्त्यं च सुतं मुनिम् ||

7.s: dadatustatsuparṇābhyāṃ yannāsatyeti kīrtyate | kākṣīvatyai ca ghoṣāyai na tasyāmājuro'nayā ||
7.d: ददतुस्तत्सुपर्णाभ्यां यन्नासत्येति कीर्त्यते | काक्षीवत्यै च घोषायै न तस्यामाजुरोऽनया ||
7.e: What the ' Nasatyas' by means of their two winged steeds (suparnabhyam) & gave to Ghosa, daughter of Kaksivat, is proclaimed by the (stanzas), ' Not of that' (na tasya: x. 40. 11) (and) - Of her that grows old at home' (amajurah: x. 39.3).

7.s: prājāpatyāsurī tvāsīd vikuṇṭhā nāma nāmataḥ | sechantīndrasamaṃ putraṃ tepe'tha sumahattapaḥ ||
7.d: प्राजापत्यासुरी त्वासीद् विकुण्ठा नाम नामतः | सेछन्तीन्द्रसमं पुत्रं तेपेऽथ सुमहत्तपः ||
7.e: There was an Asuri, daughter of Prajapati, Vikuntha by name. She, desiring a son like Indra, performed very severe austerities

7.s: sā prajāpatitaḥ kārmāṃllebhe'tha vividhān varān | tasyāṃ cendraḥ svayaṃ jajñe jiyāṃsurdaityadānavān ||
7.d: सा प्रजापतितः कार्मांल्लेभेऽथ विविधान् वरान् | तस्यां चेन्द्रः स्वयं जज्ञे जियांसुर्दैत्यदानवान् ||
7.e: She then obtained from Prajapati her desires (in the form of) various boons. And Indra himself was born of her, as he wished to slay the Daityas and Danavas.

7.s: ekadā dānavaiḥ sārdhaṃ samare samasajyata | jaghāna teṣāṃ navatīr nava sapta ca saptakān ||
7.d: एकदा दानवैः सार्धं समरे समसज्यत | जघान तेषां नवतीर् नव सप्त च सप्तकान् ||
7.e: Once he was engaged in battle with the Danavas. Of them he slew nine nineties a and seven groups of seven.

7.s: bhittvā svabāhuvīryeṇa haimaraupyāyasīḥ purīḥ | hatvā sarvān yathāsthānaṃ pṛthivyādivyavasthitān ||
7.d: भित्त्वा स्वबाहुवीर्येण हैमरौप्यायसीः पुरीः | हत्वा सर्वान् यथास्थानं पृथिव्यादिव्यवस्थितान् ||
7.e: Having shattered with the might of his arm their citadels of gold, silver, and iron, (and) having slain all (of them) in their respective spheres (yathasthanam), as arrayed on earth and in the other (two worlds). x.

7.s: pṛthivyāṃ kālakeyāṃśca paulomāṃścaiva dhanvinaḥ | tāṃśca vyutsādayāmāsa prahlādatanayāndivi ||
7.d: पृथिव्यां कालकेयांश्च पौलोमांश्चैव धन्विनः | तांश्च व्युत्सादयामास प्रह्लादतनयान्दिवि ||
7.e: On earth he exterminated both the Kalakeyas and the race of Puloma, the archers, and in heaven the notorious (tan) offspring of Prahlada.

7.s: rājyaṃ prāpya sa daityeṣu svena vīryeṇa darpitaḥ | devānbādhitumārebhe mohito'suramāyayā ||
7.d: राज्यं प्राप्य स दैत्येषु स्वेन वीर्येण दर्पितः | देवान्बाधितुमारेभे मोहितोऽसुरमायया ||
7.e: Having obtained sovereignty among the Daityas (and) puffed up with pride by reason of his might, he began to harass the gods, being infatuated by the craft of the Asuras.

7.s: bādhyamānāstu tenāpi asureṇāmitaujasā | upādhāvannṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ tatprabodhāya saptagum ||
7.d: बाध्यमानास्तु तेनापि असुरेणामितौजसा | उपाधावन्नृषिश्रेष्ठं तत्प्रबोधाय सप्तगुम् ||
7.e: Now while they were being harassed by that same Asura of unlimited power, they fled for succour to Saptagu, most excellent of seers, in order that (the latter) should admonish him (Indra).

7.s: ṛṣistu saptagurnāma tasyāsītsupriyaḥ sakhā | sa cainamabhituṣṭāva jagṛbhmeti kare spṛśan ||
7.d: ऋषिस्तु सप्तगुर्नाम तस्यासीत्सुप्रियः सखा | स चैनमभितुष्टाव जगृभ्मेति करे स्पृशन् ||
7.e: Now the seer called Saptagu was a dear friend of his, and (so) he praised him with the (hymn), 'We have grasped' (jagrbhma: x. 47), as he took him by the hand. sa

7.s: tataḥ sa buddhvā cātmānaṃ saptagustutiharṣitaḥ | ātmānameva tuṣṭāva ahaṃ bhuvamiti tribhiḥ ||
7.d: ततः स बुद्ध्वा चात्मानं सप्तगुस्तुतिहर्षितः | आत्मानमेव तुष्टाव अहं भुवमिति त्रिभिः ||
7.e: Then he coming to (buddhva) himself (and) rejoiced at the praise of Saptagu, praised himself with the three (hymns) 'I was' (aham bhuvam: x.

7.s: kīrtayansvāni karmāṇi yāni sma kṛtavānpurā | yathākarocca vaidehaṃ vyaṃsaṃ somapatiṃ nṛpam ||
7.d: कीर्तयन्स्वानि कर्माणि यानि स्म कृतवान्पुरा | यथाकरोच्च वैदेहं व्यंसं सोमपतिं नृपम् ||

7.s: vasiṣṭhaśāpādabhavad vaideho nṛpatiḥ purā | indraprasādādīje ca sattraiḥ sārasvatādibhiḥ ||
7.d: वसिष्ठशापादभवद् वैदेहो नृपतिः पुरा | इन्द्रप्रसादादीजे च सत्त्रैः सारस्वतादिभिः ||

7.s: prabhūtāṃ śaktimattāṃ ca śatrūṇāmapyapākriyām | nṛṣu sarveṣu caiśvaryaṃ prabhutvaṃ bhuvaneṣu ca | pra vo maha iti tvasyām ātmano vīryamakṣayam ||
7.d: प्रभूतां शक्तिमत्तां च शत्रूणामप्यपाक्रियाम् | नृषु सर्वेषु चैश्वर्यं प्रभुत्वं भुवनेषु च | प्र वो मह इति त्वस्याम् आत्मनो वीर्यमक्षयम् ||
7.e: The curse of Vasistha, it appears, relegated Vyamsa to a remote Eastern region (Tirhut) beyond the pale of orthodox Brahmanism, but the favour of Indra afterwards enabled him to perform sacrifices on the Sarasvati and so to become a lord of Soma,' like himself (somapati being an epithet of Indra). B 60. and (praising) his great power and his injury to foes, and his sovereignty among all men and his lordship in the worlds; but in the (stanza) Forth to your great' (pra vo mahe: x. 50. 1) his own imperishable might.

7.s: vaiśvānare gṛhapatau yaviṣṭhe'gnau ca pāvake | vaṣaṭkāreṇa vṛkṇeṣu bhrātṛṣvagnau sahaḥsute ||
7.d: वैश्वानरे गृहपतौ यविष्ठेऽग्नौ च पावके | वषट्कारेण वृक्णेषु भ्रातृष्वग्नौ सहःसुते ||

7.s: apacakrāma devebhyaḥ saucīko'gniriti śrutiḥ | sa praviśadapakramya ṛtūnapo vanaspatīn ||
7.d: अपचक्राम देवेभ्यः सौचीकोऽग्निरिति श्रुतिः | स प्रविशदपक्रम्य ऋतूनपो वनस्पतीन् ||
7.e: Agni Saucika departed from the gods, so Vedic text (relates). He on departing entered the seasons, the waters, (and) the trees.

7.s: tato'surāḥ prādurāsan naṣṭe'gnau havyavāhane | te'gnimevānvavaikṣanta devā hatvāsurānyudhi ||
7.d: ततोऽसुराः प्रादुरासन् नष्टेऽग्नौ हव्यवाहने | तेऽग्निमेवान्ववैक्षन्त देवा हत्वासुरान्युधि ||
7.e: Then the Asuras appeared, when Agni the oblation-bearer had vanished. The gods, having slain the Asuras in fight, looked about in quest of Agni.

7.s: taṃ tu dūrādyamaścaiva varuṇaścānvapaśyatām | ubhāvenaṃ samādāya devānevābhijagmatuḥ ||
7.d: तं तु दूराद्यमश्चैव वरुणश्चान्वपश्यताम् | उभावेनं समादाय देवानेवाभिजग्मतुः ||
7.e: Now Yama and Varuna a espied him from afar. Both of them, taking him with them, went to the gods.

7.s: dṛṣṭvā devāstvenamūcur agne havyāni no vaha | varān gṛhāṇa cāsmattaś citrabhāno bhajasva naḥ | devayānān sugān pathaḥ kuruṣva sumanāḥ svayam ||
7.d: दृष्ट्वा देवास्त्वेनमूचुर् अग्ने हव्यानि नो वह | वरान् गृहाण चास्मत्तश् चित्रभानो भजस्व नः | देवयानान् सुगान् पथः कुरुष्व सुमनाः स्वयम् ||
7.e: On seeing him the gods said : '0 Agni, bear our oblations, and accept boons & from us; do thou, O brilliantly shining one, attend upon us; B do thou thyself graciously make the paths trodden by the gods easy to traverse.'

7.s: pratyuvācātha tānagni viśve devā yadūca mām | tatkariṣye juṣantāṃ tu hotraṃ pañca janā mama ||
7.d: प्रत्युवाचाथ तानग्नि विश्वे देवा यदूच माम् | तत्करिष्ये जुषन्तां तु होत्रं पञ्च जना मम ||
7.e: Agni then answered them : ' What all ye gods have said to me I will do; but let the five races enjoy my priesthood's

7.s: śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇāścāgnir ete pañca janāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
7.d: शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः | उत्तरो दक्षिणाश्चाग्निर् एते पञ्च जनाः स्मृताः ||

7.s: manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gandharvoragarākṣasāḥ | gandharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ||
7.d: मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः | गन्धर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ||
7.e: Men, Fathers, Gods, Gandharvas, Serpents, Demons & ; B (or) Gandharvas, Fathers, Gods, Asuras, Yaksas (and) Demons : x.

7.s: yāskaupamanyavāvetān āhatuḥ pañca vai janān | niṣādapañcamān varṇān manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ||
7.d: यास्कौपमन्यवावेतान् आहतुः पञ्च वै जनान् | निषादपञ्चमान् वर्णान् मन्यते शाकटायनः ||
7.e: Yaska a and Aupamanyava state these to be the five races. Sakatayana thinks they are the (four) castes with the Nisadas as a fifth.

7.s: ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate | hotādhvaryustathodgātā brahmā ceti vadanti tān ||
7.d: ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते | होताध्वर्युस्तथोद्गाता ब्रह्मा चेति वदन्ति तान् ||
7.e: Sakapuni, however, thinks they are the (four) priests (rtvij) and the institutor of the sacrifice (yajamana). B Those (priests) they call Hotr,' 'Adhvaryu,' 'Udgatr,' and 'Brahman.'

7.s: cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ | gandharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā ||
7.d: चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः | गन्धर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा ||
7.e: Eye, ear, mind, speech, and breath, say the theosophists (atmavadin). They are stated to be Gandharvas and Apsarases, Gods, Men, Fathers, and Serpents in the sacred text of the Aitareya Brahmanab_ 'and (continued Agni) whatever other terrestrial creatures (prthivijatah) and other divine beings (devah) there are that receive worship (yajniyah). Rg-veda x. 51-] 1 BRHADDEVATA vii. 73- [270 72.

7.s: sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyante hyaitareyake | ye cānye pṛthivījātā devāścānye'tha yajñiyāḥ ||
7.d: सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयन्ते ह्यैतरेयके | ये चान्ये पृथिवीजाता देवाश्चान्येऽथ यज्ञियाः ||

7.s: āyurastu ca me dīrghaṃ havīṃṣi vividhāni ca | ariṣṭiḥ pūrvajānāṃ ca bhrātṛṇāmadhvare'dhvare ||
7.d: आयुरस्तु च मे दीर्घं हवींषि विविधानि च | अरिष्टिः पूर्वजानां च भ्रातृणामध्वरेऽध्वरे ||
7.e: And let me have long life, and various oblations, and let my elder brothers enjoy safety at every sacrifice;

7.s: prayājāścānuyājāśca ghṛtaṃ some ca yaḥ paśuḥ | maddaivatyāni vai santu yajño maddevato'stu ca ||
7.d: प्रयाजाश्चानुयाजाश्च घृतं सोमे च यः पशुः | मद्दैवत्यानि वै सन्तु यज्ञो मद्देवतोऽस्तु च ||

7.s: tavāgne yajña ityetat pratyādhi sviṣṭakṛcca saḥ | yasya trīṇi sahasrāṇi nava trīṇi śatāni ca ||
7.d: तवाग्ने यज्ञ इत्येतत् प्रत्याधि स्विष्टकृच्च सः | यस्य त्रीणि सहस्राणि नव त्रीणि शतानि च ||
7.e: This was accorded (pratyardhi) with (the words) 'Thine, O Agni, the sacrifice' (tavagne yajnah: x. 51. 9); and he (became) Svistakrt (offering right sacrifice), to whom the three thousand, three hundred and nine

7.s: triṃśaccaiva tu devānāṃ sarvāmeva varāndaduḥ | tato'gniḥ sumanāḥ prīto viśvedevaiḥ puraskṛtaḥ ||
7.d: त्रिंशच्चैव तु देवानां सर्वामेव वरान्ददुः | ततोऽग्निः सुमनाः प्रीतो विश्वेदेवैः पुरस्कृतः ||

7.s: vidhūyāṅgāni yajñeṣu cakre hotramatandritaḥ | bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ proto divyātmā havyavāhanaḥ ||
7.d: विधूयाङ्गानि यज्ञेषु चक्रे होत्रमतन्द्रितः | भ्रातृभिः सहितः प्रोतो दिव्यात्मा हव्यवाहनः ||

7.s: tasyāsthi devadārvāsīn medo māṃsaṃ ca gugguluḥ | sugandhitejanaṃ snāyu śukraṃ rajatakāñcane ||
7.d: तस्यास्थि देवदार्वासीन् मेदो मांसं च गुग्गुलुः | सुगन्धितेजनं स्नायु शुक्रं रजतकाञ्चने ||
7.e: His bone became a the Devadaru tree; his fat and flesh, bdellium; his sinew, fragrant Tejana grass; his semen, silver and gold;

7.s: romāṇi kāśāḥ keśāstu kṛśāḥ kūrmā nakhāni ca | antrāṇi caivāpyavakā majjā sikataśarkarāḥ ||
7.d: रोमाणि काशाः केशास्तु कृशाः कूर्मा नखानि च | अन्त्राणि चैवाप्यवका मज्जा सिकतशर्कराः ||

7.s: asṛk pittaṃ ca vividhā dhātavo gairikādayaḥ | evamagniśca devāśca sūktairmahaditi tribhiḥ ||
7.d: असृक् पित्तं च विविधा धातवो गैरिकादयः | एवमग्निश्च देवाश्च सूक्तैर्महदिति त्रिभिः ||

7.s: samūdire pare tvasmād aindre sūkte tu tāṃ su te | vidhuṃ dadrāṇamityasyāṃ sūryācandramasau stutau ||
7.d: समूदिरे परे त्वस्माद् ऐन्द्रे सूक्ते तु तां सु ते | विधुं दद्राणमित्यस्यां सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ स्तुतौ ||

7.s: prāṇavaccātmavaccāpi stutirapyatra dṛśyate | idaṃ dve vaiśvadeve ca dvitīye manasastṛcaḥ ||
7.d: प्राणवच्चात्मवच्चापि स्तुतिरप्यत्र दृश्यते | इदं द्वे वैश्वदेवे च द्वितीये मनसस्तृचः ||
7.e: The praise here also appears as of Breath and of Soul. The two (hymns) 'This' (idam: x. 56, 57) are addressed to the Allgods. In the second (57) b there is a triplet (3-5) to Mind (manas).

7.s: prathamaindro dvitīyāgneyy antyā tatsomadevatā | api stauti pitṝnetad ārtvijaṃ yattaduttaram ||
7.d: प्रथमैन्द्रो द्वितीयाग्नेय्य् अन्त्या तत्सोमदेवता | अपि स्तौति पितॄनेतद् आर्त्विजं यत्तदुत्तरम् ||
7.e: The first (stanza) is addressed to Indra (x. 57. 1), the second to Agni (2), the last (6) has the Soma (mentioned) in it (tat) for its deity. B This (hymn) praises the Fathers a also (and) should be recited (in that sense) by priests (artvija). The hymn (beginning) Which' (yat x. 58), coming next after that,

7.s: sūktamākhyānasaṃyuktaṃ vaktukāmasya me śṛṇu | saṃmohānnaṣṭasaṃjñasya śatruṇābhihatasya tu ||
7.d: सूक्तमाख्यानसंयुक्तं वक्तुकामस्य मे शृणु | संमोहान्नष्टसंज्ञस्य शत्रुणाभिहतस्य तु ||

7.s: jīvāvṛttiḥ subandhorvā yadi vā manasa stavaḥ | rājāsamātiraikṣvākū rathaproṣṭhaḥ purohitān ||
7.d: जीवावृत्तिः सुबन्धोर्वा यदि वा मनस स्तवः | राजासमातिरैक्ष्वाकू रथप्रोष्ठः पुरोहितान् ||
7.e: Subandhu's life is (here) recalled (jivavrtti) or (the hymn) is (in) praise of Mind (manas). King Asamati, of the race of Iksvaku, the Rathaprosthac, cast off (vyudasya) his domestic

7.s: vyudasya bandhuprabhṛtīn dvaipadā ye'trimaṇḍale | dvau kirātākulī nāma tato māyāvinau dvijau ||
7.d: व्युदस्य बन्धुप्रभृतीन् द्वैपदा येऽत्रिमण्डले | द्वौ किराताकुली नाम ततो मायाविनौ द्विजौ ||
7.e: Bandhu and the rest who in the Mandala of the Atris (v. 24) are seers of Dvipadas (dvaipadah).

7.s: asamātiḥ puro'dhatta variṣṭhau tau hi manyate | tau kapotau dvijau bhūtvā gatvā gopāyanānabhi ||
7.d: असमातिः पुरोऽधत्त वरिष्ठौ तौ हि मन्यते | तौ कपोतौ द्विजौ भूत्वा गत्वा गोपायनानभि ||
7.e: Asamati made his domestic priests; for he considered them the best. These two priests having become pigeons and having gone against the

7.s: māyābalācca yogācca subandhumabhipetatuḥ | sa duḥkhādabhighātācca mumoha ca papāta ca ||
7.d: मायाबलाच्च योगाच्च सुबन्धुमभिपेततुः | स दुःखादभिघाताच्च मुमोह च पपात च ||

7.s: tau tato'syāsumālucya rājānamabhijagmatuḥ | tataḥ subandhau patite gatāsau bhrātarastrayaḥ ||
7.d: तौ ततोऽस्यासुमालुच्य राजानमभिजग्मतुः | ततः सुबन्धौ पतिते गतासौ भ्रातरस्त्रयः ||
7.e: When they had plucked out (alucya) his spirit (asu), they went to the king. Then, after Subandhu had fallen lifeless to the ground, the three

7.s: jepuḥ svastyayanaṃ sarvai meti gaupāyanāḥ saha | manaāvartanaṃ tasya sūktaṃ yaditi te'bhyayuḥ ||
7.d: जेपुः स्वस्त्ययनं सर्वै मेति गौपायनाः सह | मनआवर्तनं तस्य सूक्तं यदिति तेऽभ्ययुः ||

7.s: jepuśca bheṣajārthaṃ yaṃ pra tārīti paraṃ tataḥ | sūktasyādyastṛcastatra nirṛterapanodanaḥ ||
7.d: जेपुश्च भेषजार्थं यं प्र तारीति परं ततः | सूक्तस्याद्यस्तृचस्तत्र निरृतेरपनोदनः ||
7.e: And the following (triplet) which, (beginning) 'Let be prolonged' (pra tari: x. 59), they muttered with a view to remedies is the first triplet of the hymn (1-3): it is there meant to drive away (apanodana) Dissolution (nirrti).

7.s: trayaḥ pādā mo ṣviti tu saumyā nairṛta uttamaḥ | ṛk saumyā nairṛtī caiṣā asunīte stutiḥ pare ||
7.d: त्रयः पादा मो ष्विति तु सौम्या नैरृत उत्तमः | ऋक् सौम्या नैरृती चैषा असुनीते स्तुतिः परे ||
7.e: Now the three verses 'Not at all' (mo su: x. 59. 4 abe) are addressed to Soma, the last (4%) to Nirrtia: this whole stanza being addressed to Soma and Nirrti. The following two (stanzas: 5, 6) are (in) praise of Asuniti. x.

7.s: dvṛce tvānumataṃ pādam antyaṃ yāskastu manyate | bhūrdyauḥ somaśca pūṣā ca khaṃ pathyā svastireva ca ||
7.d: द्वृचे त्वानुमतं पादम् अन्त्यं यास्कस्तु मन्यते | भूर्द्यौः सोमश्च पूषा च खं पथ्या स्वस्तिरेव च ||
7.e: Now in (this) couplet Yaska a thinks the last verse (59. 6) is addressed to Anumati.

7.s: subandhoreva śāntyarthaṃ punarna ṛci tu smṛtāḥ | tṛcaḥ śamiti rodasyor aindro'rdharcaḥ samityṛci ||
7.d: सुबन्धोरेव शान्त्यर्थं पुनर्न ऋचि तु स्मृताः | तृचः शमिति रोदस्योर् ऐन्द्रोऽर्धर्चः समित्यृचि ||

7.s: rapaso nāśanārthaṃ vai tuṣṭuvustyatha rodasī | rapa ityabhidhānaṃ tu gaditaṃ pāpakṛchrayoḥ ||
7.d: रपसो नाशनार्थं वै तुष्टुवुस्त्यथ रोदसी | रप इत्यभिधानं तु गदितं पापकृछ्रयोः ||
7.e: Now they praised the Two Worlds for the destruction of infirmity (rapas): 'infirmity' is stated to be a designation of sin or (bodily) trouble.

7.s: ṛgbhireti catasṛbhis tata aikṣvākumastuvan | indra kṣatretyṛcā cāsya stutvāśaṃsiṣurāśiṣaḥ ||
7.d: ऋग्भिरेति चतसृभिस् तत ऐक्ष्वाकुमस्तुवन् | इन्द्र क्षत्रेत्यृचा चास्य स्तुत्वाशंसिषुराशिषः ||
7.e: Then with the four stanzas 'Hither' (a: x. 60. 1-4) they praised the scion of Iksvaku, and after praising him they uttered prayers for him with the stanza O Indra, dominion' (indra ksatra x. 60. 5).

7.s: agastyasyeti mātā ca teṣāṃ tuṣṭāva taṃ nṛpam | stutaḥ sa rājā savrīḻas tasthau gopāyanānabhi ||
7.d: अगस्त्यस्येति माता च तेषां तुष्टाव तं नृपम् | स्तुतः स राजा सव्रीḻअस् तस्थौ गोपायनानभि ||
7.e: And their mother & praised the king with (the stanza) 'Of Agastya' (agastyasya: x. 60.6).

7.s: sūktenāpyastuvannagniṃ dvaipadena yathātriṣu | agnirapyatrabravīdetān aymantaḥ paridhyasuḥ ||
7.d: सूक्तेनाप्यस्तुवन्नग्निं द्वैपदेन यथात्रिषु | अग्निरप्यत्रब्रवीदेतान् अय्मन्तः परिध्यसुः ||
7.e: As among the Atris a they had also praised Agni with a dvipada hymn (dvaipada), Agni, on his part, said to them, 'Here within the sacrificial barrier' (antahparidhi) b is the spirit suktenapya ° bfkn, suktenatha, suktenaisam Am'.

7.s: subandhorasya caikṣvākor mayā gupto hitarthinā | subandhave pradāyāsuṃ jīvetyuktvā ca pāvakaḥ ||
7.d: सुबन्धोरस्य चैक्ष्वाकोर् मया गुप्तो हितर्थिना | सुबन्धवे प्रदायासुं जीवेत्युक्त्वा च पावकः ||

7.s: stuto gaupāyanaiḥ prīto jagāma tridivaṃ prati | ayaṃ māteti hṛṣṭāste subandhorasumāhvayan ||
7.d: स्तुतो गौपायनैः प्रीतो जगाम त्रिदिवं प्रति | अयं मातेति हृष्टास्ते सुबन्धोरसुमाह्वयन् ||

7.s: naṅkuke'ṅgunuṣṭuṣṭam || śarīramabhinirdiśya subandhoḥ patitaṃ bhuvi | sūktaśeṣaṃ jaguścāsya cetaso dhāraṇāya te ||
7.d: नङ्कुकेऽङ्गुनुष्टुष्टम् || शरीरमभिनिर्दिश्य सुबन्धोः पतितं भुवि | सूक्तशेषं जगुश्चास्य चेतसो धारणाय ते ||
7.e: Pointing to the body of Subandhu prostrate on the ground, they sang the remainder of the hymn for the maintenance of his consciousness (cetas). a According to the Sarvanukramani, they summoned back his life with stanzas 7-11: parabhih subandhor jivitam ahvayan.

7.s: labdhāsuṃ cāyamityasyāṃ pṛthak pāṇibhiraspṛśan | ṣaḻidaṃ vaiśvadevāni dvitīye'ṅgirasāṃ stutiḥ ||
7.d: लब्धासुं चायमित्यस्यां पृथक् पाणिभिरस्पृशन् | षḻइदं वैश्वदेवानि द्वितीयेऽङ्गिरसां स्तुतिः ||
7.e: And in the (stanza) 'This' (ayam: x. 60. 12) they individually (prthak) touched him with their hands when he had recovered his spirit. There are six (hymns) addressed to the All-gods (beginning) 'This' (idam: x. 61-66). In the second (62) there is praise of the Angirases.

7.s: janma karma ca sakhyaṃ ca indreṇa saha kīrtayan | stauti pra nūnamityādyāḥ sāvarṇyasya mano stutiḥ ||
7.d: जन्म कर्म च सख्यं च इन्द्रेण सह कीर्तयन् | स्तौति प्र नूनमित्याद्याः सावर्ण्यस्य मनो स्तुतिः ||
7.e: (The seer) praises (them), proclaiming (their) birth, and activity, and friendship with Indra. 'May he now prosper' (pra nunam: x. 62. 8-11) b and the rest are a praise of Manu, son of Savarna (savarnya).

7.s: tasyaiva cāyuṣo'rthāya devānstautyabhyayādṛṣiḥ | sutrāmāṇaṃ mahīmū ṣu dakṣasyetyadite stutiḥ ||
7.d: तस्यैव चायुषोऽर्थाय देवान्स्तौत्यभ्ययादृषिः | सुत्रामाणं महीमू षु दक्षस्येत्यदिते स्तुतिः ||
7.e: And for the sake of long life for him the seer praises the gods (so) he came upon 'Her that well guards' (sutramanam: x. 63. 10) (and) 'Her that is great' (mahim u su)a. 'Of Daksa' (daksasya: x. 64. 5) is (in) praise of Aditi.

7.s: pathyāsvasteḥ svastiriddhi svasti no marutāṃ stutiḥ | mārutīmṛcamanvāhety uktamādhvaryaveṣu hi ||
7.d: पथ्यास्वस्तेः स्वस्तिरिद्धि स्वस्ति नो मरुतां स्तुतिः | मारुतीमृचमन्वाहेत्य् उक्तमाध्वर्यवेषु हि ||
7.e: The goddess of Welfare, indeed' (svastir id dhi: x. 63. 16) is (in praise) of Pathya svasti; 'Welfare to us' (svasti nah: 15) is (in) praise of the Maruts; for it is stated in the texts of the Adhvaryus (with regard to it) 'He repeats the stanza addressed to the

7.s: yā gauriti tathaivāsyāṃ stūyate madhyamā tu vāk | mitrāya maitrāvaruṇī bhujyumaṃhasa āśvinī ||
7.d: या गौरिति तथैवास्यां स्तूयते मध्यमा तु वाक् | मित्राय मैत्रावरुणी भुज्युमंहस आश्विनी ||
7.e: So also in the (stanza) 'The Cow that' (ya gauh: x. 65. 6) the Middle Vac is praised; 'To Mitra' (mitraya: 5) is addressed to Mitra-Varuna; 'Bhujyu from distress' (bhujyum amhasah: 12) is addressed to the Asvins.

7.s: stautyapi ca manuṃ svasti dvṛce vācaṃ ca madhyamām | athemāṃ dve bārhaspatye bhadrā āgneyamāpriyaḥ ||
7.d: स्तौत्यपि च मनुं स्वस्ति द्वृचे वाचं च मध्यमाम् | अथेमां द्वे बार्हस्पत्ये भद्रा आग्नेयमाप्रियः ||
7.e: He also praises Manu and the Middle Vac in the couplet containing svastia (x. 66. 14, 15). Then the two (hymns) 'This' (imam: x. 67, 68) are addressed to Brhaspati; 'The auspicious' (bhadrah: x. 69) is addressed to Agni; (then comes) an Apri hymn (x. 70).

7.s: prathame bārhaspatye tu ardharce brahmaṇaspatiḥ | yajjyotiramṛtaṃ brahma yadyogātsamupāśnute | tajjñānamabhituṣṭāva sūktenātha bṛhaspatiḥ ||
7.d: प्रथमे बार्हस्पत्ये तु अर्धर्चे ब्रह्मणस्पतिः | यज्ज्योतिरमृतं ब्रह्म यद्योगात्समुपाश्नुते | तज्ज्ञानमभितुष्टाव सूक्तेनाथ बृहस्पतिः ||
7.e: That knowledge which is immortal light and by union with which one attains to Brahma, Brhaspati praised next (atha) a with a hymn (71).

7.s: jīvanārthaṃ prayogastu mantrāṇāṃ pratiṣidhyate | vedatattvārthavijñānaṃ prāyeṇātra hi dṛśyate ||
7.d: जीवनार्थं प्रयोगस्तु मन्त्राणां प्रतिषिध्यते | वेदतत्त्वार्थविज्ञानं प्रायेणात्र हि दृश्यते ||
7.e: Now the employment of formulas for the sake of a livelihood is forbidden. There appears here for the most part correct knowledge of the essential meaning of the Veda (as the subject of the hymn).

7.s: ācāryā kecidityāhur atra vāgviduṣāṃ stavaḥ | yathābhirnindyate'trargbhiḥ bhūkte'nyābhiranarthavit ||
7.d: आचार्या केचिदित्याहुर् अत्र वाग्विदुषां स्तवः | यथाभिर्निन्द्यतेऽत्रर्ग्भिः भूक्तेऽन्याभिरनर्थवित् ||
7.e: Some teachers say that there is here praise of those who are wise in speech with some (abhih) stanzas, but with others in this hymn the man who does not know the meaning (of the Veda) is blamed.

7.s: yathaitāmanvavindanta vidvāṃsarṣigatāṃ satīm | yathā ca vyabhajan yajñe tadatroktaṃ tṛtīyayā ||
7.d: यथैतामन्वविन्दन्त विद्वांसर्षिगतां सतीम् | यथा च व्यभजन् यज्ञे तदत्रोक्तं तृतीयया ||
7.e: And how the wise found that (speech) when she was located among the seers, and how they divided her at the sacrifice-all this is here told in the third ( stanza : x. 71. 3).

7.s: praśasyate daśamyā tu vidvānuttamayā tvṛcā | yajñe mahartvijāmāha viniyogaṃ ca karmaṇām ||
7.d: प्रशस्यते दशम्या तु विद्वानुत्तमया त्वृचा | यज्ञे महर्त्विजामाह विनियोगं च कर्मणाम् ||
7.e: But in the tenth the wise man is lauded (x. 71. 10), while in the last stanza he (the seer) states the distribution (viniyoga) of the (four) chief priests and of their rites at the sacrifice.

7.s: pare tu stūyate dakṣo aṣṭau caivāditeḥ sutāḥ | dhātendro varuṇo mitro aṃśaḥ sūryo'ryamā bhagaḥ ||
7.d: परे तु स्तूयते दक्षो अष्टौ चैवादितेः सुताः | धातेन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अंशः सूर्योऽर्यमा भगः ||
7.e: Now in the following (hymn: x. 72 ) Daksa is praised a and also the eight sons of Aditi: Dhatr, Indra, Varuna, Mitra, Amsa, Surya, Aryaman, Bhaga. tu

7.s: aindre janiṣṭhā sūkte dve pra svityatra paraṃ tu yat | tatra prācyaḥ pratīcyaśca sravantyo dakṣiṇāśca yaḥ ||
7.d: ऐन्द्रे जनिष्ठा सूक्ते द्वे प्र स्वित्यत्र परं तु यत् | तत्र प्राच्यः प्रतीच्यश्च स्रवन्त्यो दक्षिणाश्च यः ||
7.e: The two hymns (beginning) Thou hast been born' (janisthah: x. 73, 74) are addressed to Indra; but in (the hymn) which here follows (beginning) Let well proclaim' (pra su: x. 75) the streams (sravantyah) which flow east, and west, and south 116. are praised together according to preeminence (pradhanatah) in seven groups of seven. 'Hither you' (a vah: x. 76) is to the pressing stones; the two 'Of the sprinkling of the cloud' (abhraprusah: x. 77, 78) are traditionally held to be addressed to the Maruts.

7.s: tāḥ sapta saptakairvargaiḥ saṃstūyante pradhānataḥ | grāvṇāmā vo mārute dve abhrapruṣa iti smṛte ||
7.d: ताः सप्त सप्तकैर्वर्गैः संस्तूयन्ते प्रधानतः | ग्राव्णामा वो मारुते द्वे अभ्रप्रुष इति स्मृते ||

7.s: apaśyamiti cāgneye ya imā vaiśvakarmaṇe | mānyave yasta ityete paraṃ yattu mama vrate ||
7.d: अपश्यमिति चाग्नेये य इमा वैश्वकर्मणे | मान्यवे यस्त इत्येते परं यत्तु मम व्रते ||
7.e: The two (beginning) 'I saw' (apasyam: x. 79, 80) are addressed to Agni; the two 'Who these' (ya imaa: x. 81, 82) are addressed to Visvakarman; the two Who to thee' (yas te: 83, 84) are addressed to Manyu. But that which follows, 'In my vow (mama vrate),

7.s: tadāśīrvādabahulaṃ stauti viśvāndivaukasaḥ | parākadāsa āgneyaṃ yadudityaṣṭakaṃ param ||
7.d: तदाशीर्वादबहुलं स्तौति विश्वान्दिवौकसः | पराकदास आग्नेयं यदुदित्यष्टकं परम् ||

7.s: maitrāvaruṇyṛk tatrāsti caturthyendrāgnyupottamā | sāvitrī caiva sūryā ca saiva patnī vivasvataḥ ||
7.d: मैत्रावरुण्यृक् तत्रास्ति चतुर्थ्येन्द्राग्न्युपोत्तमा | सावित्री चैव सूर्या च सैव पत्नी विवस्वतः ||
7.e: The fourth stanza there is addressed to Mitra - Varuna &, while the last but one (x. 85. 7) is addressed to Indra and Agni. Savitri and Suryac are one and the same wife of

7.s: stutā vṛṣākapāyīti uṣā iti ca yocyate | uṣā eṣā tridhātmānaṃ vibhajya praiti gopatim ||
7.d: स्तुता वृषाकपायीति उषा इति च योच्यते | उषा एषा त्रिधात्मानं विभज्य प्रैति गोपतिम् ||

7.s: uṣāḥ purodayād bhūtvā sūryā madhyaṃdine sthite | bhūtvā vṛṣākapāyī ca dinānteṣvavagacchati ||
7.d: उषाः पुरोदयाद् भूत्वा सूर्या मध्यंदिने स्थिते | भूत्वा वृषाकपायी च दिनान्तेष्ववगच्छति ||
7.e: Becoming Usas before sunrise, Surya when midday reigns, and becoming Vrsakapayi at the end of days, she goes down.

7.s: satyasūryartasomānāṃ sauryādyātra hyṛgucyate | parābhistisṛbhistvṛgbhir ucyate soma oṣadhiḥ ||
7.d: सत्यसूर्यर्तसोमानां सौर्याद्यात्र ह्यृगुच्यते | पराभिस्तिसृभिस्त्वृग्भिर् उच्यते सोम ओषधिः ||
7.e: The first stanza here (x. 85. 1) addressed to Surya a is stated to be connected with Satya, Surya, Rta and Soma; but with the following three stanzas (2-4) Soma as a plant is spoken of.

7.s: vispaṣṭamuttarā tvāsām ṛk candramasamarcati | sūryāyai bhāvavṛttaṃ tu raibhītyaṣṭābhirucyate ||
7.d: विस्पष्टमुत्तरा त्वासाम् ऋक् चन्द्रमसमर्चति | सूर्यायै भाववृत्तं तु रैभीत्यष्टाभिरुच्यते ||
7.e: But the stanza which comes next to these (5) clearly adores the moon (candramas), while with the eight (stanzas) 'The singer's' (raibhi x. 85. 6-13) the evolutional section (bhavavrttam) for Suryaa is expressed.

7.s: yadaśvinau dvṛca stauti sūryamevottarārcati | saptadaśī vaiśvadevī sauryācāndramasī parā ||
7.d: यदश्विनौ द्वृच स्तौति सूर्यमेवोत्तरार्चति | सप्तदशी वैश्वदेवी सौर्याचान्द्रमसी परा ||
7.e: The couplet 'When' (yat: x. 85. 14, 15) praises the Asvins; the following (stanza) adores Surya (16); the seventeenth is addressed to the All-gods (17); the following one is addressed to Sun and Moon (18).

7.s: parasyāḥ prathamau pādau sauryau cāndramasau parau | aurṇavābho dvṛce tvasminn aśvinau manyate stutau ||
7.d: परस्याः प्रथमौ पादौ सौर्यौ चान्द्रमसौ परौ | और्णवाभो द्वृचे त्वस्मिन्न् अश्विनौ मन्यते स्तुतौ ||
7.e: Of the following (stanza: x. 85. 19) the first two verses are addressed to the Sun (19%), while the following two (19) are to the Moon. Aurnavabha, however, thinks that in this couplet the Asvins are praised.

7.s: sūryācandramasau tau hi prāṇāpānau ca tau smṛtau | ahorātrau ca tāveva syātāṃ tāveva rodasī ||
7.d: सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ तौ हि प्राणापानौ च तौ स्मृतौ | अहोरात्रौ च तावेव स्यातां तावेव रोदसी ||
7.e: For those two (Asvins) are traditionally held to be Sun and Moon, and Prana (outward breath) and Apana (downward breath); and these two may be Day and Night, (or) these two (may be) the Two Worlds (rodasi).

7.s: aśnuvāte hi tau lokāñ jyotiṣā ca rasena ca | pṛthakpṛthak ca carato dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca ||
7.d: अश्नुवाते हि तौ लोकाञ् ज्योतिषा च रसेन च | पृथक्पृथक् च चरतो दक्षिणेनोत्तरेण च ||
7.e: For these two permeate (asnwvate) the world with light and moisture ; and they fare (caratah), each separately, to the south and the north.

7.s: sūryaḥ sarati bhūteṣu su vīrayati tāni vā | su īryatvāya yātyeṣu sarvakāryāṇi saṃdadhat ||
7.d: सूर्यः सरति भूतेषु सु वीरयति तानि वा | सु ईर्यत्वाय यात्येषु सर्वकार्याणि संदधत् ||
7.e: Surya moves (sarati) among beings, or he instigates (virayati) them well (su) : apportioning (samdadhat) all their functions (karyani) he goes among them in order to instigate (iryatvaya) them well.

7.s: cāru dramati vā cāyaṃś cāyanīyo dramatyuta | cameḥ pūrvaṃ sametāni nirmimīte'tha candramāḥ ||
7.d: चारु द्रमति वा चायंश् चायनीयो द्रमत्युत | चमेः पूर्वं समेतानि निर्मिमीतेऽथ चन्द्रमाः ||
7.e: The Moon (candramah) runs (dramati) beautifully (caru) or observing (cayan), or (uta) runs as one worthy to be observed (cayaniya); (or) the prior (member of the compound comes) from (the verb) cam ; or (atha) he (candra) fashions (nir-ma) the aggregate of beings (sam-etani).

7.s: sukiṃśukamiti tvasyāṃ sūryāmārohatīṃ patim | stauti viśvāvasuṃ caiva dvṛce gandharvamuttare ||
7.d: सुकिंशुकमिति त्वस्यां सूर्यामारोहतीं पतिम् | स्तौति विश्वावसुं चैव द्वृचे गन्धर्वमुत्तरे ||
7.e: Now in the (stanza) 'Bright, with Kimsuka flowers' (sukimsukam: x. 85. 20) (the seer) praises Surya mounting (the car of) her husband, and in the next distich (21, 22) the Gandharva Visvavasu.

7.s: anṛkṣarā ityanayā yātau stautīha daṃpatī | gṛhānprapadyamānāṃ tu parābhiḥ pañcabhirvadhūm ||
7.d: अनृक्षरा इत्यनया यातौ स्तौतीह दंपती | गृहान्प्रपद्यमानां तु पराभिः पञ्चभिर्वधूम् ||
7.e: With the (stanza) Thornless' (anrksarah: x. 85. 23) (the seer) here praises the wedded couple (dampati) who have started (yatau), but with the following five (24-28) the wife as she reaches the house (of her husband).

7.s: vāsasaśca vadhūnāṃ ca varadānaṃ pracakṣate | tat striyā virāgasya vibhave sati vāsasaḥ ||
7.d: वाससश्च वधूनां च वरदानं प्रचक्षते | तत् स्त्रिया विरागस्य विभवे सति वाससः ||
7.e: And (in the next: x. 85. 29) they declare (that) the presentation by the bridegroom (vara-dana) of (newly-married) wives (is expressed). Then (30) the woman's garment, when indifference prevails (vibhave sati)

7.s: anyatra maithunādbhartur haraṇaṃ pratiṣidhyate | ye yakṣmanāśino stauti dvṛce mā paripanthinaḥ ||
7.d: अन्यत्र मैथुनाद्भर्तुर् हरणं प्रतिषिध्यते | ये यक्ष्मनाशिनो स्तौति द्वृचे मा परिपन्थिनः ||
7.e: (that is), except at the time of intercourse, is forbidden to be taken hold of (harana) by the husband. The stanza (The diseases) which' (ye: x. 85. 31) is destructive of consumption (yaksma); in the couplet 'May not' (ma: 32, 33) (the seer) praises the waylayers.

7.s: tṛṣṭametaditi tvāha yādṛgvādhūyamarhati | āśāste caiva vividhaṃ jñātibhyaścānuśāsanam ||
7.d: तृष्टमेतदिति त्वाह यादृग्वाधूयमर्हति | आशास्ते चैव विविधं ज्ञातिभ्यश्चानुशासनम् ||
7.e: But (the stanza) Rough is this' (trstam etat: x. 85. 34) states what sort of man deserves (to receive) the bridal dress. And various directions bare given to her

7.s: baddhā strī bhāvavṛttiśca paravā tvatra kathyate | gṛbhṇāmi ta ṛcā hastaṃ guhṇannatha dhanāśiṣaḥ ||
7.d: बद्धा स्त्री भाववृत्तिश्च परवा त्वत्र कथ्यते | गृभ्णामि त ऋचा हस्तं गुह्णन्नथ धनाशिषः ||

7.s: āśāste parayā tasyāḥ saṃyogārthāstathāśiṣaḥ | parābhirāśīścāśāste pṛthak tābhyāṃ sahaiva ca ||
7.d: आशास्ते परया तस्याः संयोगार्थास्तथाशिषः | पराभिराशीश्चाशास्ते पृथक् ताभ्यां सहैव च ||

7.s: adhoreti tṛce tasyāḥ samiheti dvayordvayoḥ | ā naḥ prajāpater aindrī cāntyā bṛhaspateḥ ||
7.d: अधोरेति तृचे तस्याः समिहेति द्वयोर्द्वयोः | आ नः प्रजापतेर् ऐन्द्री चान्त्या बृहस्पतेः ||

7.s: mantrā vaivāhikā hyete nigadyante nṛṇāmapi | ārtvijā yājamānāśca yathārūpaṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
7.d: मन्त्रा वैवाहिका ह्येते निगद्यन्ते नृणामपि | आर्त्विजा याजमानाश्च यथारूपं विशेषतः ||
7.e: Now these wedding formulas are recited for men also, being connected with the priests (artvijah) a and with the institutor of the rite (yajamanah) according to their respective form (and) their peculiarity (visesa).

7.s: pratyṛcaṃ pratikīrtyante devatāśceha yāsu yāḥ | vadettāṃ devatāṃ tāsu nārāśaṃsīrvadeta vā ||
7.d: प्रत्यृचं प्रतिकीर्त्यन्ते देवताश्चेह यासु याः | वदेत्तां देवतां तासु नाराशंसीर्वदेत वा ||
7.e: And in those stanzas here in which respectively (pratyrcam) deities are proclaimed, one should state the one mentioned (tam) to be the deity or should state that (the stanzas) are addressed to Narasamsa (narasamsi).

7.s: auṣasī sarvathā caitā bhāvavṛtaṃ pracakṣate | sūryayā saha sūkte'smin pādaścaivātra lakṣyate ||
7.d: औषसी सर्वथा चैता भाववृतं प्रचक्षते | सूर्यया सह सूक्तेऽस्मिन् पादश्चैवात्र लक्ष्यते ||
7.e: And they declare that these stanzas addressed to Usas a form as a whole (sarvatha) (hymn) concerned with evolution (bhavavrtta); and in this hymn a verse (pada) is also (thus) characterized with Suryac.

7.s: vi hi vārṣākapaṃ sūktam asau hi kapilo vṛṣā | indraḥ prajāpatiścaiva viśvasmādindra uttaraḥ ||
7.d: वि हि वार्षाकपं सूक्तम् असौ हि कपिलो वृषा | इन्द्रः प्रजापतिश्चैव विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ||
7.e: Away, indeed' (vi hi: x. 86) is a hymn addressed to Vrsakapi; for that brown (kapila) bull (vrsan) is Indra a and Prajapati Indra is superior to all'b.

7.s: rakṣohaṇādi cāgneyaṃ trīn stautyagnīn paraṃ haviḥ | imaṃ ca madhyamaṃ caiva asau vaiśvānaraṃ ca yaḥ ||
7.d: रक्षोहणादि चाग्नेयं त्रीन् स्तौत्यग्नीन् परं हविः | इमं च मध्यमं चैव असौ वैश्वानरं च यः ||
7.e: (The hymn) beginning The demon-slayer' (raksohanam: x. 87) is addressed to Agni. The following one, 'The oblation x. 91 (havih: x. 88), praises the three Agnis, this (terrestrial) one, and the Middle one, and Vaisvanara a who is that (celestial) one. •di

7.s: aindrātpuruṣasaktaṃ ca antyayā pauruṣasya tu | yathainamabhajansādhyā yajñārthaṃ so'rtha ucyate ||
7.d: ऐन्द्रात्पुरुषसक्तं च अन्त्यया पौरुषस्य तु | यथैनमभजन्साध्या यज्ञार्थं सोऽर्थ उच्यते ||
7.e: And after (a hymn: x. 89) addressed to Indra (comes) the Purusa hymn (x. 90). With the last (stanza: 16) of (the hymn) addressed to Purusa the circumstances (artha) are told in which the Sadhyas divided him for the purpose of sacrifice.

7.s: āpāntamanyurityaindryāṃ stutaḥ somo'tra dṛśyate | sālokyātsāhacaryādvā stūyate soma eva vā ||
7.d: आपान्तमन्युरित्यैन्द्र्यां स्तुतः सोमोऽत्र दृश्यते | सालोक्यात्साहचर्याद्वा स्तूयते सोम एव वा ||
7.e: In the stanza addressed to Indra, 'He who gives zeal when imbibed' (apantamanyuh: x. 89. 5), Soma is clearly praised. Soma is praised either because he belongs to the same world or because he is (Indra's) companion.

7.s: nipātabhājaṃ somaṃ ca asyāṃ rathītaro'bravīt | sendreṣu hi nipāto'tra stuto'gniraruṇena sam ||
7.d: निपातभाजं सोमं च अस्यां रथीतरोऽब्रवीत् | सेन्द्रेषु हि निपातोऽत्र स्तुतोऽग्निररुणेन सम् ||
7.e: Rathitara a has said that in this (stanza) Soma is incidental (nipatabhaj); for in (hymns) addressed to Indra there is here (such) incidental mention. In 'Together' (sam: x. 91) Agni is praised by Aruna. II.

7.s: yajñasya yo vaiśvadeve praita ityuttaraṃ tu yat | tatrāvudastu grāvāṇaṃ mūrtimantamivārcati ||
7.d: यज्ञस्य यो वैश्वदेवे प्रैत इत्युत्तरं तु यत् | तत्रावुदस्तु ग्रावाणं मूर्तिमन्तमिवार्चति ||
7.e: 'Of your sacrifice' (yajnasya vah: x. 92) are two addressed to the All-gods (92, 93); but in that which (comes) next, 'Forth these' (praite x.

7.s: pra tadduḥsīma ityṛgbhyāṃ rājñāṃ dānaṃ ca śaṃsati | pururavasi rājarṣāv apsarāstūrvaśo purā | nyavasatsaṃvidaṃ kṛtvā tasmindharmaṃ cacāra ca ||
7.d: प्र तद्दुःसीम इत्यृग्भ्यां राज्ञां दानं च शंसति | पुरुरवसि राजर्षाव् अप्सरास्तूर्वशो पुरा | न्यवसत्संविदं कृत्वा तस्मिन्धर्मं चचार च ||

7.s: tathā tasya ca saṃvāsam asayūn pākaśāsanaḥ | paitāmahaṃ cānurāgam indravaccāpi tasya tu ||
7.d: तथा तस्य च संवासम् असयून् पाकशासनः | पैतामहं चानुरागम् इन्द्रवच्चापि तस्य तु ||
7.e: And the Chastiser of Paka (Indra), being jealous of his cohabitation with her and of Brahma's (paitamaha) and his (Pururavas') passion (for her) as if he (Pururavas) were Indra

7.s: sa tathostu viyogārthaṃ pārśvasthaṃ vajramabravīt | prītiṃ bhinddhi tayorvajra mama cedicchasi priyam ||
7.d: स तथोस्तु वियोगार्थं पार्श्वस्थं वज्रमब्रवीत् | प्रीतिं भिन्द्धि तयोर्वज्र मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम् ||

7.s: tathetyuktvā tayoḥ prīti vajro'bhinatsvamāyayā | tatastayā vihīnastu cacāronmattavannṛpaḥ ||
7.d: तथेत्युक्त्वा तयोः प्रीति वज्रोऽभिनत्स्वमायया | ततस्तया विहीनस्तु चचारोन्मत्तवन्नृपः ||
7.e: 'Very well,' said the bolt, and destroyed their alliance with its craft. Then bereft of her the king wandered about like one distracted.
