7.s: caransarasi so'paśyad abhirūpāmivorvaśīm | sakhībhirabhirūpābhiḥ pañcabhiḥ pārśvato vṛtām ||
7.d: चरन्सरसि सोऽपश्यद् अभिरूपामिवोर्वशीम् | सखीभिरभिरूपाभिः पञ्चभिः पार्श्वतो वृताम् ||
7.e: As he wandered, he saw in a lake the beautiful (abhirupam) & Urvasi, as it seemed (iva), surrounded by five beautiful & maiden friends at her side.

7.s: tāmāha punarehīti duḥkhātsā tyabravīnnṛpam | āprāpyāhaṃ tvayādyeha svarge prāpsyasi māṃ punaḥ ||
7.d: तामाह पुनरेहीति दुःखात्सा त्यब्रवीन्नृपम् | आप्राप्याहं त्वयाद्येह स्वर्गे प्राप्स्यसि मां पुनः ||
7.e: To her he said, 'Come back.' But she sorrowfully (duhkhat) answered the king, 'You cannot now obtain me here; in heaven you will obtain me again.'

7.s: āhvānaṃ prati cākhyānam itaretarayoridam | saṃvādaṃ manyate yāska itihāsaṃ tu śaunakaḥ ||
7.d: आह्वानं प्रति चाख्यानम् इतरेतरयोरिदम् | संवादं मन्यते यास्क इतिहासं तु शौनकः ||
7.e: This reciprocal narrative (akhyana) a in connexion with a summons (ahvana), Yaska considers a dialogue, but Saunaka a story,

7.s: haya iti paramaindraṃ pra te yā oṣadhāstavaḥ | prayoge bhiṣajastvetad yakṣmanāśāya kalpate ||
7.d: हय इति परमैन्द्रं प्र ते या ओषधास्तवः | प्रयोगे भिषजस्त्वेतद् यक्ष्मनाशाय कल्पते ||
7.e: (that is, the hymn beginning) 'Ho' (haye: x. 95). The following one, 'Forth thy' (pra te: x. 96), is addressed to Indra. 'Which' (yah: x. 97) is (in) praise of Plants. B In (its) employment this (hymn) of Bhisaj a is applicable to the cure of consumption (yaksma).

7.s: ārṣṭiṣeṇastu devāpiḥ kauravyaścaiva śaṃtanuḥ | bhrātarau kuruṣu tvetau rājaputrau babhūvatuḥ ||
7.d: आर्ष्टिषेणस्तु देवापिः कौरव्यश्चैव शंतनुः | भ्रातरौ कुरुषु त्वेतौ राजपुत्रौ बभूवतुः ||

7.s: jyeṣṭhastayostu devāpiḥ kanīyāṃścaiva śaṃtanuḥ | tvagdoṣī rājaputrastu ṛṣṭiṣeṇasuto'bhavat ||
7.d: ज्येष्ठस्तयोस्तु देवापिः कनीयांश्चैव शंतनुः | त्वग्दोषी राजपुत्रस्तु ऋष्टिषेणसुतोऽभवत् ||
7.e: Now the elder of these two was Devapi, and the younger Samtanu; but the (former) prince, the son of Rstisena, was afflicted with skin-disease. x.

7.s: rājyena chandayāmāsuḥ prajāḥ svargaṃ gate gurau | sa muhūrttamiva dhyātvā prajāstāḥ pratyabhāṣata ||
7.d: राज्येन छन्दयामासुः प्रजाः स्वर्गं गते गुरौ | स मुहूर्त्तमिव ध्यात्वा प्रजास्ताः प्रत्यभाषत ||
7.e: When his father had gone to heaven his subjects offered him the sovereignty. Reflecting for but a moment, he replied to his

8.s: na rājyamarhāmi nṛpatirvostu śantanuḥ | tathetyuktvābhyasiñcyaṃstāḥ prajā rājyāya śantanuḥ ||
8.d: न राज्यमर्हामि नृपतिर्वोस्तु शन्तनुः | तथेत्युक्त्वाभ्यसिञ्च्यंस्ताः प्रजा राज्याय शन्तनुः ||
8.e: 'I am not worthy of the sovereignty: let Samtanu be ruler.' Assenting to this, his subjects anointed Samtanu king. The second line is

8.s: tatobhiṣeke kauravye vanaṃ devāpirāviśat | na vavarṣātha parjanyo rājye dvādaśa vai samāḥ ||
8.d: ततोभिषेके कौरव्ये वनं देवापिराविशत् | न ववर्षाथ पर्जन्यो राज्ये द्वादश वै समाः ||
8.e: When the scion of Kuru had been anointed, Devapi retired to the forest. Thereupon Parjanya did not rain in (that) realm for twelve years.

8.s: tatobhyagacchaddevāpiṃ prajābhiḥ saha śantanuḥ | prasādayāmāsa cainaṃ tasmindharmavyatikrame ||
8.d: ततोभ्यगच्छद्देवापिं प्रजाभिः सह शन्तनुः | प्रसादयामास चैनं तस्मिन्धर्मव्यतिक्रमे ||
8.e: Samtanu accordingly came with his subjects to Devapi and propitiated him with regard to that dereliction of duty.

8.s: śiśikṣa cainaṃ rājyena prajābhiḥ sahitastadā | tamuvācātha devāpiḥ prahvaṃ tu prāñjalisthitam ||
8.d: शिशिक्ष चैनं राज्येन प्रजाभिः सहितस्तदा | तमुवाचाथ देवापिः प्रह्वं तु प्राञ्जलिस्थितम् ||
8.e: Then, in company with his subjects, he offered him the sovereignty. To him, as he stood humbly with folded hands, Devapi replied: cainam rajyena hm'rp, cainam rajye ca

8.s: na rājyamahamarhāmi tvagdoṣopatendriyaḥ | yājayiṣyāmi te rājan vṛṣṭikāmejyayā svayam ||
8.d: न राज्यमहमर्हामि त्वग्दोषोपतेन्द्रियः | याजयिष्यामि ते राजन् वृष्टिकामेज्यया स्वयम् ||
8.e: 'I am not worthy of the sovereignty, my energy being impaired by skin-disease; I will myself officiate, O king, as your priest in a sacrifice for rain.'

8.s: tatastaṃ tu purodhatta ārtvijyāya sa śantanuḥ | sa cāsya cakre karmāṇi vārṣikāṇi yathāvidhi ||
8.d: ततस्तं तु पुरोधत्त आर्त्विज्याय स शन्तनुः | स चास्य चक्रे कर्माणि वार्षिकाणि यथाविधि ||
8.e: Then Samtanu appointed him to be his chaplain (puro 'dhatta) and to act as priest (artvijyaya). So he (Devapi) duly performed the rites productive of rain. sa

8.s: bṛhaspate pratītyṛgbhir īje caiva bṛhaspatim | dvitīyayāsya sūktasya bodhite jātavedasā ||
8.d: बृहस्पते प्रतीत्यृग्भिर् ईजे चैव बृहस्पतिम् | द्वितीययास्य सूक्तस्य बोधिते जातवेदसा ||
8.e: And he sacrificed to Brhaspati with the stanzas, 'O Brhaspati, to' (brhaspate prati: x. 98. 1-3)a. B When with the second (stanza) of this hymn Jatavedas b had informed him (bodhite), pratityrgbhir bikrn, pratikadbhir P. pratityetad Am'.

8.s: āsye te dyumatīṃ vācaṃ dadhāmi stuhi devatāḥ | tataḥ so'smai dadau prīto vācaṃ devīṃ tathā ca saḥ ||
8.d: आस्ये ते द्युमतीं वाचं दधामि स्तुहि देवताः | ततः सोऽस्मै ददौ प्रीतो वाचं देवीं तथा च सः ||
8.e: 'I will place brilliant speech in your mouth: praise the Gods,' then he (Brhaspati) being pleased bestowed on him (Devapi) divine Speech; and therewith

8.s: ṛgbhiścatasṛbhirdevāñ jagau vṛṣṭyarthameva tu | agniṃ ca sūktaśeṣeṇa kamaindraṃ sūktamuttaram ||
8.d: ऋग्भिश्चतसृभिर्देवाञ् जगौ वृष्ट्यर्थमेव तु | अग्निं च सूक्तशेषेण कमैन्द्रं सूक्तमुत्तरम् ||

8.s: indra dṛhyeti viśveṣām udityṛtvikastutiḥ param | śaktiprakāśanenaiṣāṃ viniyogo'tra kīrtyate ||
8.d: इन्द्र दृह्येति विश्वेषाम् उदित्यृत्विकस्तुतिः परम् | शक्तिप्रकाशनेनैषां विनियोगोऽत्र कीर्त्यते ||
8.e: 'O Indra, stand fast' (indra drhya: x. 100) is to the All- (gods); the following one, 'Awake' (ut: x. 101), is (in) praise of the priests a the application of rites (viniyoga) is here proclaimed by setting forth the powers of these (priests).

8.s: pretītihāsasūktaṃ tu manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ | yāsko draughaṇamaindraṃ vā vaiśvadevaṃ tu śaunakaḥ ||
8.d: प्रेतीतिहाससूक्तं तु मन्यते शाकटायनः | यास्को द्रौघणमैन्द्रं वा वैश्वदेवं तु शौनकः ||
8.e: ' Forth ' (pra : x. 102), Sakatayana a considers a narrative hymn : Yaskab (thinks) that it is addressed to the Mallet (drughana) or to Indra; but Saunaka, that it is addressed to the All-gods.

8.s: ājāvanena bhārmyaśva indrāsomau tu mudgalaḥ | ajayadvṛṣabhaṃ yuktvā aindraṃ ca drughaṇaṃ rathe ||
8.d: आजावनेन भार्म्यश्व इन्द्रासोमौ तु मुद्गलः | अजयद्वृषभं युक्त्वा ऐन्द्रं च द्रुघणं रथे ||
8.e: By this (hymn) Mudgala Bharmyasva in a contest overcame Indra and Soma, having yoked a bull and Mallet belonging to Indra, to his chariot.

8.s: yudhyan saṃkhye jayaṃ prepsure aindro'pratiratho jagau | āśuraindramapvā devo amīṣāmityṛci stutā ||
8.d: युध्यन् संख्ये जयं प्रेप्सुरे ऐन्द्रोऽप्रतिरथो जगौ | आशुरैन्द्रमप्वा देवो अमीषामित्यृचि स्तुता ||
8.e: Apratiratha Aindra desiring victory when fighting in battle sang (the hymn). 'The swift' (asuh: x 103 ) is addressed to Indra : in the stanza ' Of those' (amisam : 12 ) & the goddess Apva is praised.

8.s: caturthī bārhaspatyā syān nākule ca mahāniti | dvrṛcastu mārutaḥ pretety aindrī vā brahma yatparam ||
8.d: चतुर्थी बार्हस्पत्या स्यान् नाकुले च महानिति | द्व्रृचस्तु मारुतः प्रेतेत्य् ऐन्द्री वा ब्रह्म यत्परम् ||
8.e: The fourth ( stanza ) should be (regarded as) addressed to Brhaspati 4, as well as (the stanza ) 'The great one' (mahan) in the hymn of Nakula. x. 103 Now there is a couplet addressed to the Maruts, 'Advance (preta: x. 103. 13), the (first stanza being) optionally addressed to Indra. (The hymn) which follows (begins) 'Brahma'. ab

8.s: tatrāniruktasūktādāv ṛgekā sūryamarcati | gharmaparāścatasrastu savitāramabhīti yā ||
8.d: तत्रानिरुक्तसूक्तादाव् ऋगेका सूर्यमर्चति | घर्मपराश्चतस्रस्तु सवितारमभीति या ||
8.e: In it, at the beginning of the hymn, where no deity is specified (anirukta), one stanza (1) adores the Sun, that which (begins) 'Unto' (abhi: 4), Savitr, while the (first) four are closely connected with the Caldron (gharma-parah).

8.s: sūktaśeṣasya ṣaḻṛcaḥ sūryāyacandramasau saha | tuṣṭāvendramasāvīti aṣṭako'smātpareṇa tu ||
8.d: सूक्तशेषस्य षḻऋचः सूर्यायचन्द्रमसौ सह | तुष्टावेन्द्रमसावीति अष्टकोऽस्मात्परेण तु ||
8.e: The six stanzas of the rest of the hymn (adore) Sun and Moon together. Now with the (hymn) which comes after this (beginning) 'It has been pressed' (asavi: x. 104) Astaka b praised Indra.

8.s: kautsaḥ kadā vaso sūktaṃ durmitro nāma nāmataḥ | sumitraścaiva nāma syād guṇārthamitaratpadam ||
8.d: कौत्सः कदा वसो सूक्तं दुर्मित्रो नाम नामतः | सुमित्रश्चैव नाम स्याद् गुणार्थमितरत्पदम् ||
8.e: The descendant of Kutsa, by name Durmitra, (saw) the hymn When, Glorious One?' (kada vaso: x. 105). Sumitra may also be his name, (while) the other word (Durmitra) would express an attribute (guna).

8.s: bhūtāṃśastu prajākāmaḥ karmāṇi kṛtavānpurā | na hi lebhe prajāḥ kāścit kaśyapo munisattamaḥ ||
8.d: भूतांशस्तु प्रजाकामः कर्माणि कृतवान्पुरा | न हि लेभे प्रजाः काश्चित् कश्यपो मुनिसत्तमः ||
8.e: Now Bhutamsa Kasyapa, being desirous of offspring, in days of old performed rites; for this most excellent of sages had not obtained any children.

8.s: uvāca bhāryā bhūtāṃśaṃ sutānicchasi yāvataḥ | tāvato janayiṣyāmi devatā dvandvaśa stuhi ||
8.d: उवाच भार्या भूतांशं सुतानिच्छसि यावतः | तावतो जनयिष्यामि देवता द्वन्द्वश स्तुहि ||
8.e: His wife said to Bhutamsa: 'I will bear as many sons as you wish (only) praise the gods in pairs.' x.

8.s: tamabhyayustu sarvāṇi dvandvāni stutikāmyayā | tānyavekṣyātha taccakre nāsatyau sūktabhāginau ||
8.d: तमभ्ययुस्तु सर्वाणि द्वन्द्वानि स्तुतिकाम्यया | तान्यवेक्ष्याथ तच्चक्रे नासत्यौ सूक्तभागिनौ ||
8.e: Now all pairs came to him from desire of praise. Observing them he did so (praise them in x. 106): the Asvins own the hymn (suktabhagin).

8.s: tadetadantato bhāvād āśvinaṃ sūktamucyate | na hyasmindevatāliṅgaṃ prāgantyāddṛśyate padāt ||
8.d: तदेतदन्ततो भावाद् आश्विनं सूक्तमुच्यते | न ह्यस्मिन्देवतालिङ्गं प्रागन्त्याद्दृश्यते पदात् ||
8.e: This same hymn (x. 106) is stated to be addressed to the Asvins because of (their) occurrence (bhavat) at the end. For in this hymn the characteristic (name) of the deity does not appear till the last verse (pada).

8.s: sūktena tu pareṇātra svayamāvirabhūditi | ātmānameva tuṣṭāva prājāpatyātha dakṣiṇā ||
8.d: सूक्तेन तु परेणात्र स्वयमाविरभूदिति | आत्मानमेव तुष्टाव प्राजापत्याथ दक्षिणा ||
8.e: Now with the hymn here following, 'There has appeared' (avir abhut x. 107), Daksina Prajapatya praised herself. eva

8.s: dātṝnatra stutāneke dakṣiṇānāṃ vadanti tu | dātṛtvāddakṣiṇānāṃ ca bhojāścatasṛbhi stutāḥ ||
8.d: दातॄनत्र स्तुतानेके दक्षिणानां वदन्ति तु | दातृत्वाद्दक्षिणानां च भोजाश्चतसृभि स्तुताः ||
8.e: Some, however, say that the givers of sacrificial fees are here praised; and that, because they are the givers of sacrificial fees, liberal donors (bhojah) are praised with four (stanzas).

8.s: asurā paṇayo nāma rasāpāranivāsinaḥ | gāste'pajahurindrasya nyagūhaṃśca prayatnataḥ ||
8.d: असुरा पणयो नाम रसापारनिवासिनः | गास्तेऽपजहुरिन्द्रस्य न्यगूहंश्च प्रयत्नतः ||
8.e: There were demons called Panis who dwelt on the farther bank of the Rasa. These carried off the cows of Indra and hid them away carefully.

8.s: bṛhaspatistathāpaśyad dṛṣṭvendrāya śaśaṃsa ca | prāhiṇottatra dūtye'tha saramāṃ pākaśāsanaḥ ||
8.d: बृहस्पतिस्तथापश्यद् दृष्ट्वेन्द्राय शशंस च | प्राहिणोत्तत्र दूत्येऽथ सरमां पाकशासनः ||
8.e: Brhaspati saw ( it was) thus ; and having seen it he reported it to Indra. Then the Chastiser of Paka (Indra) dispatched Sarama a thither on a message.

8.s: kimītyatrāyujābhistāṃ papracchuḥ paṇayo'surāḥ | kutaḥ kasyāsi kalyāṇi kiṃvā kāryamihāsti te ||
8.d: किमीत्यत्रायुजाभिस्तां पप्रच्छुः पणयोऽसुराः | कुतः कस्यासि कल्याणि किंवा कार्यमिहास्ति ते ||
8.e: In the (hymn) 'What? ' (kcim : x. 108) the Pani demons interrogated her with the uneven stanzas, (saying) Whence ( do you come ) ? To whom do you belong, fair one? Or what is your business here

8.s: athābravīttānsaramā dūtyaindrī vicarāmyaham | yuṣmānvrajaṃ cānviṣyantī gāścaivendrasya pṛcchataḥ ||
8.d: अथाब्रवीत्तान्सरमा दूत्यैन्द्री विचराम्यहम् | युष्मान्व्रजं चान्विष्यन्ती गाश्चैवेन्द्रस्य पृच्छतः ||
8.e: Then Sarama addressed them : 'I wander about as the messenger of Indra, seeking you and (your) stall and the kine of Indra who is asking for them.'

8.s: viditatvendrasya dūtīṃ tām asurāḥ pāpacetasaḥ | ūcurmā sarame gāstvam ihāsmākaṃ svasā bhava ||
8.d: विदितत्वेन्द्रस्य दूतीं ताम् असुराः पापचेतसः | ऊचुर्मा सरमे गास्त्वम् इहास्माकं स्वसा भव ||
8.e: On learning that she was the messenger of Indra, the wicked demons said: 'Do not depart, Sarama; be our sister here.

8.s: vibhajāmo gavāṃ bhāgaṃ māhitā ha tataḥ punaḥ | sūktasyāsyāntyayā carcā yugmābhistveva sarvadāḥ ||
8.d: विभजामो गवां भागं माहिता ह ततः पुनः | सूक्तस्यास्यान्त्यया चर्चा युग्माभिस्त्वेव सर्वदाः ||
8.e: Let us divide our share of the cows; be not unfriendly (ahita) henceforth again.' And with the last stanza of this hymn (x. 108. 11), as well as with the even ones throughout,

8.s: sābravīnnāhamicchāmi svasṛtvaṃ vā dhanāni vā | pibeyaṃ tu payastāsāṃ gavāṃ yāstā nigūhatha ||
8.d: साब्रवीन्नाहमिच्छामि स्वसृत्वं वा धनानि वा | पिबेयं तु पयस्तासां गवां यास्ता निगूहथ ||

8.s: asurāstāṃ tathetyuktvā tadājahruḥ payastataḥ | sā svabhāvācca laulyācca pītvā tatpaya āsuram ||
8.d: असुरास्तां तथेत्युक्त्वा तदाजह्रुः पयस्ततः | सा स्वभावाच्च लौल्याच्च पीत्वा तत्पय आसुरम् ||
8.e: The demons saying 'yes' to her, then brought her the milk. She having, from natural taste and greed, drunk the demons' milk

8.s: paraṃ saṃvananaṃ hṛdyaṃ balapuṣṭikaraṃ tataḥ | śatayojanavistārām atarattāṃ rasāṃ punaḥ ||
8.d: परं संवननं हृद्यं बलपुष्टिकरं ततः | शतयोजनविस्ताराम् अतरत्तां रसां पुनः ||

8.s: yasyāḥ pāre pare teṣāṃ puramāsītsudurjayam | papracchendraśca saramāṃ kaccidgā dṛṣṭavatyasi ||
8.d: यस्याः पारे परे तेषां पुरमासीत्सुदुर्जयम् | पप्रच्छेन्द्रश्च सरमां कच्चिद्गा दृष्टवत्यसि ||

8.s: sā neti pratyuvācendraṃ prabhāvādāsurasya tu | tāṃ jaghāna padā kruddhaḥ udgirantī payastataḥ ||
8.d: सा नेति प्रत्युवाचेन्द्रं प्रभावादासुरस्य तु | तां जघान पदा क्रुद्धः उद्गिरन्ती पयस्ततः ||
8.e: But she, under the influence of the demons' (milk), replied 'no' to Indra. He, enraged, struck her with his foot. She then, vomiting the milk,

8.s: jagāma sā bhayodvignā punareva paṇīnprati | padānusāripaddhatyā rathena harivāhanaḥ ||
8.d: जगाम सा भयोद्विग्ना पुनरेव पणीन्प्रति | पदानुसारिपद्धत्या रथेन हरिवाहनः ||

8.s: gatvā jaghāna ca paṇīn gāśca tāḥ punarāharat | te'vadanvaiśvadevaṃ tu brahmajāyā juhūrjagau ||
8.d: गत्वा जघान च पणीन् गाश्च ताः पुनराहरत् | तेऽवदन्वैश्वदेवं तु ब्रह्मजाया जुहूर्जगौ ||

8.s: jāmadagnaṃ samiddho'dya āprīsūktamataḥ param | yugapadvai vrajantaṃ taṃ vairūpā ṛṣayastribhiḥ ||
8.d: जामदग्नं समिद्धोऽद्य आप्रीसूक्तमतः परम् | युगपद्वै व्रजन्तं तं वैरूपा ऋषयस्त्रिभिः ||
8.e: After it follows the Apri hymn of Jamadagni, 'Kindled to-day' (samiddho 'dya: x. 110). The Vairupa seers simultaneously with the three hymns (x. 111-113) 'Ye Wise Ones' (manisinah: x. 111. 1) sang to Indra as he set out against the Panis. The following hymn 'Two caldrons' (gharma: x. 114) is addressed to the All-gods. Some, however, think a that here are praised x. 124 37.

8.s: indraṃ pratijaguḥ sūktaiḥ paṇīnprati manīṣiṇaḥ | vaiśvadevaṃ paraṃ sūktaṃ gharmetyeke'tra tu stutān ||
8.d: इन्द्रं प्रतिजगुः सूक्तैः पणीन्प्रति मनीषिणः | वैश्वदेवं परं सूक्तं घर्मेत्येकेऽत्र तु स्तुतान् ||

8.s: devānindraṃ ca manyante chandāṃsyagniṃ ca madhyamam | āgneyaṃ citra ityetaj jagādarṣirupastutaḥ ||
8.d: देवानिन्द्रं च मन्यन्ते छन्दांस्यग्निं च मध्यमम् | आग्नेयं चित्र इत्येतज् जगादर्षिरुपस्तुतः ||

8.s: pibendraṃ stauti netyannaṃ rākṣoghnāgneyamuttaram | itivai lābamaindraṃ tad āptyāḥ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ nipātitāḥ ||
8.d: पिबेन्द्रं स्तौति नेत्यन्नं राक्षोघ्नाग्नेयमुत्तरम् | इतिवै लाबमैन्द्रं तद् आप्त्याः षष्ठ्यां निपातिताः ||
8.e: 'Drink' (piba: x. 116) praises Indra; 'Not' (na: x. 117), Food. The next (x. 118) is demon-slaying (and) addressed to Agni. So, indeed' (iti vai: x. 119) is addressed to Laba. 'That' (tat: x. 120) is addressed to Indra: the Aptyas are incidentally mentioned in the sixth (stanza).

8.s: prājāpatyamathāgneyaṃ vainyamityanupūrvaśaḥ | varuṇendrāgnisomānām imaṃ na iti saṃstavaḥ ||
8.d: प्राजापत्यमथाग्नेयं वैन्यमित्यनुपूर्वशः | वरुणेन्द्राग्निसोमानाम् इमं न इति संस्तवः ||
8.e: Then (comes a hymn) addressed to Prajapati (x. 121), one to Agni (x. 122), one to Vena (x. 123) in succession. 'To this our' (imam nah: x. 124) is (in) praise of Varuna, Indra, Agni, Soma.

8.s: catasrastvatra sūktādāv āgnirātmastavaṃ jagau | stutaḥ somastu ṣaṣṭhyā ca navamyā ca padaistribhiḥ ||
8.d: चतस्रस्त्वत्र सूक्तादाव् आग्निरात्मस्तवं जगौ | स्तुतः सोमस्तु षष्ठ्या च नवम्या च पदैस्त्रिभिः ||
8.e: Now the four stanzas here at the beginning of the hymn (x. 124. 1-4), Agni sang in praise of himself; but Soma is 304 praised with the sixth (6) and with the ninth in three verses (gabe).

8.s: vāruṇyastvitarāstisra aindramevottamaṃ padam | ahaṃ vāksūktamaryamṇo mitrasya varuṇasya ca ||
8.d: वारुण्यस्त्वितरास्तिस्र ऐन्द्रमेवोत्तमं पदम् | अहं वाक्सूक्तमर्यम्णो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च ||
8.e: But the remaining three (x. 124. 5, 7, 8) are addressed to Varuna, while the last verse (9) is addressed to Indra alone. 'I' (aham: x. 125) is a hymn to Vac. To Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuna

8.s: na taṃ rātryāḥ paraṃ sūktaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ mameti yat | namaste vaidyutaṃ sūktam āśīrvāda paraṃ tu yat ||
8.d: न तं रात्र्याः परं सूक्तं वैश्वदेवं ममेति यत् | नमस्ते वैद्युतं सूक्तम् आशीर्वाद परं तु यत् ||
8.e: 'Not him' (na tam: x. 126). The following hymn is to Ratri (x. 127). That which (begins) To me' (mama: x. 128) is addressed to the All-gods. The hymn addressed to Lightning 'Obeisance to thee' (namas te) b is a benediction. But that which

8.s: yāṃ kalpayanti no'rayaḥ kṛtyānāśanamātmanaḥ | hiraṇyastutirāyuṣyaṃ nāsadyatparameṣṭhinaḥ ||
8.d: यां कल्पयन्ति नोऽरयः कृत्यानाशनमात्मनः | हिरण्यस्तुतिरायुष्यं नासद्यत्परमेष्ठिनः ||
8.e: (The spell) which our foes prepare' (yam kalpayanti no 'rayah), is destructive of sorcery. 'Bestowing length of life' (ayusyam) b is (in) praise of gold for oneself. Neither nonbeing' (nasat x. 129) is to Paramesthin.

8.s: vadanti bhāvavṛttaṃ tad yo yajña iti cottaram | apaindramatra tvāśvinyau caturthī pañcamī smṛte ||
8.d: वदन्ति भाववृत्तं तद् यो यज्ञ इति चोत्तरम् | अपैन्द्रमत्र त्वाश्विन्यौ चतुर्थी पञ्चमी स्मृते ||
8.e: They call this (hymn) evolutional (bhavavrtta); also the nexta, 'The sacrifice which' (yo yajnah: x. 130). 'Away' (apa: x. 131) is addressed to Indra; here, however, the fourth and the fifth (stanzas: 4, 5) are traditionally held to be addressed to the Asvins.

8.s: maitrāvaruṇamījānaṃ prathamāyāmṛci stutāḥ | ardharce dyauśca bhūmiśca aśvinau cottare tataḥ ||
8.d: मैत्रावरुणमीजानं प्रथमायामृचि स्तुताः | अर्धर्चे द्यौश्च भूमिश्च अश्विनौ चोत्तरे ततः ||
8.e: 'The sacrificer' (ijanam: x. 132) is addressed to MitraVaruna; in the first stanza Heaven and Earth are praised in the (first) hemistich (1), and the Asvins in the next (1 cd).

8.s: proṃ ṣvaindre vaiśvadevyṛk tu nakirdevā minīmasi | yasminvṛkṣa iti tvasmin dyusthāna stūyate yamaḥ ||
8.d: प्रों ष्वैन्द्रे वैश्वदेव्यृक् तु नकिर्देवा मिनीमसि | यस्मिन्वृक्ष इति त्वस्मिन् द्युस्थान स्तूयते यमः ||
8.e: 'Forth, well' (pro su: x. 133. 1) are two (hymns) addressed to Indra (133, 134); but the stanza 'Never, O Gods, do we transgress' (nakir deva minimasi: x. 134. 7) is addressed to the All-gods. In the (hymn) Under which tree' (yasmin vrkse: x. 135) the celestial Yama is praised. II.

8.s: keśyagniṃ kaiśinaṃ sūktam uta devāḥ paraṃ tu yat | devānāmatra cādyā syād vātadevastṛcaḥ paraḥ ||
8.d: केश्यग्निं कैशिनं सूक्तम् उत देवाः परं तु यत् | देवानामत्र चाद्या स्याद् वातदेवस्तृचः परः ||
8.e: The hymn 'The Hairy One (bears) Agni' (kesy agnim: x. 136) is addressed to the Hairy Ones; in that which follows, 'And, O Gods' (uta devah: x. 137), the first stanza (1) should be (regarded as) to the Gods; the following triplet (2-4) has Vata as its god. kesyagnim 1, kesyegnim hd, kesamim, kesyanam f.

8.s: trāyatāṃ vaiśvadevyṛk tu śeṣastvabdaivataḥ paraḥ | syādetadviśvabhaiṣajyaṃ rapaso vā vināśanam ||
8.d: त्रायतां वैश्वदेव्यृक् तु शेषस्त्वब्दैवतः परः | स्यादेतद्विश्वभैषज्यं रपसो वा विनाशनम् ||
8.e: The stanza 'May they protect' (trayantam: x. 137. 5) is addressed to the All-gods; but the remainder (of the hymn) that follows (6, 7) has the waters as its divinity. This (hymn) may be considered as containing universal remedies or as destructive of infirmity.

8.s: bhūmirlākṣaṃ paraṃ sūktaṃ tavaindraṃ sūktamuttaram | sūryaraśmiriti tvasmin sāvitraḥ prathamastṛcaḥ ||
8.d: भूमिर्लाक्षं परं सूक्तं तवैन्द्रं सूक्तमुत्तरम् | सूर्यरश्मिरिति त्वस्मिन् सावित्रः प्रथमस्तृचः ||
8.e: The following hymn, 'The Earth' (bhumih), is addressed to Laksa. The next hymn, 'Of thee' (tava: x. 138), is addressed to Indra. In the (hymn) 'Sun-rayed' (suryarasmih: x. 139) the first triplet (1-3) is addressed to Savitr. x.

8.s: ātmā stutaḥ parokṣastu gandharveṇottare tṛce | indro vaiṣa nipātena athavā sūrya ucyate ||
8.d: आत्मा स्तुतः परोक्षस्तु गन्धर्वेणोत्तरे तृचे | इन्द्रो वैष निपातेन अथवा सूर्य उच्यते ||
8.e: Now his own self is indirectly (paroksa) a praised by Gandharva in the next triplet (x. 139. 4-6): he is spoken of incidentally either as Indra or Surya.

8.s: sūkte'smindevatāstisra etā eva prakīrtitāḥ | āgneyaṃ tvagne taveti vāgne accheti yatparam ||
8.d: सूक्तेऽस्मिन्देवतास्तिस्र एता एव प्रकीर्तिताः | आग्नेयं त्वग्ने तवेति वाग्ने अच्छेति यत्परम् ||
8.e: In this hymn (x. 139) these three deities only are celebrated. Now O Agni, thine' (agne tava: x. 140) is addressed to Agni; that which follows, 'O Agni, to (us)' (agne acha: x. 141)

8.s: āgneyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca ayamityatra tu dvṛcāḥ | śārṅgāścatvāra ṛṣayo agnimārcanpṛthakpṛthak ||
8.d: आग्नेयं वैश्वदेवं च अयमित्यत्र तु द्वृचाः | शार्ङ्गाश्चत्वार ऋषयो अग्निमार्चन्पृथक्पृथक् ||

8.s: āśvinaṃ tyaṃ cidityetad ayamaindraṃ tataḥ param | imāṃ khanāmīti sūktam indrāṇī yatsvayaṃ jagau ||
8.d: आश्विनं त्यं चिदित्येतद् अयमैन्द्रं ततः परम् | इमां खनामीति सूक्तम् इन्द्राणी यत्स्वयं जगौ ||
8.e: The (hymn) 'Him indeed' (tyam cit: x. 143) is addressed to the Asvins. 'This' (ayam: x. 144), following after that, is addressed to Indra. 'This (plant) I dig' (imam khanami: x. 145), the hymn which Indrani herself sang, tatah param

8.s: tadaupaniṣadaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ bhāvavṛttaṃ pracakṣate | uttānaparṇāṃ pāṭhāṃ tu stauti sūkte mahauṣadhim ||
8.d: तदौपनिषदं षट्कं भाववृत्तं प्रचक्षते | उत्तानपर्णां पाठां तु स्तौति सूक्ते महौषधिम् ||

8.s: patisaṃvananī tvantyānyāḥ sapatnyapanodikāḥ | araṇyānītyaraṇyānyā stutiraindre śraduttare ||
8.d: पतिसंवननी त्वन्त्यान्याः सपत्न्यपनोदिकाः | अरण्यानीत्यरण्यान्या स्तुतिरैन्द्रे श्रदुत्तरे ||
8.e: Now the last stanza (x. 145. 6) is intended to win the love of a husband, while the rest are meant to repel a rival wife. "O Aranyani' (aranyani: x. 146) is (in) praise of Aranyani. The next two (beginning) 'Faith' (srat: x. 147, 148) are addressed to Indra.

8.s: sāvitraṃ savitā yantraiḥ samiddhaścitsamidhyase | āgneyaṃ śraddhayā śrāddhaṃ medhāsūktamataḥ param ||
8.d: सावित्रं सविता यन्त्रैः समिद्धश्चित्समिध्यसे | आग्नेयं श्रद्धया श्राद्धं मेधासूक्तमतः परम् ||
8.e: 'Savitr with bonds' (savita yantraih: x. 147) is addressed to Savitr. Enkindled even thou art fanned' (samiddhas cit sam idhyase: x. 150) is addressed to Agni. With faith' (sraddhaya: x. 151) is addressed to Sraddha. After that follows the hymn of Wisdom (medha-sukta).

8.s: āgneyamā sūretvetac chāsa aindre tataḥ pare | soma ekebhya ityetad bhāvavṛttaṃ pracakṣate ||
8.d: आग्नेयमा सूरेत्वेतच् छास ऐन्द्रे ततः परे | सोम एकेभ्य इत्येतद् भाववृत्तं प्रचक्षते ||
8.e: The (hymn) May the Father come' (a sur etu) a is addressed to Agni. Then follow two (152, 153) addressed to Indra (beginning) A ruler' (sasah: x. 152. 1). The (hymn) 'Soma for some' (soma ekebhyah: x. 154) they declare to be evolutional.

8.s: yadarāyītyalakṣmīghnaṃ tatra catto iti dvṛce | prādhānyādvā nipātādvā stūyate brahmaṇaspatiḥ ||
8.d: यदरायीत्यलक्ष्मीघ्नं तत्र चत्तो इति द्वृचे | प्राधान्याद्वा निपाताद्वा स्तूयते ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ||
8.e: 'O Arayi' (arayi: x. 155) is destructive of bad luck: in the couplet there 'Driven away' (catto: x. 155. 2, 3) Brahmanaspati is praised either as the chief deity or incidentally;

8.s: indraścaiva yadityasyāṃ viśve devāḥ parītyṛci | āgneyaṃ cāgnimityetad vaiśvadevamimā nu kam ||
8.d: इन्द्रश्चैव यदित्यस्यां विश्वे देवाः परीत्यृचि | आग्नेयं चाग्निमित्येतद् वैश्वदेवमिमा नु कम् ||

8.s: indraḥ prādhānyatastvatra viśvairdevaiḥ saha stutaḥ | ādityaiśca marudbhiśca tathārūpaṃ hi dṛśyate ||
8.d: इन्द्रः प्राधान्यतस्त्वत्र विश्वैर्देवैः सह स्तुतः | आदित्यैश्च मरुद्भिश्च तथारूपं हि दृश्यते ||
8.e: Indra a is, however, here predominantly praised along with the All-gods, and the Adityas and the Maruts. For (the hymn) evidently has this character.

8.s: sūryo na iti sauryaṃ tu yattvetadudasāviti | paulomī svānguṇāṃstatra sapatnīnāṃ ca śaṃsati ||
8.d: सूर्यो न इति सौर्यं तु यत्त्वेतदुदसाविति | पौलोमी स्वान्गुणांस्तत्र सपत्नीनां च शंसति ||
8.e: Now 'May us the Sun' (suryo nah: x. 158) is addressed to Surya; but as to the (hymn) 'Aloft that' (ud asau: x. 159), Paulomi in it lauds her own virtues and (those) of her co-wives.

8.s: aindraṃ tīvrasya muñcāmi bhaiṣajyaṃ yakṣmanāśanam | rājayakṣmahaṇaṃ sūktaṃ prājāpatyaṃ taducyate ||
8.d: ऐन्द्रं तीव्रस्य मुञ्चामि भैषज्यं यक्ष्मनाशनम् | राजयक्ष्महणं सूक्तं प्राजापत्यं तदुच्यते ||
8.e: 'Of the potent' (tivrasya: x. 160) is addressed to Indra. 'I release' (muncami: x. 161) is a remedy destructive of consumption (yaksma). This hymn of Prajapatya's a is spoken of as destroying royal consumption' (raja-yaksma). x.

8.s: aindrāgnaṃ manyate yāska eke liṅgoktadaivatam | rākṣoghnāgneyamityuktaṃ yattvetadbrahmaṇeti tu ||
8.d: ऐन्द्राग्नं मन्यते यास्क एके लिङ्गोक्तदैवतम् | राक्षोघ्नाग्नेयमित्युक्तं यत्त्वेतद्ब्रह्मणेति तु ||
8.e: Yaska considers that the hymn is addressed to Indra-Agni ; some, that it is addressed to the divinities expressed by name. Now as to the (hymn) With the prayer' (brahmana: x. 162), it is said to be demon-slaying and addressed to Agni.

8.s: sravatāmapi garbhāṇāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tadanumantraṇam | vainyaṃ tu venastatpaśyad akṣībhyāṃ yakṣmanāśanam ||
8.d: स्रवतामपि गर्भाणां दृष्टं तदनुमन्त्रणम् | वैन्यं तु वेनस्तत्पश्यद् अक्षीभ्यां यक्ष्मनाशनम् ||
8.e: This is also recognized (drstam) as a consecrating prayer for children issuing from the womb (sravatam). 'Vena saw that' (venas tat pasyat) a is addressed to Vena. 'From the eyes' (aksibhyam: x. 163) is destructive of consumption (yaksma). 66 ab =V. - - 870.

8.s: duḥsvapnaghnamapehīti nipātīndro'gnireva ca | āsīdṛṣirdīrghatapāḥ kapoto nāma nairṛtaḥ ||
8.d: दुःस्वप्नघ्नमपेहीति निपातीन्द्रोऽग्निरेव च | आसीदृषिर्दीर्घतपाः कपोतो नाम नैरृतः ||
8.e: 'Depart' (apehi: x. 164) is destructive of evil dreams: Indra and Agnia are incidental. There was a seer, Kapota Nairrta by name, who practised prolonged austerity.

8.s: akarotkapotastasyāṣṭryām agnidhāne padaṃ kila | sa tamātmahitairvākyaiḥ kapotaṃ stutavānṛṣiḥ ||
8.d: अकरोत्कपोतस्तस्याष्ट्र्याम् अग्निधाने पदं किल | स तमात्महितैर्वाक्यैः कपोतं स्तुतवानृषिः ||

8.s: devā iti tu sūktena prāyaścittārthamucyate | ṛṣabhaṃ mā sapatnaghnaṃ yenedamiti mānasam ||
8.d: देवा इति तु सूक्तेन प्रायश्चित्तार्थमुच्यते | ऋषभं मा सपत्नघ्नं येनेदमिति मानसम् ||

8.s: tubhyetyṛṣī dadṛśatur aindraṃ gāyinabhārgavau | varuṇo vidhātānumatir dhātā somo bṛhaspatiḥ ||
8.d: तुभ्येत्यृषी ददृशतुर् ऐन्द्रं गायिनभार्गवौ | वरुणो विधातानुमतिर् धाता सोमो बृहस्पतिः ||
8.e: The two seers Gathina (Visvamitra) and Bhargava (Jamadagni) a saw (the hymn) addressed to Indra (beginning) To thee' (tubhya x. 167).

8.s: ṣaḻetā devatāstatra tṛtīyāyāmṛci stutāḥ | vātasyeti pareṇāstaud anilaḥ pitaraṃ svakam ||
8.d: षḻएता देवतास्तत्र तृतीयायामृचि स्तुताः | वातस्येति परेणास्तौद् अनिलः पितरं स्वकम् ||

8.s: mayobhūriti yatsūktam apaśyacchabara ṛṣiḥ | nānārūpāḥ payasvinyo gāvastatra tu saṃstutāḥ ||
8.d: मयोभूरिति यत्सूक्तम् अपश्यच्छबर ऋषिः | नानारूपाः पयस्विन्यो गावस्तत्र तु संस्तुताः ||
8.e: The seer Sabara a saw the hymn which (begins) 'Refreshing' (mayobhuh: x. 169). Now various kinds of milch kine are there praised.

8.s: vibhrāṭ sauryaṃ tvaṃ tyamaindram ā yāhītyuṣasa stutiḥ | ā tvā rājñe'bhiṣiktāya dve sūkte cānumantraṇe ||
8.d: विभ्राट् सौर्यं त्वं त्यमैन्द्रम् आ याहीत्युषस स्तुतिः | आ त्वा राज्ञेऽभिषिक्ताय द्वे सूक्ते चानुमन्त्रणे ||
8.e: 'Far-shining' (vibhrat: x. 170) is addressed to Surya; 'Thou this' (tvam tyam: x. 171) is addressed to Indra; 'Come hither' (a yahi: x. 172) is (in) praise of Dawn; and 'Hither thee' (a tva: x. 173. 1) are two hymns (173, 174) for consecrating a king a who has been anointed.

8.s: pra va ityuttaraṃ grāvṇāṃ dadarśa stutimārbudiḥ | yattvataḥ paramāgneyaṃ tatrārbhavyṛk pra sūnavaḥ ||
8.d: प्र व इत्युत्तरं ग्राव्णां ददर्श स्तुतिमार्बुदिः | यत्त्वतः परमाग्नेयं तत्रार्भव्यृक् प्र सूनवः ||
8.e: Arbudi a saw the next (hymn) Forth you' (pra vah: x. 175) as (in) praise of the Pressing Stones. Now that which follows this (x. 176) is addressed to Agni: there the stanza 'Forth the sons' (pra sunavah: x. 176. 1) is addressed to the Rbhus.

8.s: ṛṣirjagau pataṃgastu pataṃgamiti yatparam | tatsauryameke manyante māyābhedaṃ tathāpare ||
8.d: ऋषिर्जगौ पतंगस्तु पतंगमिति यत्परम् | तत्सौर्यमेके मन्यन्ते मायाभेदं तथापरे ||
8.e: Now the seer Patamga sang the hymn which follows, 'The Bird' (patamgam: x. 177); some regard this as addressed to Surya, while others (think that it is) destructive of sorcery (mayabheda).

8.s: māyābhede dvitīyāyāṃ pāk stutetyāha śaunakaḥ | devī bibharti manasā yā vācaṃ viditāṃ satīm ||
8.d: मायाभेदे द्वितीयायां पाक् स्तुतेत्याह शौनकः | देवी बिभर्ति मनसा या वाचं विदितां सतीम् ||
8.e: In (this hymn) destructive of sorcery, in the second (stanza: x. 177. 2) is praised Vac, the goddess who cherishes in her heart a the speech which is well known (viditam).

8.s: tayamū ṣu tārkṣyadaivatyaṃ sūktaṃ svastyayanaṃ viduḥ | udaindre vaiśvadevaṃ tu prathaśceti ca yatparam ||
8.d: तयमू षु तार्क्ष्यदैवत्यं सूक्तं स्वस्त्ययनं विदुः | उदैन्द्रे वैश्वदेवं तु प्रथश्चेति च यत्परम् ||
8.e: The hymn 'Forthwith this' (tyam u su: x. 178), which has Tarksya for its deity, they regard as a charm for good luck (svastyayana). 'Up' (ut: x. 179) are two (hymns) addressed to Indra (179, 180), while that which follows, 'Both extension' (prathas ca x. 181), is addressed to the All-gods.

8.s: ātmaprabhāvamācakhyus tatrādyā ṛṣayastrayaḥ | rathaṃtaraṃ yathā stotraṃ stotraṃ caiva yathā bṛhat ||
8.d: आत्मप्रभावमाचख्युस् तत्राद्या ऋषयस्त्रयः | रथंतरं यथा स्तोत्रं स्तोत्रं चैव यथा बृहत् ||
8.e: In it the first three seers a have declared their own power: how the Rathamtara chant (stotra) and how the Brhat chant,

8.s: yathā ca saṃbhūto dharmaḥ savituścopalakṣyate | bṛhaspatiriti tvasmin stutaḥ sūkte bṛhaspatiḥ ||
8.d: यथा च संभूतो धर्मः सवितुश्चोपलक्ष्यते | बृहस्पतिरिति त्वस्मिन् स्तुतः सूक्ते बृहस्पतिः ||

8.s: āśiṣo yajamānasya kecidetāṃ stutiṃ viduḥ | prājāpatyasya yatsūktam apaśyaṃ tvā prajāvataḥ ||
8.d: आशिषो यजमानस्य केचिदेतां स्तुतिं विदुः | प्राजापत्यस्य यत्सूक्तम् अपश्यं त्वा प्रजावतः ||
8.e: Some consider this praise (of Brhaspati) to be prayers for the institutor of the sacrifice (yajamana). The hymn of Prajavat Prajapatya, which (begins) 'I saw thee' (apasyam tva: x. 183)

8.s: pratyṛcaṃ devatā stauti liṅgairevātra lakṣitāḥ | āśiṣaḥ putrakāmasya prathamā hi vadatyatha ||
8.d: प्रत्यृचं देवता स्तौति लिङ्गैरेवात्र लक्षिताः | आशिषः पुत्रकामस्य प्रथमा हि वदत्यथ ||

8.s: dvitīyā putrakāmāyās tṛtīyātmastavaṃ tvṛṣeḥ | yadviṣṇuriti sūktaṃ tu vaiśvadevaṃ pracakṣate ||
8.d: द्वितीया पुत्रकामायास् तृतीयात्मस्तवं त्वृषेः | यद्विष्णुरिति सूक्तं तु वैश्वदेवं प्रचक्षते ||

8.s: tasminsvadāragarbhārtham ṛṣirāśāsta āśiṣaḥ | paraṃ tu nejameṣeti garbhārthaṃ vā taducyate ||
8.d: तस्मिन्स्वदारगर्भार्थम् ऋषिराशास्त आशिषः | परं तु नेजमेषेति गर्भार्थं वा तदुच्यते ||
8.e: In it the seer utters prayers with a view to his wife's (obtaining) offspring. Now the following (hymn) is 'O Nejamesa' (nejamesa). It is stated to be optionally (applicable: va) c with a view to offspring. r.

8.s: asyai me putrakāmāyai garbhamā dhehi yaḥ pumān | āśiṣo yogametaṃ hi sarvargardhena manyate ||
8.d: अस्यै मे पुत्रकामायै गर्भमा धेहि यः पुमान् | आशिषो योगमेतं हि सर्वर्गर्धेन मन्यते ||
8.e: To this (wife) of mine longing for a son do thou grant offspring which (shall be) male'a with (this) half of the whole (first) stanza heb means this whole combination (yoga) of prayer

8.s: ekāramanukampārthe nāmni smarati māṭharaḥ | ākhyāte bhūtakaraṇaṃ vāṣkalā āvyayoriti ||
8.d: एकारमनुकम्पार्थे नाम्नि स्मरति माठरः | आख्याते भूतकरणं वाष्कला आव्ययोरिति ||

8.s: māhitraṃ yanmahi trīṇām ādityānāṃ stutiṃ viduḥ | varuṇārthamamitrāṇām ādityeṣvitareṣu tu ||
8.d: माहित्रं यन्महि त्रीणाम् आदित्यानां स्तुतिं विदुः | वरुणार्थममित्राणाम् आदित्येष्वितरेषु तु ||
8.e: The Mahitra (hymn) which (begins) The great (aid) of the three' (mahi trinam: x. 185) they regard as praise of the Adityas, Varuna, Aryaman, Mitra. Now in very few b other (hymns) addressed to the

8.s: eta eva trayo devā stutāḥ svalpeṣvato'nyathā | śāntyarthaṃ sūktametaddhi pāvanaṃ caiva vai śrutam | yātāmapi svastyayane dṛṣṭaṃ tadanumantraṇam ||
8.d: एत एव त्रयो देवा स्तुताः स्वल्पेष्वतोऽन्यथा | शान्त्यर्थं सूक्तमेतद्धि पावनं चैव वै श्रुतम् | यातामपि स्वस्त्ययने दृष्टं तदनुमन्त्रणम् ||

8.s: ulo'stautpitaraṃ vātaṃ vāta āgneyamuttaram | vispaṣṭaṃ jātavedasyaṃ preti dāśatayīṣu tu ||
8.d: उलोऽस्तौत्पितरं वातं वात आग्नेयमुत्तरम् | विस्पष्टं जातवेदस्यं प्रेति दाशतयीषु तु ||
8.e: (Then) Ula praised his father Vata (in) 'May Vata' (vatah x. 186). The next (hymn) is addressed to Agni (x. 187). But in the ten books (of the Rg-veda) the (hymn which begins) 'Forth' (pra x. 188) is the one (which is) clearly addressed to Jatavedas.

8.s: yatkiñcidanyatrāgneyaṃ jātavedasyamucyate | āyaṃ gauriti yatsūktaṃ sārparājñā svayaṃ jagau ||
8.d: यत्किञ्चिदन्यत्राग्नेयं जातवेदस्यमुच्यते | आयं गौरिति यत्सूक्तं सार्पराज्ञा स्वयं जगौ ||
8.e: Whatever elsewhere is spoken of as addressed to Jatavedas a is (really) addressed to Agni. As to the hymn 'Hither this bull' (ayam gauh: x. 189), Sarparajni sang of herself (in it).

8.s: tasmātsā devatā tatra saryūmeke pracakṣate | mudgalaḥ śākapūṇiśca ācāryaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ ||
8.d: तस्मात्सा देवता तत्र सर्यूमेके प्रचक्षते | मुद्गलः शाकपूणिश्च आचार्यः शाकटायनः ||
8.e: Therefore she is the deity in it; some declare Surya (to be the deity).

8.s: tristhānādhiṣṭhitāṃ vācaṃ manyante pratyṛcaṃ stutām | bhāvavṛttaṃ paraṃ sūktaṃ dadarśāthāghamarṣaṇaḥ ||
8.d: त्रिस्थानाधिष्ठितां वाचं मन्यन्ते प्रत्यृचं स्तुताम् | भाववृत्तं परं सूक्तं ददर्शाथाघमर्षणः ||

8.s: paraṃ na vidyate yasmāc chāntyai vā pāvanāya vā | yathāśvamedhaḥ ṛturāṭ sarvariprapraṇodanaḥ ||
8.d: परं न विद्यते यस्माच् छान्त्यै वा पावनाय वा | यथाश्वमेधः ऋतुराट् सर्वरिप्रप्रणोदनः ||

8.s: tathāghamarṣaṇaṃ brahma sarvariprapraṇodanam | tadādīnīti yaccātaḥ saṃjñānaṃ jñānasaṃstavaḥ ||
8.d: तथाघमर्षणं ब्रह्म सर्वरिप्रप्रणोदनम् | तदादीनीति यच्चातः संज्ञानं ज्ञानसंस्तवः ||

8.s: caturthaṃ yattu nairhastyaṃ tatsapatnanibarhaṇam | saṃsamitprādhvarāṇāṃ cety āgneyyāveva te smṛte ||
8.d: चतुर्थं यत्तु नैर्हस्त्यं तत्सपत्ननिबर्हणम् | संसमित्प्राध्वराणां चेत्य् आग्नेय्यावेव ते स्मृते ||
8.e: Now as to the fourth (hymn) 'Of the handless fiends (nairhastyam), it is destructive of rivals. Together, together, indeed' (sam-sam it: x. 191. 1) and Forth, of sacrifices (praadhvaranam) b are traditionally held to be two (stanzas) addressed to Agni.

8.s: uśanā varuṇaścendraś cāgniśca savitā stutāḥ | saṃjñāne prathamasyāṃ tu dvitīyasyāmathāśvinau ||
8.d: उशना वरुणश्चेन्द्रश् चाग्निश्च सविता स्तुताः | संज्ञाने प्रथमस्यां तु द्वितीयस्यामथाश्विनौ ||
8.e: Now in the first (stanza) of 'Unanimity,' Usana, Varuna, Indra, Agni, and Savitr are praised, then in the second, the Asvins.

8.s: tṛtīyā cottame ca dve āśiṣo'bhivadanti tāḥ | indraḥ pūṣā sapatnaghne dvitīyasyāmṛci stutau ||
8.d: तृतीया चोत्तमे च द्वे आशिषोऽभिवदन्ति ताः | इन्द्रः पूषा सपत्नघ्ने द्वितीयस्यामृचि स्तुतौ ||
8.e: The third and the last two (3, 4, 5) express prayers. Indra (and) Pusan are praised in the second stanza of (the hymn) destructive of rivals. x.

8.s: devānāmitarāḥ proktā āśīrvādaparāśca yāḥ | saṃsaṃ saṃjñānamityete paraṃ saṃvananaṃ viduḥ ||
8.d: देवानामितराः प्रोक्ता आशीर्वादपराश्च याः | संसं संज्ञानमित्येते परं संवननं विदुः ||
8.e: And the other (stanzas) which are chiefly concerned with benedictions are pronounced to be (addressed) to the Gods. They regard 'Together, together' (sam-sam: x. 191) and 'Unanimity' (samjnanam) to be the best (charm for) conciliation.

8.s: mahānāmnya ṛco guhyās tā endryaścaiva yo vadet | sahasrayugaparyantam aharbrāhmaṃ sa rādhyate ||
8.d: महानाम्न्य ऋचो गुह्यास् ता एन्द्र्यश्चैव यो वदेत् | सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तम् अहर्ब्राह्मं स राध्यते ||
8.e: The Mahanamni stanzas are mystical (guhya) and they are addressed to Indra: whosoever repeats (them) obtains a day of Brahma which lasts for a thousand years.

8.s: tṛcādhamaṃ yājñikāḥ sūktamāhus tasminstutau dṛśyante yāḥ sūktabhājaḥ | pradhānamuktaṃ kila devatā yāḥ sūktabhājaḥ sarvadā śaunakena || aindrīrṛco mahānāmnīstu vidyāt tathā hi iṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇe sūktaśabdaḥ | pradhānamuktaṃ kila devatā yāḥ sūktabhājaḥ sarvadā śaunakena ||
8.d: तृचाधमं याज्ञिकाः सूक्तमाहुस् तस्मिन्स्तुतौ दृश्यन्ते याः सूक्तभाजः | प्रधानमुक्तं किल देवता याः सूक्तभाजः सर्वदा शौनकेन || ऐन्द्रीरृचो महानाम्नीस्तु विद्यात् तथा हि इष्टं ब्राह्मणे सूक्तशब्दः | प्रधानमुक्तं किल देवता याः सूक्तभाजः सर्वदा शौनकेन ||
8.e: The ritualists (yajnika) say that a hymn (sukta) has a minimum of three stanzas. The deities which appear in praise b therein, own the hymn (suktabhaj). It has, as is well known, been stated by Saunaka that the deities which own the hymn are always the chief object (of praise). II.

8.s: aindrīrṛco mahānāmnīstu vidyāt tathā hi iṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇe sūktaśabdaḥ | na dṛśyate sūktavādo nivitsu yathā praiṣeṣvāha sūktābhidhānam ||
8.d: ऐन्द्रीरृचो महानाम्नीस्तु विद्यात् तथा हि इष्टं ब्राह्मणे सूक्तशब्दः | न दृश्यते सूक्तवादो निवित्सु यथा प्रैषेष्वाह सूक्ताभिधानम् ||
8.e: Now one should know that the Mahanamnis a are stanzas addressed to Indra, for such is the statement that appears (drstam) in Brahmana. The term hymn does not appear (applied to them); the expression (vada) hymn (sukta) is (used) in connexion with the Nivids, as one applies (aha) the designation of hymn to the Praisas.

8.s: sūktaikadeśā iti tānpratīyād anyāśca kuntyāḥ padaśo viśāstā | yathaitaśo devanīthādisaṃjñā kuntāpe tatsarvamekaṃ hi sūktam ||
8.d: सूक्तैकदेशा इति तान्प्रतीयाद् अन्याश्च कुन्त्याः पदशो विशास्ता | यथैतशो देवनीथादिसंज्ञा कुन्तापे तत्सर्वमेकं हि सूक्तम् ||
8.e: One should understand that these a constitute (in reality only) single parts of (what is technically called) a hymn, as well as other stanzas which belong to the Kuntapa (kuntya) b and are separated by padas, as the Aitasa (pralapa) d and the verses technically called Devanitha, &c.; for in the Kuntapa (section) all that constitutes one hymne.

8.s: purīṣapadamāsāṃ tu prathamaṃ syātprajāpateḥ | āgneyamaindraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ pauṣṇaṃ caiva tu pañcamam ||
8.d: पुरीषपदमासां तु प्रथमं स्यात्प्रजापतेः | आग्नेयमैन्द्रं वैष्णवं पौष्णं चैव तु पञ्चमम् ||
8.e: Now the first supplementary passage (purisa-pada) a of these (Mahanamni stanzas) should be (regarded as belonging) to Prajapati, (then) one is addressed to Agni, one to Indra, one to Visnu, and the fifth to Pusan.

8.s: agneḥ prayājānuyājāḥ praiṣā ye ca havīṃṣi ca | yaddaivataṃ havistu syāt praiṣāstaddaivatāśca te ||
8.d: अग्नेः प्रयाजानुयाजाः प्रैषा ये च हवींषि च | यद्दैवतं हविस्तु स्यात् प्रैषास्तद्दैवताश्च ते ||
8.e: To Agni belong the Prayajas and the Anuyajas, the Praisas and the oblations. Now whatever may be the divinity of the oblations, must also be the divinity of the Praisas. praisa ye ca

8.s: nividāṃ nigadānāṃ ca svaiḥ svarliṅgaiśca devatāḥ | nigadena nigadyante yāśca kalpānugā ṛcaḥ ||
8.d: निविदां निगदानां च स्वैः स्वर्लिङ्गैश्च देवताः | निगदेन निगद्यन्ते याश्च कल्पानुगा ऋचः ||
8.e: The deities of the Nivids and of the Nigadas (can be ascertained) by their respective characteristic names; and those stanzas are recited with Nigada which are (thus employed) in conformity with the ceremonial.

8.s: agnereva tu gāyatrya uṣṇihaḥ savituḥ smṛtāḥ | anuṣṭubhastu somasya bṛhatyastu bṛhaspateḥ ||
8.d: अग्नेरेव तु गायत्र्य उष्णिहः सवितुः स्मृताः | अनुष्टुभस्तु सोमस्य बृहत्यस्तु बृहस्पतेः ||
8.e: Now to Agni are traditionally held to belong the Gayatris, to Savitr the Usnihs, to Soma the Anustubhs, to Brhaspati the Brhatis.

8.s: paṃktyastriṣṭubhaścaiva vidyādaindryaśca sarvaśaḥ | viśveṣāṃ caiva devānāṃ jagatyo yāstu kāścana ||
8.d: पंक्त्यस्त्रिष्टुभश्चैव विद्यादैन्द्र्यश्च सर्वशः | विश्वेषां चैव देवानां जगत्यो यास्तु काश्चन ||
8.e: The Panktis and the Tristubhs, one should know, belong entirely to Indra; and all Jagatis b whatsoever belong to the All-gods.

8.s: virājaścaiva mitrasya svarājo varuṇasya ca | indrasya nicṛtaḥ proktā vāyośca bhurijaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
8.d: विराजश्चैव मित्रस्य स्वराजो वरुणस्य च | इन्द्रस्य निचृतः प्रोक्ता वायोश्च भुरिजः स्मृतः ||
8.e: The Virajes belong to Mitra, the Svarajes to Varuna. The Nicrts are declared to be Indra's, and the Bhurijes are traditionally held to be

8.s: viṣaye yasya vā syātāṃ syātāṃ vā vāyudevate | yāstvatichandasaḥ kāścittāḥ prajāpatidevatāḥ ||
8.d: विषये यस्य वा स्यातां स्यातां वा वायुदेवते | यास्त्वतिछन्दसः काश्चित्ताः प्रजापतिदेवताः ||

8.s: vicchandasastu vāyavyā mantrāḥ pādaiśca ye mitāḥ | pauruṣyo dvipadāḥ sarvā brāhmya ekapadāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
8.d: विच्छन्दसस्तु वायव्या मन्त्राः पादैश्च ये मिताः | पौरुष्यो द्विपदाः सर्वा ब्राह्म्य एकपदाः स्मृताः ||
8.e: But formulas consisting of various metres (vichandas) belong to Vayu. As for those which are measured by padas, all Dvipadas are sacred to Purusa, Ekapadas are traditionally held to be sacred to Brahma.

8.s: samastā ṛca āgneyyo vāyavyāni yajūṃṣi ca | sauryāṇi caiva sāmāni sarvāṇi brāhmaṇāni ca ||
8.d: समस्ता ऋच आग्नेय्यो वायव्यानि यजूंषि च | सौर्याणि चैव सामानि सर्वाणि ब्राह्मणानि च ||
8.e: All stanzas of the Rg-veda (rc) are sacred to Agni, sacrificial formulas (yajus) are sacred to Vayu, all chants (saman) and Brahmanas are sacred to Surya.

8.s: vaiśvadevo vaṣaṭkāro hiṃkāro ye yajāmahe | rūpaṃ vajrasya vākpūrvaṃ svāhākāro'gnidevatā ||
8.d: वैश्वदेवो वषट्कारो हिंकारो ये यजामहे | रूपं वज्रस्य वाक्पूर्वं स्वाहाकारोऽग्निदेवता ||
8.e: The call 'Vasat' is sacred to the All-gods, (and) the sound 'him' (himkara). (The Agur formula) 'We who sacrifice' (ye yajamahe) b is a form of the thunderbolt which is preceded by speech. The call 'Svaha' has Agni as its deity.

8.s: devānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ca namaskāraḥ svadhaiva ca | kruṣṭo mūrdhāni vijñeyas tālavyaḥ prathamaḥ svaraḥ ||
8.d: देवानां च पितॄणां च नमस्कारः स्वधैव च | क्रुष्टो मूर्धानि विज्ञेयस् तालव्यः प्रथमः स्वरः ||
8.e: To the Gods and the Fathers belong obeisance and oblation (svadha). The shrill (krusta) tone (svara) is to be recognized as in the head; the first tone belongs to the palate.

8.s: dvitīyastu bhruvormadhye tṛtīyaḥ karṇasaṃśritaḥ | caturtho nāsikāgre syād auraso mandra ucyate | mandrakarṣaṇasaṃyuktam atisvāraṃ praśaṃsati ||
8.d: द्वितीयस्तु भ्रुवोर्मध्ये तृतीयः कर्णसंश्रितः | चतुर्थो नासिकाग्रे स्याद् औरसो मन्द्र उच्यते | मन्द्रकर्षणसंयुक्तम् अतिस्वारं प्रशंसति ||
8.e: But the second belongs to the centre of the brows, the third has its place (samsrita) in the ear, the fourth should (be (regarded as) in the tip of the nose, the low (tone) is stated to belong to the chest; one pronounces the Atisvara. as formed by a protraction (karsana) of the low (tone).

8.s: vadanti devatāḥ kruṣṭaṃ manuṣyāḥ prathamaṃ svaram | dvitīyaṃ paśavaḥ sarve gandharvāpsarasaḥ svaram ||
8.d: वदन्ति देवताः क्रुष्टं मनुष्याः प्रथमं स्वरम् | द्वितीयं पशवः सर्वे गन्धर्वाप्सरसः स्वरम् ||
8.e: The Gods speak in (vadanti) the shrill (krusta) tone, men in the first, all beasts in the second, Gandharvas and Apsarases in the (next) tone.

8.s: aṇḍajāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarpāś caturthamupabhuñjate | mandraṃ piśācā rakṣāṃsi asurāścopabhuñjate ||
8.d: अण्डजाः पक्षिणः सर्पाश् चतुर्थमुपभुञ्जते | मन्द्रं पिशाचा रक्षांसि असुराश्चोपभुञ्जते ||
8.e: Egg-born creatures, birds, serpents, employ the fourth; Pisacas, Raksases, and Asuras employ the low tone (mandra).

8.s: atisvārastu sarvasya jaṅgamasthāvarasya ca | vaiśvadevaḥ svaraḥ kruṣṭo nityaṃ yo mūrdhni tiṣṭhati ||
8.d: अतिस्वारस्तु सर्वस्य जङ्गमस्थावरस्य च | वैश्वदेवः स्वरः क्रुष्टो नित्यं यो मूर्ध्नि तिष्ठति ||
8.e: But the Atisvara is peculiar to everything that moves or is stationary. The shrill (krusta) tone, which permanently resides in the head, is sacred to the All-gods.

8.s: tālavyaḥ prathamaḥ sāmnāṃ svara ādityadaivataḥ | svaro dvitīyaḥ sādhyānāṃ bhruvordeśaṃ samāśritaḥ ||
8.d: तालव्यः प्रथमः साम्नां स्वर आदित्यदैवतः | स्वरो द्वितीयः साध्यानां भ्रुवोर्देशं समाश्रितः ||
8.e: The first tone, belonging to the palate (and) peculiar to the Samans, has the Adityas for its divinities. The second tone, which has its location in the region of the brows, is connected with the Sadhyas.

8.s: āśvinastu tṛtīyo'tra svaraḥ karṇau samāśritaḥ | caturthastvatra vāyavyo nāsikyaḥ svara ucyate ||
8.d: आश्विनस्तु तृतीयोऽत्र स्वरः कर्णौ समाश्रितः | चतुर्थस्त्वत्र वायव्यो नासिक्यः स्वर उच्यते ||
8.e: But the third tone here, which has its location in the ears, is sacred to the Asvins; but the fourth tone here, which is nasal, is stated to be sacred to Vayu.

8.s: pañcamastu svaraḥ proktaś cākṣuṣaḥ sūryadaivataḥ | yastu sāmasvaraḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ sa saumyo mandra ucyate ||
8.d: पञ्चमस्तु स्वरः प्रोक्तश् चाक्षुषः सूर्यदैवतः | यस्तु सामस्वरः षष्ठः स सौम्यो मन्द्र उच्यते ||
8.e: But the fifth tone, which is related to the eyes, is declared to have Surya as its divinity. But the sixth Saman tone the low (mandra) is stated to be sacred to Soma.

8.s: vikarṣeṇa tu mandrasya yukto'tisvārya ucyate | sa maitrāvaruṇā jñeyo mandrasthānasamāhitaḥ ||
8.d: विकर्षेण तु मन्द्रस्य युक्तोऽतिस्वार्य उच्यते | स मैत्रावरुणा ज्ञेयो मन्द्रस्थानसमाहितः ||
8.e: But that which is formed with the protraction of the low (tone) is called Atisvarya: it is to be known as sacred to Mitra-Varuna. It is located a in the position of the low (tone).

8.s: sāmasvarāṇāṃ saptānām eto devā ihoditāḥ | trayāṇāmitareṣāṃ tu lokādhipatayastrayaḥ ||
8.d: सामस्वराणां सप्तानाम् एतो देवा इहोदिताः | त्रयाणामितरेषां तु लोकाधिपतयस्त्रयः ||
8.e: These have here been stated to be the gods of the seven Saman tones. But (the gods) of the other three a are the three Lords of the World.

8.s: vāgdevatyo'thavāgneyaḥ thastāvaścaiva sāmasu | udgīthopadravāvaindrau syātāṃ vā vāyudevatau ||
8.d: वाग्देवत्योऽथवाग्नेयः थस्तावश्चैव सामसु | उद्गीथोपद्रवावैन्द्रौ स्यातां वा वायुदेवतौ ||
8.e: The Prastava in the Samans has Vac as its deity, or is sacred to Agni; the Udgitha and the Upadrava are sacred to Indra, or they may have Vayu for their deity.

8.s: sauryaḥ syātpratihāro'tra nidhanaṃ vaiśvadevatam | hiṅkārapraṇavābhyāṃ tu purastādeva kīrtanāt ||
8.d: सौर्यः स्यात्प्रतिहारोऽत्र निधनं वैश्वदेवतम् | हिङ्कारप्रणवाभ्यां तु पुरस्तादेव कीर्तनात् ||
8.e: Now the Response (pratihara) should be (regarded as ) sacred to Surya, the Finale (nidhana) to the All-gods, by pronouncing them with the sound him' and with the sacred syllable Om (pranava) at the beginning.

8.s: iti vyastasamastānāṃ mantrāṇāmiha daivatam | devatāvidavekṣeta prayoge sarvakarmaṇām ||
8.d: इति व्यस्तसमस्तानां मन्त्राणामिह दैवतम् | देवताविदवेक्षेत प्रयोगे सर्वकर्मणाम् ||
8.e: Thus he who knows the deities (of the Rg-veda) should here consider the divinity of the individual and the collective formulas in (their) application to all rites. ab

8.s: saptarṣayo vasavaścāpi devā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somasūryāḥ | pathyā svastī rodasī coktamantre kūhūrguṅgūraditirdhenudaghnyā ||
8.d: सप्तर्षयो वसवश्चापि देवा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोमसूर्याः | पथ्या स्वस्ती रोदसी चोक्तमन्त्रे कूहूर्गुङ्गूरदितिर्धेनुदघ्न्या ||
8.e: The Seven Seers, the Vasus, the Gods, the Atharvans, the Bhrgus, Soma, Surya, and Surya, Pathya svasti, the Two Worlds for whom formulas are stated, Kuhu, Gungu, Aditi, Dhenu, Aghnya; saptarsayo vasavascapi deva mr, saptarsayo rsayascapi devah hd, saptarsayo devascapi deva

8.s: asunītiriḻā cāptyā vidhātānumatirha yā | āṅgirobhiḥ sahaitāḥ syur uktamantrāśca devatāḥ ||
8.d: असुनीतिरिḻआ चाप्त्या विधातानुमतिर्ह या | आङ्गिरोभिः सहैताः स्युर् उक्तमन्त्राश्च देवताः ||
8.e: Asuniti and Ilaa, the Aptyas, Vidhatr, Anumatic, together with the Angirases, these should be (regarded as) deities for whom formulas are stated.

8.s: vaiśvānaro hi suparṇo vivasvān prajāpatirdyauḥ sudhanvā nagohyaḥ | apāṃnapādaryamā vātajūtir iḻaspatiścāpi rathaspatiśca ||
8.d: वैश्वानरो हि सुपर्णो विवस्वान् प्रजापतिर्द्यौः सुधन्वा नगोह्यः | अपांनपादर्यमा वातजूतिर् इḻअस्पतिश्चापि रथस्पतिश्च ||
8.e: Vaisvanara, Suparna, Vivasvat, Prajapati, Dyaus, Sudhanvan, Nagohyaa, Apam napat, Aryaman, Vatajuti, Ilaspati, and

8.s: ṛbhavaḥ parjanyaḥ parvatā gnāśca dakṣo bhago devapatnīrdiśaśca | ādityā rudrāḥ pitaro'tha sādhyā nipātino vaiśvadeveṣu sarve ||
8.d: ऋभवः पर्जन्यः पर्वता ग्नाश्च दक्षो भगो देवपत्नीर्दिशश्च | आदित्या रुद्राः पितरोऽथ साध्या निपातिनो वैश्वदेवेषु सर्वे ||

8.s: anukrāntā devatāḥ sūktabhājo havirbhājaścobhayathā nipātaiḥ | apyevaṃ syādubhayathānyathā vā na pratyakṣamanṛṣerasti mantram ||
8.d: अनुक्रान्ता देवताः सूक्तभाजो हविर्भाजश्चोभयथा निपातैः | अप्येवं स्यादुभयथान्यथा वा न प्रत्यक्षमनृषेरस्ति मन्त्रम् ||
8.e: The deities which own hymns and own oblations have (thus) been stated in succession, in both cases together with (those which occur in) incidental mention. Whether (this) be so in both ways a or in the other way, no formula is directly known (pratyaksa) to any one who is not a seer.

8.s: yogena dākṣyeṇa damena buddhyā bāhuśrutyena tapasā niyogaiḥ | upāsyāstāḥ kṛtsnaśo devatā yā ṛco ha yo veda sa veda devān | yajūṃṣi yo veda sa veda yajñān sāmāni yo veda sa veda tattvam ||
8.d: योगेन दाक्ष्येण दमेन बुद्ध्या बाहुश्रुत्येन तपसा नियोगैः | उपास्यास्ताः कृत्स्नशो देवता या ऋचो ह यो वेद स वेद देवान् | यजूंषि यो वेद स वेद यज्ञान् सामानि यो वेद स वेद तत्त्वम् ||
8.e: These deities are altogether to be adored with concentration, assiduity, self-control, intelligence, deep learning, austerity, and by injunctions (to others). He who knows the stanzas (of the Rg-veda) knows the gods. A He who knows the sacrificial formulas (yajus) knows the sacrifices. He who knows the chants (saman) knows the truth (tattva).

8.s: mantrāṇāṃ devatāvidyaḥ prayuṅkte karma karhicit | juṣante devatāstasya havirnādevatāvidaḥ ||
8.d: मन्त्राणां देवताविद्यः प्रयुङ्क्ते कर्म कर्हिचित् | जुषन्ते देवतास्तस्य हविर्नादेवताविदः ||
8.e: Of him who knowing the deities of the formulas, at any time employs a rite, the deities taste the oblation, but not that of him who is ignorant of (those) deities.

8.s: avijñānapradiṣṭaṃ hi havirneheta daivatam | tasmānmanasi saṃnyasya devatāṃ juhuyāddhaviḥ ||
8.d: अविज्ञानप्रदिष्टं हि हविर्नेहेत दैवतम् | तस्मान्मनसि संन्यस्य देवतां जुहुयाद्धविः ||
8.e: For an oblation assigned (pradista) without correct knowledge a divinity would not desire (iheta). Therefore one should offer an oblation (only) after carefully committing (samnyasya) the deity to mind.

8.s: svādhyāyamapi yo'dhīte mantradaivatavicchuciḥ | sa sattrasadiva svarge sattraśadbhirapīḍyate ||
8.d: स्वाध्यायमपि योऽधीते मन्त्रदैवतविच्छुचिः | स सत्त्रसदिव स्वर्गे सत्त्रशद्भिरपीड्यते ||

8.s: niyamo'yaṃ jape home ṛṣiśchando'tha daivatam | anyathā cetprayuñjānas tatphalāccātra hīyate ||
8.d: नियमोऽयं जपे होमे ऋषिश्छन्दोऽथ दैवतम् | अन्यथा चेत्प्रयुञ्जानस् तत्फलाच्चात्र हीयते ||
8.e: In muttered prayer and in offering an oblation this is a necessity-the seer, the metre, and the divinity & ; and applying them wrongly one is here deprived of their fruit. rsischando hd, rsichando mr.

8.s: ṛṣichandodaivatādi jñānaṃ yajñādiṣu śrutam | tadāśritya prāṇadṛṣṭir viṣitātreti gamyatām ||
8.d: ऋषिछन्दोदैवतादि ज्ञानं यज्ञादिषु श्रुतम् | तदाश्रित्य प्राणदृष्टिर् विषितात्रेति गम्यताम् ||
8.e: As to the knowledge of the seer, the metre, the divinity, and the rest, acquired (srutam) at sacrifices and the like, it should be understood that by resorting to it, the faculty of seeing the Spirit (prana) is here established (vihita).

8.s: aviditvā ṛṣiṃ chando daivataṃ yogameva ca | yo'dhyāpayejjapedvāpi pāpīyāñjāyate tu saḥ ||
8.d: अविदित्वा ऋषिं छन्दो दैवतं योगमेव च | योऽध्यापयेज्जपेद्वापि पापीयाञ्जायते तु सः ||
8.e: He who without knowing the seer, the metre, the divinity, and the application (yoga), should teach or even mutter (a formula), will fare the worse (papiuanjayate).

8.s: arthepsavaḥ khalvṛṣayaś chandobhirdevatāḥ purā | abhyadhāvanniti chando madhye tvāhurmaharṣayaḥ ||
8.d: अर्थेप्सवः खल्वृषयश् छन्दोभिर्देवताः पुरा | अभ्यधावन्निति छन्दो मध्ये त्वाहुर्महर्षयः ||
8.e: In olden times the seers, desirous of wealth, resorted with metres to the deities: it is for this reason (iti) that the great seers mention metre in the middle. * This sloka was known to the author of the Sarvanukramani as most of it has been incorporated in the introduction, §ii. 7: arthepsava rsayo devatas chandobhir abhyadhavan; cp. Sadgurusisya, p. 60. A

8.s: ṛṣiṃ tu prathamaṃ brūyād chandastu tadanantaram | devatāmatha mantrāṇāṃ karmasvevamiti śrutiḥ ||
8.d: ऋषिं तु प्रथमं ब्रूयाद् छन्दस्तु तदनन्तरम् | देवतामथ मन्त्राणां कर्मस्वेवमिति श्रुतिः ||
8.e: Now one should first state the seer, next the metre, and then the deity of the formulas in regard to the rites in this order (evam), so says a sacred text.

8.s: ādhāraṃ vyāpyanādhāraṃ vivicyātmānamātmani | īkṣamāṇo śubhau saṃdhim ṛcodaivatavitpaṭhet ||
8.d: आधारं व्याप्यनाधारं विविच्यात्मानमात्मनि | ईक्षमाणो शुभौ संधिम् ऋचोदैवतवित्पठेत् ||
8.e: Distinguishing the Self in his self as the receptacle (adhara) and at the same time not the receptacle (of all things), one who knows the divinities should recite (the formulas) having an eye to both-the euphonic combination (samdhi) (and) the stanzas (themselves).

8.s: sa brahyāmṛtamatyantaṃ yoniṃ sadsatodhruvam | mahaccāṇu ca viśveśaṃ viśati jyotiruttamam ||
8.d: स ब्रह्यामृतमत्यन्तं योनिं सद्सतोध्रुवम् | महच्चाणु च विश्वेशं विशति ज्योतिरुत्तमम् ||
8.e: Such an one enters into the Brahma, the immortal, the 334 infinite, the permanent source of that which is and is not, both vast and minute, the lord of all, the light supreme.
